+# v5 AGENTIC GRPO: multi-turn rollout with TOOL CALLING, LoRA, on 2 GPUs through Ray + vLLM.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type grpo` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.grpo.run_grpo. This builds on ../grpo/grpo.sh (read it first for the GRPO objective); what
+# makes it AGENTIC is `--max_turns` (a multi-turn rollout) + `--tools` (the model can call tools mid-episode).
+#
+# What an agentic rollout does: instead of one shot generation, each episode runs turn by turn up to
+# --max_turns. The policy generates; if it emits a tool call, the tool runs inside a sandbox env and its
+# observation is fed back as a `tool` message; the policy then continues from there. The WHOLE multi-turn
+# trajectory's response tokens are trained, and GRPO scores the final trajectory with --orm (group-relative
+# advantage over --num_generations sibling episodes of the same prompt, exactly as in grpo.sh). This is how a
+# policy learns to INTERLEAVE reasoning with tool use (run code, read/write files) rather than answer blindly.
+#
+# Tools (`--tools`): names registered 'tool' plugins, resolved through the PluginRegistry.
+#   - `sandbox` (built-in, used below) exposes the sandbox env's OWN default tools -- run_command / write_file
+#     / read_file -- bound to the exact workspace this episode leased. No plugin code to write.
+#   - custom tools: write a ToolPlugin subclass in a .py, register it with @PluginRegistry.register('tool',
+#     'myname'), load it with `--external_plugins mytools.py`, then select it with `--tools myname`. Each tool
+#     implements __call__(name, arguments)->str (the observation fed back) and tool_info()->the OpenAI-shaped
+#     schema. AVOID eval/exec in a custom tool -- the sandbox already caps memory/time; keep tools narrow.
+#   - `--tools` REQUIRES `--max_turns`: tools are injected per turn, so a single-turn rollout has no turn to
+#     call them in and validate refuses the combination.
+#
+# Sandbox env: with no `--sandbox_template` the pool is local `LocalEnv` slots (light, in-process, a fresh
+# workspace per slot) -- what runs below. Naming `--sandbox_template <id>` switches to an `AgentEnv` microVM
+# (E2B; boots on first use, needs the control-plane URL). `--sandbox_num_envs` is the pool size: one env is
+# leased per CONCURRENT episode, so it also caps how many trajectories roll out at once. `--sandbox_command_
+# timeout` / `--sandbox_memory_limit_gb` bound each tool call (a model-emitted command cannot run away).
+#
+# Length budgets: per-turn generation length is --max_completion_length (the sampling max_tokens); the WHOLE
+# trajectory is capped by --max_trajectory_tokens (optional). Multi-turn trajectories are longer than a single
+# completion, so --max_length must fit the accumulated turns.
+#

+# Programmatic Python entry for v5 DPO -- the code equivalent of ../dpo/dpo.sh.
+#
+# A .sh script spells the run as CLI flags; this file builds the SAME run as typed Config OBJECTS and drives
+# it through swift's public programmatic API, so you can compute flags in Python (sweeps, conditional knobs,
+# values from another pipeline) instead of hand-editing a shell string. See ./grpo.py for the full rationale.
+#
+# DPO is an OFFLINE preference algorithm: it forwards a fixed chosen/rejected dataset, it does NOT roll out a
+# sampler. So the placement forcing differs from the online family -- only mode='ray' is forced (the policy is
+# a Ray actor; a full-parameter run also puts a frozen reference on its own 'ref' group). No vLLM sampler.
+#
+# Run: python examples/rl/code/dpo.py   (set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to your free cards first).
+import os
+
+from swift.dev.cli.rl import run_rl_configs
+from swift.dev.config import (
+    CheckpointConfig,
+    DatasetConfig,
+    DistributedConfig,
+    GenerationConfig,
+    LoggingConfig,
+    ModelConfig,
+    PluginConfig,
+    QuantizeConfig,
+    RLConfig,
+    RolloutConfig,
+    TemplateConfig,
+    TrainConfig,
+    TunerConfig,
+)
+
+#: Offline preference rl_types run mode='ray' but roll out nothing (mirrors parse_rl_configs).
+_OFFLINE_TYPES = {'dpo', 'kto', 'cpo', 'orpo', 'simpo', 'rm'}
+
+
+def _force_offline_placement(configs: dict) -> None:
+    """Replicate the CLI's Ray forcing for the offline family, which run_rl_configs does NOT do.
+
+    parse_rl_configs sets mode='ray' (and NO vLLM sampler) for dpo/kto/cpo/orpo/simpo/rm; a programmatic
+    caller bypasses that parser, so it must force the mode itself. Keep in sync with
+    swift/dev/cli/rl.py::parse_rl_configs (the source of truth).
+    """
+    if configs['rl_config'].rl_type in _OFFLINE_TYPES:
+        configs['distributed_config'].mode = 'ray'
+
+
+def build_configs() -> dict:
+    """Assemble the DPO run as Config objects (the same knobs as ../dpo/dpo.sh)."""
+    return {
+        # attn_impl='flash_attention_2' is NOT cosmetic: the offline preference path's default SDPA picks a
+        # cuDNN bf16 kernel whose backward returns NaN on this box, so DPO must pin flash_attention_2 (see
+        # ../dpo/dpo.sh). A programmatic build has to set it just like the CLI script does.
+        'model_config': ModelConfig(
+            model='Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct', torch_dtype='bfloat16', attn_impl='flash_attention_2'),
+        'plugin_config': PluginConfig(),
+        'template_config': TemplateConfig(max_length=2048),
+        'dataset_config': DatasetConfig(dataset=['hjh0119/shareAI-Llama3-DPO-zh-en-emoji#10000']),
+        'train_config': TrainConfig(
+            learning_rate=1e-4,
+            warmup_ratio=0.05,
+            num_train_epochs=1,
+            per_device_train_batch_size=1,
+            gradient_accumulation_steps=8,
+            gradient_checkpointing=True,
+        ),
+        'distributed_config': DistributedConfig(nproc_per_node=2),
+        'checkpoint_config': CheckpointConfig(
+            output_dir='output', save_strategy='steps', save_steps=100, save_total_limit=2),
+        'logging_config': LoggingConfig(report_to=['tensorboard'], logging_steps=5),
+        'tuner_config': TunerConfig(tuner='lora', lora_rank=8, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=['all-linear']),
+        'generation_config': GenerationConfig(),
+        # No sampler for an offline run; RolloutConfig stays at its inert defaults.
+        'rollout_config': RolloutConfig(),
+        # beta is the KL-to-reference strength; under LoRA the reference is the policy's own base with the
+        # adapter disabled (no second model, no extra GPUs).
+        'rl_config': RLConfig(rl_type='dpo', beta=0.1),
+        'quantize_config': QuantizeConfig(),
+        'megatron_config': None,
+        'moe_config': None,
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    os.environ.setdefault('USE_SWIFT_V5', '1')
+    configs = build_configs()
+    _force_offline_placement(configs)
+    history = run_rl_configs(configs)
+    # DPO convergence: rewards/margins rising and rewards/accuracies -> 1 (a reference-gated DPOMetric tag).
+    print(f'DPO finished: {len(history)} optimizer steps; last loss={history[-1].get("loss") if history else None}')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+# it through swift's public programmatic API, so you can compute flags in Python (sweeps, conditional knobs,

+# run_rl -- exactly what `swift rl` does after parsing argv. The ONE thing a programmatic caller must do
+# itself is the PLACEMENT FORCING that normally lives in the argv parser (parse_rl_configs): every ONLINE

+#
+# Run: python examples/rl/code/grpo.py   (set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to your free cards first).
+import os
+
+from swift.dev.cli.rl import run_rl_configs
+from swift.dev.config import (
+    CheckpointConfig,
+    DatasetConfig,
+    DistributedConfig,
+    GenerationConfig,
+    LoggingConfig,
+    ModelConfig,
+    PluginConfig,
+    QuantizeConfig,
+    RLConfig,
+    RolloutConfig,
+    TemplateConfig,
+    TrainConfig,
+    TunerConfig,
+)
+
+#: Online rl_types roll out on a separate vLLM sampler over Ray (mirrors parse_rl_configs).
+_ONLINE_TYPES = {'grpo', 'ppo', 'rft', 'gkd', 'opsd', 'mopd'}
+
+
+def _force_online_placement(configs: dict) -> None:
+    """Replicate the CLI's Ray+vLLM placement forcing, which run_rl_configs does NOT do.
+
+    parse_rl_configs applies this after parsing argv; a programmatic caller bypasses that parser, so it
+    must force the placement itself or the online loop would build with no sampler. Keep in sync with
+    swift/dev/cli/rl.py::parse_rl_configs (the source of truth).
+    """
+    rl_config = configs['rl_config']
+    if rl_config.rl_type in _ONLINE_TYPES:
+        rollout_config = configs['rollout_config']
+        rollout_config.use_vllm = True
+        rollout_config.vllm_mode = rollout_config.vllm_mode or 'colocate'
+        configs['distributed_config'].mode = 'ray'

+

+    """Assemble the GRPO run as Config objects (the same knobs as ../grpo/grpo.sh)."""

+        'template_config': TemplateConfig(max_length=3072),
+        'dataset_config': DatasetConfig(dataset=['AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR#5000']),
+        'train_config': TrainConfig(

+            warmup_ratio=0.05,
+            num_train_epochs=1,
+            per_device_train_batch_size=2,
+            gradient_accumulation_steps=4,
+            gradient_checkpointing=True,
+        ),
+        # mode='ray' is forced by _force_online_placement; nproc_per_node IS required (in Ray mode the driver
+        # orchestrates and holds no GPU). Pick free cards via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.
+        'distributed_config': DistributedConfig(nproc_per_node=2),
+        'checkpoint_config': CheckpointConfig(
+            output_dir='output', save_strategy='steps', save_steps=100, save_total_limit=2),
+        'logging_config': LoggingConfig(report_to=['tensorboard'], logging_steps=1),
+        'tuner_config': TunerConfig(tuner='lora', lora_rank=8, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=['all-linear']),
+        'generation_config': GenerationConfig(temperature=1.0, max_new_tokens=2048),
+        # GRPO is Ray-only with a weight-syncable vLLM sampler; colocate shares the trainer GPUs.
+        'rollout_config': RolloutConfig(vllm_mode='colocate', vllm_gpu_memory_utilization=0.5),

+            epsilon=0.2,
+            num_iterations=1,
+            beta=0.04,

+            log_completions=True,
+        ),
+        'quantize_config': QuantizeConfig(),
+        'megatron_config': None,
+        'moe_config': None,
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    os.environ.setdefault('USE_SWIFT_V5', '1')
+    configs = build_configs()
+    _force_online_placement(configs)
+    history = run_rl_configs(configs)
+    # Judge convergence by the REWARD curve (train/total_reward climbing), not the loss -- see ../grpo/grpo.sh.
+    print(f'GRPO finished: {len(history)} optimizer steps; '
+          f'last reward={history[-1].get("reward") if history else None}')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+#
+# A .sh script spells the run as CLI flags; this file builds the SAME run as typed Config OBJECTS and drives
+# it through swift's public programmatic API, so you can compute flags in Python (sweeps, conditional knobs,
+# values from another pipeline) instead of hand-editing a shell string. See ./grpo.py for the full rationale.
+#
+# OPSD is an ONLINE distillation algorithm: the student rolls out on a vLLM sampler and a frozen teacher
+# scores those completions, so it takes the SAME online placement forcing as GRPO (use_vllm + mode='ray').
+# It also loads a custom dataset plugin (../opsd/opsd_plugin.py) via PluginConfig.external_plugins.
+#
+# Run: python examples/rl/code/opsd.py   (set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to your free cards first).
+import os
+
+from swift.dev.cli.rl import run_rl_configs
+from swift.dev.config import (
+    CheckpointConfig,
+    DatasetConfig,
+    DistributedConfig,
+    GenerationConfig,
+    LoggingConfig,
+    ModelConfig,
+    PluginConfig,
+    QuantizeConfig,
+    RLConfig,
+    RolloutConfig,
+    TemplateConfig,
+    TrainConfig,
+    TunerConfig,
+)
+
+#: Online rl_types roll out on a separate vLLM sampler over Ray (mirrors parse_rl_configs).
+_ONLINE_TYPES = {'grpo', 'ppo', 'rft', 'gkd', 'opsd', 'mopd'}
+
+#: The OPSD dataset plugin, resolved from THIS file's location so the example runs from any CWD.
+_OPSD_PLUGIN = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..', 'opsd', 'opsd_plugin.py')
+
+
+def _force_online_placement(configs: dict) -> None:
+    """Replicate the CLI's Ray+vLLM placement forcing, which run_rl_configs does NOT do.
+
+    parse_rl_configs applies this after parsing argv; a programmatic caller bypasses that parser, so it
+    must force the placement itself or the online loop would build with no sampler. Keep in sync with
+    swift/dev/cli/rl.py::parse_rl_configs (the source of truth).
+    """
+    rl_config = configs['rl_config']
+    if rl_config.rl_type in _ONLINE_TYPES:
+        rollout_config = configs['rollout_config']
+        rollout_config.use_vllm = True
+        rollout_config.vllm_mode = rollout_config.vllm_mode or 'colocate'
+        configs['distributed_config'].mode = 'ray'
+
+
+def build_configs() -> dict:
+    """Assemble the OPSD run as Config objects (the same knobs as ../opsd/opsd.sh)."""
+    return {
+        'model_config': ModelConfig(model='Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct', torch_dtype='bfloat16'),
+        # external_plugins imports the dataset plugin BEFORE anything is built, so the `opsd_numina` dataset
+        # name below resolves (PluginRegistry.load_configured; see ../opsd/opsd_plugin.py).
+        'plugin_config': PluginConfig(external_plugins=[_OPSD_PLUGIN]),
+        # max_length carries the PRIVILEGED teacher view (question + reference solution), which is longer than
+        # the student prompt -- do not shrink it below the encoded reference length or rows are truncated.
+        'template_config': TemplateConfig(max_length=8192),
+        'dataset_config': DatasetConfig(dataset=['opsd_numina#5000']),
+        'train_config': TrainConfig(
+            learning_rate=2e-5,
+            warmup_ratio=0.05,
+            num_train_epochs=1,
+            per_device_train_batch_size=4,
+            gradient_accumulation_steps=1,
+            gradient_checkpointing=True,
+        ),
+        'distributed_config': DistributedConfig(nproc_per_node=2),
+        'checkpoint_config': CheckpointConfig(
+            output_dir='output', save_strategy='steps', save_steps=100, save_total_limit=2, save_only_model=True),
+        'logging_config': LoggingConfig(report_to=['tensorboard'], logging_steps=1),
+        'tuner_config': TunerConfig(tuner='lora', lora_rank=8, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=['all-linear']),
+        'generation_config': GenerationConfig(max_new_tokens=2048),
+        'rollout_config': RolloutConfig(vllm_mode='colocate', vllm_gpu_memory_utilization=0.5),
+        # teacher_model is the frozen scorer; lmbda=1.0 is purely on-policy (required for the async/streaming
+        # distillation loop); opsd_reverse selects the reverse-KL OPSD objective; num_generations=1 (a single
+        # student rollout per prompt, teacher-scored).
+        'rl_config': RLConfig(
+            rl_type='opsd',
+            teacher_model=['Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct'],

+            num_generations=1,
+            sampling_temperature=1.0,
+            max_completion_length=2048,
+        ),
+        'quantize_config': QuantizeConfig(),
+        'megatron_config': None,
+        'moe_config': None,
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> None:

+    configs = build_configs()

+    print(f'OPSD finished: {len(history)} optimizer steps; last loss={history[-1].get("loss") if history else None}')

+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+# v5 Contrastive Preference Optimization (CPO) with LoRA, on 2 GPUs through Ray.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type cpo` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.preference.run_dpo (the offline-preference family: dpo/kto/cpo/orpo/simpo/rm share one entry point).
+#
+# What CPO does: it is DPO's preference margin WITHOUT the reference model, plus an explicit behaviour-
+# cloning term. The margin still pushes the chosen completion's logp above the rejected one's, but there is
+# no logp_reference subtracted -- CPO assumes the reference is uniform and drops it, which removes the second
+# forward pass entirely. On top of the margin it adds an NLL (cross-entropy) loss on the CHOSEN completion,
+# weighted by --cpo_alpha (twinkle names it bc_coef), so the policy is also directly supervised toward the
+# preferred answer. That BC anchor is what replaces the reference's role of keeping the policy sensible.
+#
+# Reference-free: because there is no reference, a CPO run loads NO second model and runs NO adapter-disabled
+# forward -- lighter than DPO. Do NOT pass --ref_model (the validator rejects it for cpo); do NOT pass
+# --reference_free (that is a DPO knob, CPO has no reference to free).
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: CPO is reference-free, so unlike DPO it has NO rewards/margins and NO
+# rewards/accuracies -- those need reference logps (the implicit reward is beta*(logp_policy - logp_reference)),
+# which CPO never computes. twinkle.metric's DPOMetric emits them only when a reference is present, so the
+# record here holds just logps/chosen|rejected (the scalar tags carry NO `train/` prefix):
+#   - console head signal:  `step N  loss=...  grad_norm=...` (no margins/accuracies);
+#   - tensorboard scalars:  `logps/chosen` (should RISE), `logps/rejected` (should FALL), so the GAP
+#                           logps/chosen - logps/rejected WIDENS -- that widening is the preference being
+#                           learned -- plus `loss` (falls) and `grad_norm`. No `rewards/*`, no `logps/ref_*`.
+#
+# Data / NO periodic eval / placement: identical to DPO. --dataset is a chosen/rejected preference set fed
+# INTERLEAVED; --per_device_train_batch_size counts preference ROWS (pairs). Offline preference training has
+# no eval loop, so there is no --split_dataset_ratio / --eval_steps (an eval split with --eval_steps raises
+# NotImplementedError). mode='ray' is forced, no vLLM sampler; --nproc_per_node is required (the driver holds
+# no GPU and sizes the data-parallel actor group). `#10000` takes a 10000-row slice of the real hub dataset.
+# --padding_free true is wired for cpo and improves throughput on length-varied pairs.
+#
+# Attention kernel: --attn_impl flash_attention_2 is PINNED because bf16 training on the default SDPA path can
+# select a cuDNN attention kernel whose BACKWARD returns NaN on some torch/cuDNN builds (reproduced on torch
+# 2.11 / cuDNN 9.19: loss goes NaN a few steps in, during warmup, while the lr is still ~0 -- a kernel NaN, not
+# divergence). flash-attn needs the flash-attn package and an Ampere+ GPU; drop the flag only if your stack does
+# not hit the SDPA NaN.
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0/2 busy, so the default below uses 1,3. The global batch is
+# per_device * dp * grad_accum; going to --nproc_per_node 1 halves dp, so double --gradient_accumulation_steps
+# to 16 to hold the effective batch.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold, not a 2-step demo. For a fast smoke run, shrink everything at once: a
+# smaller policy (Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), a tiny slice (`#512`), and cap `--max_steps 60`.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type cpo \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'hjh0119/shareAI-Llama3-DPO-zh-en-emoji#10000' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --beta 0.1 \
+    --cpo_alpha 1.0 \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --gradient_checkpointing true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# swift.dev.recipe.preference.run_dpo (the offline-preference family: dpo/kto/cpo/orpo/simpo/rm share one entry point).
+#
+# What DPO does: it turns a preference dataset into a policy update WITHOUT a reward model and WITHOUT
+# rollout. Each row is a prompt plus a CHOSEN and a REJECTED completion. The loss maximises the margin
+# between the policy's implicit reward on the chosen vs the rejected completion, where the implicit reward
+# is beta * (logp_policy - logp_reference). The frozen reference keeps the policy from drifting arbitrarily
+# far to widen the margin; --beta weights that anchor (larger beta = tighter leash to the reference).
+#
+# Reference under LoRA: DPO needs a frozen reference, but a LoRA run does NOT load a second model -- the
+# reference is the policy's OWN base weights with the adapter DISABLED (run_dpo builds it automatically via
+# forward_only(disable_lora=True)), so it costs no extra GPU. A FULL-parameter run instead loads a separate
+# frozen ref_model (defaulted to the policy's init) on its own 'ref' DeviceGroup -- pass --ref_model only to
+# point at a different checkpoint. Do NOT pass --ref_model to a LoRA run: the validator rejects it.
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: judge convergence by the REWARD MARGIN and ACCURACY, not the raw loss. Every step's
+# record is assembled from twinkle.metric's DPOMetric, so watch (the scalar tags carry NO `train/` prefix):
+#   - console head signal:  `step N  loss=...  rewards/margins=<chosen_r - rejected_r>  rewards/accuracies=<% chosen wins>`;
+#   - tensorboard scalars:  `rewards/margins` (should RISE), `rewards/accuracies` (should climb toward 100%),
+#                           `rewards/chosen`, `rewards/rejected`, `logps/chosen` (rises), `logps/rejected`
+#                           (falls), `logps/ref_chosen`, `logps/ref_rejected`, plus `loss` and `grad_norm`.
+# A rising margin with an accuracy approaching 100% is the preference signal being learned; the loss alone
+# (a softplus of the margin) hides the trend. The margin/accuracy are present BECAUSE DPO has a reference:
+# the implicit reward is beta*(logp_policy - logp_reference), so DPOMetric needs the reference logps to form
+# them (the reference-free cpo/orpo/simpo log only logps/chosen|rejected -- see those examples).
+#
+# Data: --dataset is a chosen/rejected preference set. The template encodes each row into chosen_*/rejected_*
+# features and PreferenceLoop feeds them INTERLEAVED ([chosen_1, rejected_1, chosen_2, ...]), the layout the
+# DPO loss's even/odd split expects, so every micro-batch stays even and gradient accumulation stays correct.
+# --per_device_train_batch_size counts preference ROWS (pairs); each row becomes two sequences internally.
+# This example uses the real hub dataset hjh0119/shareAI-Llama3-DPO-zh-en-emoji; `#10000` takes a 10000-row slice.
+#
+# NO periodic eval: offline preference training does not implement an eval loop -- passing an eval split with
+# --eval_steps raises NotImplementedError. So there is no --split_dataset_ratio / --eval_steps here (the v4
+# legacy scripts carried both; they are dead on the v5 path and removed). Judge progress on the train metrics.
+#
+# Variants (all off by default, so the run below is canonical sigmoid DPO):
+#   --rpo_alpha 0.1        add an NLL/SFT term on the chosen response (RPO) to curb likelihood displacement;
+#   --loss_type ipo|hinge  a different DPO objective; --loss_type sigmoid bco_pair sft + --loss_weights
+#                          0.8 0.2 1.0 combines several as a weighted sum (MPO);
+#   --reference_free true  drop the reference log-ratio (no anchor); --f_divergence_type reshapes the margin.
+# --padding_free true is wired for the paired family and improves throughput on length-varied pairs.
+#
+# Placement: the offline preference family runs mode='ray' like every RL path -- the policy is a Ray actor on
+# the 'model' DeviceGroup -- but it rolls out NOTHING, so there is no vLLM sampler and no vllm_mode flag. The
+# dev CLI forces mode=ray for --rlhf_type dpo; --nproc_per_node IS required because in Ray mode the driver
+# orchestrates and holds no GPU (it sizes the data-parallel actor group).
+#
+# Attention kernel: --attn_impl flash_attention_2 is PINNED because bf16 training on the default SDPA path can
+# select a cuDNN attention kernel whose BACKWARD returns NaN on some torch/cuDNN builds (reproduced on torch
+# 2.11 / cuDNN 9.19: loss is a correct ln2=0.6932 at step 1, then goes NaN a few steps in -- during warmup,
+# while the lr is still ~0, so it is a kernel NaN, not divergence). flash-attn is the stable, fast path; it
+# needs the flash-attn package and an Ampere+ GPU. If your stack does not hit the SDPA NaN you may drop the
+# flag (or pass --attn_impl sdpa/eager), but flash_attention_2 is the safe default for bf16 preference training.
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0/2 busy, so the default below uses 1,3. Adjust
+# CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to the cards you actually have; a LoRA DPO on a 7B fits a single ~24GB card, so
+# --nproc_per_node 1 with one device also works (the global batch is per_device * dp * grad_accum, so double
+# --gradient_accumulation_steps to 16 to keep the same effective batch when dp drops from 2 to 1).
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold (a full pass over a 10000-row slice), not a 2-step demo, so it downloads a
+# 7B policy and runs a while. For a fast smoke run, shrink everything at once: a smaller policy
+# (Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), a tiny slice (`#512`), and cap `--max_steps 60`.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type dpo \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'hjh0119/shareAI-Llama3-DPO-zh-en-emoji#10000' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --beta 0.1 \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --gradient_checkpointing true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 Generalized Knowledge Distillation (GKD) with LoRA, on 3 GPUs through Ray + vLLM.
+# Paper: "On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes"
+#        https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI (swift.dev.cli.rl). `--rlhf_type gkd` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.distill.run_gkd.
+#
+# What GKD does: the student is trained to match a frozen teacher ON SEQUENCES THE STUDENT ITSELF GENERATES,
+# so it learns to correct its own mistakes instead of only imitating a fixed corpus. Each round the student
+# produces a response, the teacher re-scores those SAME tokens with `forward_only(return_logits=True)`, and the
+# student is pulled toward the teacher's FULL-VOCAB distribution with a beta-weighted Jensen-Shannon divergence
+# (twinkle.loss.gkd.GKDLoss). This is the key contrast with OPSD/MOPD, which use a logits-free sampled-token k3
+# surrogate: GKD scores the teacher's whole per-token distribution.
+#
+# lmbda -- GKD's signature on/off-policy mixing knob (this is what sets GKD apart from the always-on-policy
+# OPSD/MOPD):
+#   * lmbda=1.0  purely ON-policy: every round rolls out from the student's live weights. Rides the streaming
+#                driver and is the only setting async (--async_mode one_step_off) accepts.
+#   * lmbda=0.5  (used here, and the config default) each round COIN-FLIPS: with probability lmbda it rolls out
+#                on-policy, otherwise it distils on the DATASET'S OWN completions for that round. Off-policy
+#                rounds need the dataset to carry assistant completions (alpaca-gpt4-data-zh below does), run on
+#                the synchronous driver, and are why --lmbda<1 is rejected together with any async setting.
+#   * lmbda=0.0  fully OFF-policy: static-corpus KD on the dataset completions (no student generation at all).
+#
+# Teacher selection (every teacher scores with forward_only; there is NO HTTP server -- server teachers were
+# removed, all-Ray premise):
+#   * SEPARATE FROZEN TEACHER (used here): --teacher_model is a DISTINCT, stronger model (a 7B teacher into a
+#     1.5B student). It is built as a frozen Ray actor on its OWN 'teacher' DeviceGroup, so it needs +1 GPU
+#     beyond the trainer/sampler cards. It MUST share the student's tokenizer (both Qwen2.5 here), since it
+#     re-scores the student's own response token ids. A distinct checkpoint also matters for a visible signal:
+#     a self-teacher scores near-identical logits at init, so the divergence -- and the gradient -- starts ~0.
+#   * DISABLE-ADAPTER self-teacher: set --teacher_model == --model with a LoRA student -> the teacher becomes
+#     the student's own FROZEN BASE (adapter disabled), the paper's headline self-distillation setup, reusing
+#     the policy actor (NO extra GPU). Because the base and the LoRA student start identical, expect a small
+#     initial divergence that grows as lora_B moves.
+#   GKD has NO dynamic-self mode: unlike OPSD, dropping --teacher_model entirely (teacher_model=None without a
+#   LoRA student) is an error, not a moving-target self-teacher. GKD always needs an explicit teacher.
+#
+# GKD-only loss knobs (OPSD/MOPD read none of these; --beta in particular is REJECTED there, not ignored):
+#   * --beta (default 0.5) is the JSD mixture weight: beta=0 -> forward KL (mean-seeking), beta=1 -> reverse KL
+#     (mode-seeking), beta=0.5 -> symmetric JSD. Shown explicitly below for discoverability.
+#   * --temperature (default 0.9) softens the teacher/student logits inside the divergence. It is the
+#     DISTILLATION temperature, kept apart from --sampling_temperature (how hot the student ROLLS OUT);
+#     sampling_temperature defaults to temperature when unset.
+#   * --gkd_logits_topk (unset here) scores only the teacher's top-k logits instead of the full vocab, trading a
+#     little fidelity for a large memory cut on big-vocab teachers.
+#   * --sft_alpha (unset here, 0) adds a supervised cross-entropy term on the OFF-policy dataset rounds only
+#     (useful when the student has not seen the corpus style, e.g. distilling a thinking-format teacher).
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: GKD's loss IS the teacher->student divergence (the beta-JSD), so -- unlike RL, where you
+# watch the REWARD -- here a FALLING loss over the run is the convergence signal: the student's distribution is
+# collapsing onto the teacher's. There is no reward channel (GKD scores no ground truth). The console head signal
+# is `step N  loss=...`. swift registers NO GKD-specific algorithm metric, so the record holds only twinkle's
+# auto-registered base metrics, all BARE keys (no `train/` prefix):
+#   - `loss` + `grad_norm` (LossMetric): the beta-JSD divergence and its gradient. Per-round it JITTERS, because
+#     with --lmbda<1 an off-policy dataset round and an on-policy rollout round have different difficulty -- read
+#     the trend over the run, not step to step.
+#   - `accuracy` / `correct_tokens` / `total_tokens` (the Accuracy metric): the student's per-token argmax match
+#     against the labels over the scored completion tokens. A secondary read on how close the student's greedy
+#     decode already is to the target; it is NOT the distillation objective (which is the full-distribution JSD).
+#   - `iters` and `learning rate(param group N)` (TrainMetric). No `rewards/*`, no policy or value terms.
+# There is likewise no --log_completions: completion logging is GRPO-only (it lives in GRPOLoop's
+# rollout assembly, which the distillation loops bypass), so on GKD it is a dead flag the config validator
+# rejects.
+#
+# Dataset: with --lmbda 0.5 the off-policy rounds distil on the dataset's OWN completions, so the dataset must
+# carry assistant turns. AI-ModelScope/alpaca-gpt4-data-zh (instruction + output) does; `#5000` takes a 5000-row
+# slice. A purely on-policy run (--lmbda 1.0) needs only prompts and can use examples/rl/data/prompts.jsonl.
+#
+# num_generations 1: distillation samples ONE trajectory per prompt -- there is no group-relative baseline as in
+# GRPO, so a group of completions would only multiply the teacher's full-vocab scoring cost. The step budget is
+# derived from the prompt set x num_train_epochs (NOT a toy --max_steps).
+#
+# Placement: GKD is Ray-only with a weight-syncable vLLM sampler -- the dev CLI forces
+# vllm_mode=colocate and mode=ray for --rlhf_type gkd. --nproc_per_node IS required because in Ray mode the
+# driver orchestrates and holds no GPU. colocate shares the trainer GPUs with the sampler (CUDA-IPC weight sync,
+# sleep/wake hand-over each step), so --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization must leave room for training; the separate
+# teacher is placed on its own card AFTER the trainer/sampler cards.
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0/2 busy, so the default below uses 1,3 (trainer+sampler,
+# colocate) and 4 (the separate frozen teacher): 2 + 1 = 3 GPUs. Adjust CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, --nproc_per_node
+# and --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization to the cards/memory you actually have; a disable-adapter self-teacher drops
+# the third card.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold (a full pass over a 5000-row slice, --num_train_epochs 1), not a 2-step demo,
+# so it downloads a 7B teacher and a 1.5B student and runs a while. For a fast smoke run, shrink everything at
+# once: a tiny student with a tiny DISTINCT teacher of the SAME tokenizer family (--model
+# Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --teacher_model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B), a tiny slice
+# (`AI-ModelScope/alpaca-gpt4-data-zh#256`), --nproc_per_node 1, and cap `--max_steps 4` (with --lmbda 0.5 and
+# the default seed the first four rounds hit BOTH an off-policy and on-policy round, so the smoke exercises the
+# dataset-completion path AND the vLLM rollout + teacher-scoring path).
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3,4 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type gkd \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct \
+    --teacher_model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'AI-ModelScope/alpaca-gpt4-data-zh#5000' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --lmbda 0.5 \
+    --beta 0.5 \
+    --temperature 1.0 \
+    --num_generations 1 \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --vllm_mode colocate \
+    --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization 0.5 \
+    --max_completion_length 2048 \
+    --max_length 8192 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 4 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 1 \
+    --learning_rate 2e-5 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --logging_steps 1 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --save_only_model true \
+    --gradient_checkpointing true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 GRPO, ASYNC (overlapping rollout) with LoRA -- a feature sub-example of ../grpo.sh, on 3 GPUs.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type grpo` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.grpo.run_grpo. Read ../grpo.sh FIRST: this file changes only the ROLLOUT CADENCE, not the
+# GRPO objective (group-relative advantage, clipped surrogate, --orm accuracy, --beta KL). Everything GRPO
+# means is explained there; here we only turn on async.
+#
+# What async does: by default GRPO is SYNCHRONOUS (--async_mode none) -- it admits one rollout window,
+# DRAINS it (nothing left in flight), trains on it, publishes the new weights to the sampler, and only then
+# generates the next window. The sampler sits idle while the trainer runs and vice-versa. Async OVERLAPS
+# them: the sampler keeps generating the NEXT window on its own GPUs while the trainer updates on the
+# current one. The knob is a STALENESS LADDER -- how many policy versions a rollout may run ahead of the
+# weights it is trained against:
+#   - none          staleness 0: strictly on-policy, no overlap (the synchronous default, ../grpo.sh).
+#   - one_step_off  staleness 1: train version v while the sampler already generates v+1 (below).
+#   - fully_async   staleness up to --max_staleness N: the sampler runs several versions ahead, absorbing a
+#                   deeper skew (set --async_mode fully_async --max_staleness N; N>=1).
+# A sample is never TRAINED more than max_staleness versions after it was GENERATED -- the streaming
+# driver's in-flight staleness gate enforces that bound on every step.
+#
+# Why staleness > 0 needs three companions (validate refuses the run without them -- they are not optional):
+#   1. --vllm_mode disaggregated: overlap needs the sampler on its OWN GPUs. 'colocate' time-shares ONE
+#      DeviceGroup between trainer and sampler (a sleep/wake hand-over each step), so it physically cannot
+#      generate while training -- validate rejects colocate + an overlapping async_mode.
+#   2. --rollout_importance_sampling_mode: GRPO trains on RAW sampled tokens, so a stale (off-policy) batch
+#      needs a token-level importance-sampling correction (token_truncate / sequence_mask) or the ratio is
+#      silently wrong. (PPO's clipped surrogate and the distillation family's teacher target already bound
+#      the update, so they do NOT require this -- it is a GRPO-specific off-policy fix.)
+#   3. in_place publish + partial rollout: an overlapping publish OVERWRITES the sampler's single live weight
+#      copy WHILE generations are in flight, so each in-flight generation is aborted and resumed on the fresh
+#      weights (--weight_sync_strategy in_place --allow_partial_rollout true). process DERIVES both from the
+#      async_mode default, so you may omit them; they are spelled out below to document what the regime does.
+#
+# Device budget (disaggregated): total GPUs = --nproc_per_node (trainer) + sampler_world_size
+# (--vllm_tensor_parallel_size, default 1) on DISJOINT ranks. Below: nproc_per_node 2 (trainer) + 1 (sampler)
+# = 3 cards, so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES lists three.
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: judge convergence by the REWARD curve exactly as in ../grpo.sh (`step N loss= reward=`,
+# tensorboard train/total_reward climbing). Async ADDS a set of staleness telemetry scalars (bare keys, no
+# train/ prefix):
+#   - stream_publishes: how many trained policies were pushed into the disaggregated sampler. This is the
+#     signature the overlap is REAL -- it must ADVANCE every window (1,2,3,...). A flat 0 means the sampler
+#     rolled out on stale disk weights the whole time (no publish reached it).
+#   - version_span_mean / max_partial_span: the observed policy-version skew. The INVARIANT is a CEILING --
+#     <= max_staleness on EVERY step (1 here) -- enforced by the driver's in-flight staleness gate. They are
+#     NOT expected to be non-zero: whether a generation is slow enough to be consumed a version later is
+#     timing-dependent, so a fast run legitimately shows 0 (a smoke run of a 0.5B policy showed all-zero spans
+#     with stream_publishes still advancing). Read them as "never above the bound", not "must be positive".
+#   - partial_ratio / off_policy_consumed: the fraction of generations interrupted-and-resumed at a publish,
+#     and samples trained off-policy. Also bounded (not forced non-zero) for the same timing reason.
+# So the async proof is stream_publishes advancing WHILE every span stays <= max_staleness -- not a non-zero
+# span. (At staleness 0, ../grpo.sh, every one of these except stream_publishes is EXACTLY 0 by construction:
+# the drain barrier leaves nothing in flight at a publish.)
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0 busy, so the default below uses 1,3,5. Adjust
+# CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, --nproc_per_node and --vllm_tensor_parallel_size to the cards you actually have.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold (a full pass over a 5000-row slice). For a fast smoke run shrink the
+# bounded dimensions only: a smaller policy (Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), a tiny slice (`#64`),
+# --nproc_per_node 1 (then 2 cards total: 1 trainer + 1 sampler), and --max_steps 4. Keep --async_mode,
+# --vllm_mode disaggregated and --rollout_importance_sampling_mode -- they are the legality-defining flags;
+# dropping them would silently turn this back into the synchronous ../grpo.sh and prove nothing about async.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3,5 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type grpo \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR#5000' \
+    --system "You are a helpful math assistant. Solve the problem step by step and put your final answer within \boxed{}." \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --orm accuracy \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --vllm_mode disaggregated \
+    --vllm_tensor_parallel_size 1 \
+    --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization 0.5 \
+    --async_mode one_step_off \
+    --rollout_importance_sampling_mode token_truncate \
+    --weight_sync_strategy in_place \
+    --allow_partial_rollout true \
+    --parameter_sync_step 1 \
+    --num_generations 8 \
+    --advantage_estimator grpo \
+    --epsilon 0.2 \
+    --num_iterations 1 \
+    --beta 0.04 \
+    --temperature 1.0 \
+    --max_completion_length 2048 \
+    --max_length 3072 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 2 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --logging_steps 1 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --log_completions true \
+    --gradient_checkpointing true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+# v5 Group-Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with LoRA, on 2 GPUs through Ray + vLLM.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type grpo` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.grpo.run_grpo.
+#
+# What GRPO does: it is a policy-gradient method with NO critic/value model. Each step: sample
+# --num_generations completions per prompt from the CURRENT policy (the trained weights are synced into the
+# vLLM sampler before every rollout, so the behaviour policy tracks the trained one), score each completion
+# with the --orm reward, then turn a prompt's group of rewards into a GROUP-RELATIVE advantage
+# (r - mean(group)) / std(group) -- the group mean is the baseline a critic would otherwise learn. The
+# policy is then updated with a PPO-style CLIPPED surrogate (--epsilon) on that advantage, plus an optional
+# KL-to-reference penalty (--beta). Averaging over the group is what makes it critic-free: a completion that
+# scores above its siblings is pushed up, one below is pushed down.
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN (the point of the example): judge convergence by the REWARD curve, NOT by the loss.
+# A policy-gradient loss oscillates around zero by construction and hides the trend. Every step's record is
+# assembled from twinkle.metric components, so watch:
+#   - console head signal:  `step N  loss=...  reward=<mean total reward>`  (the reward should climb);
+#   - tensorboard scalars:  `train/total_reward` (+ per-channel `train/<orm>_reward`), `train/completion_length`,
+#                           and the GRPOMetric policy stats `train/clip_ratio`, `train/approx_kl`,
+#                           `train/policy_confidence`. Add `--log_entropy true` (logging-only: no entropy bonus,
+#                           so training is unchanged) to also surface `train/entropy` -- the entropy-collapse
+#                           diagnostic; without it the forward never computes per-token entropy, so that one
+#                           scalar is absent by design.
+# The reward comes from the driver-side CompletionRewardMetric; the policy stats from the model-registered
+# GRPOMetric -- a single source each, no hand-folded duplicates.
+#
+# num_generations is the GROUP SIZE and must be >= 2 (a lone completion has no siblings to be relative to).
+# The advantage is non-degenerate only when a group's rewards VARY: if all --num_generations completions of a
+# prompt get the same reward, std(group)=0 and that group contributes zero gradient. The rollout therefore
+# samples STOCHASTICALLY (--temperature below), so siblings differ and the group-relative signal is real.
+#
+# Reward: --orm accuracy is MathAccuracy (backed by math_verify); it reads the dataset's `solution` column as
+# ground truth and the completion's \boxed{} answer. This example uses the real hub dataset
+# AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR (the same one examples/train/grpo/internal/real.sh trains on); the `#5000` suffix takes
+# a 5000-row slice. Add more channels (e.g. `--orm accuracy format`) and weight them with `--orm_weights`; a
+# frozen reward MODEL (instead of a rule) is added with `--orm <model_id>` and lands on its own GPUs.
+#
+# KL reference (--beta): GRPO's default beta is 0.04, so a reference term is ON by default. Under LoRA the
+# reference is the policy's OWN base model with the adapter DISABLED -- it reuses the policy actor, so it
+# needs NO second model and NO extra GPUs. Pass `--beta 0` to drop the reference entirely (a full-parameter
+# run instead loads a separate frozen reference on its own DeviceGroup).
+#

+# v5 GRPO with MoE ROUTING REPLAY (R2/R3) -- a feature sub-example of ../grpo.sh, for a Qwen3-MoE policy.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type grpo` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.grpo.run_grpo. Read ../grpo.sh FIRST: this file changes only how the MoE router is handled in
+# the training forward, not the GRPO objective. Everything GRPO means is explained there.
+#
+# The problem routing replay solves: an MoE router picks each token's experts from the CURRENT weights. In
+# GRPO the policy moves between the rollout (which generated a token) and the training forward (which
+# recomputes that token's log-prob for the importance ratio). A training forward that RE-ROUTES under the
+# drifted weights can select DIFFERENT experts than the ones that actually generated the token, so the
+# recomputed log-prob -- and thus the GRPO ratio -- is measured against the wrong expert mixture. Routing
+# replay fixes this: the training forward is driven with `router_replay_action='replay_forward'` and each
+# row's recorded `routed_experts`, so it REPLAYS the generating routing instead of recomputing it.
+#
+# Two modes differ only in WHERE the replayed routing comes from (then feed the same replay path):
+#   - R2  RECORD the training model's OWN routing for the rollout tokens (an extra `forward_only` under the
+#         just-synced generating weights -- a faithful proxy), then replay it. Use R2 when the sampler does
+#         NOT export routing. Costs one extra full-sequence forward per window. This is the default below.
+#   - R3  replay the routing the SAMPLER exported at generation time. Needs a vLLM build + MoE checkpoint
+#         that report routing, turned on with `--vllm_engine_kwargs enable_return_routed_experts=true`; the
+#         installed vLLM exports it for Qwen3-MoE. R3 avoids R2's extra forward (the routing rides the
+#         generation), but if the engine exports none the loop RAISES ('did not export') rather than silently
+#         recomputing -- switch to R2 in that case.
+#
+# Hard constraints (validate refuses the illegal ones up front; the model/engine ones are loud runtime errors):
+#   - GRPO-ONLY. R2/R3 replay is driven inside GRPOLoop; the RFT/GKD/OPSD/PPO loops build their own
+#     forward_backward kwargs without it, so `--router_replay_mode` on a non-GRPO run is rejected.
+#   - MoE-ONLY. A dense policy has no expert routing to record, so R2 on a dense model raises at runtime.
+#   - CHORD-INCOMPATIBLE. CHORD's auxiliary SFT rows carry no expert routing, so they cannot share the replay
+#     forward; `--chord_sft_dataset` + routing replay is rejected.
+#   - Backend-agnostic: R2/R3 work on BOTH `--backend hf` (transformers, default here) and `--backend
+#     megatron` (mcore's moe_enable_routing_replay). Nothing here is transformers-specific.
+#
+# LoRA target scoping (why --target_modules names the attention projections, NOT all-linear): on Qwen3-MoE the
+# experts are PACKED 3D parameters, so peft resolves `all-linear` to the attention projections PLUS the expert
+# weights (as target_parameters). With the experts wrapped, the transformers R2 RECORD setup can no longer read
+# `top_k` off the MoE block and raises. Naming q/k/v/o_proj keeps the LoRA off the packed experts so the
+# router gate stays native and the RECORD->REPLAY mechanism runs cleanly. (On `--backend megatron` LoRA is
+# built via mcore-bridge, not peft, so `all-linear` is fine there.)
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: exactly as ../grpo.sh -- judge convergence by the REWARD curve (`step N loss= reward=`,
+# tensorboard train/total_reward climbing). Routing replay adds NO new tensorboard tags; its effect is that the
+# GRPO ratio (train/clip_ratio, train/approx_kl) is computed against the CORRECT expert mixture, so an MoE run
+# stays honest as the policy drifts. A green run that trains lora_B is itself the evidence the RECORD->REPLAY
+# path executed: R2's RECORD is fail-loudly (a dense policy or dead wiring returns no routing and raises).
+#
+# DEVICES: Qwen3-30B-A3B is a 30B-total / 3B-active MoE (~60GB bf16). The default below runs colocate over 4
+# cards; pick FREE cards (this box keeps GPU 0 busy). Adjust CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, --nproc_per_node and
+# --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization to the cards/memory you actually have.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold. For a fast smoke run shrink the bounded dimensions only: a tiny slice
+# (`#64`), --max_steps 4, a short --max_completion_length, and fewer --nproc_per_node. Keep
+# --router_replay_mode and the attention-only --target_modules -- they are the legality-defining flags; the
+# MoE model itself CANNOT be shrunk (the expert routing IS the feature), so this example needs a real MoE.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,2,3,4 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type grpo \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
+    --dataset 'AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR#5000' \
+    --system "You are a helpful math assistant. Solve the problem step by step and put your final answer within \boxed{}." \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules q_proj k_proj v_proj o_proj \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --orm accuracy \
+    --router_replay_mode R2 \
+    --nproc_per_node 4 \
+    --vllm_mode colocate \
+    --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization 0.4 \
+    --num_generations 8 \
+    --advantage_estimator grpo \
+    --epsilon 0.2 \
+    --num_iterations 1 \
+    --beta 0.04 \
+    --temperature 1.0 \
+    --max_completion_length 2048 \
+    --max_length 3072 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 2 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --logging_steps 1 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --log_completions true \
+    --gradient_checkpointing true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard
+
+# R3 variant: replay the SAMPLER's exported routing instead of recording it on the training model. Change
+# `--router_replay_mode R2` to `R3` and ask the vLLM engine to export each MoE layer's routing:
+#     --router_replay_mode R3 \
+#     --vllm_engine_kwargs '{"enable_return_routed_experts": true}' \
+# R3 drops R2's extra RECORD forward (the routing rides the generation). If the engine exports no routing the
+# loop raises 'did not export' and points back at R2 -- use R2 with a sampler/build that does not report routing.

+# v5 Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO) with LoRA, on 2 GPUs through Ray.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type kto` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.preference.run_dpo (the offline-preference family: dpo/kto/cpo/orpo/simpo/rm share one entry point).
+#
+# What KTO does: it is the UNPAIRED cousin of DPO. Where DPO needs a (chosen, rejected) pair per prompt, KTO
+# needs only a SINGLE completion per row carrying a BINARY label -- desirable (good) or undesirable (bad). The
+# loss is a Kahneman-Tversky value function: it pushes UP the implicit reward of desirable completions and
+# pushes DOWN that of undesirable ones, each measured against a reference point z_KL. The implicit reward is
+# the same as DPO's, beta * (logp_policy - logp_reference), so KTO DOES need a reference. z_KL is a detached
+# KL estimate the loop computes over a MISMATCHED "KL batch" (each prompt paired with an unrelated completion,
+# built by rotating the completions by one within the batch) -- it is the "status quo" anchor from prospect
+# theory. Being unpaired, KTO trains on the far more abundant thumbs-up/thumbs-down data instead of scarce
+# side-by-side preferences.
+#
+# The `label` column: each dataset row is a conversation whose LAST assistant turn is the completion, plus a
+# boolean `label` (true = desirable, false = undesirable). The template runs in mode='kto' and reads exactly
+# that; there is no rejected_response. A batch that is entirely one-sided still trains, but exercises only half
+# the value function -- a real dataset mixes both.
+#
+# Reference (and why KTO cannot be reference-free): KTO's implicit reward IS the policy-vs-reference log-ratio
+# and z_KL is a KL against that same reference, so both terms need reference logps. --reference_free is
+# therefore REJECTED by the validator for kto. Under LoRA the reference is the policy's OWN base weights with
+# the adapter DISABLED (built automatically, no extra GPU); a full-parameter run loads a separate frozen
+# ref_model. Do NOT pass --ref_model to a LoRA run.
+#
+# Class-imbalance weights: --desirable_weight and --undesirable_weight (both default 1.0) rescale the two
+# branches when the dataset is lopsided (e.g. many more undesirable than desirable rows). Set them so the
+# rarer class is not drowned out; the KTO paper suggests weighting toward a roughly balanced desirable:
+# undesirable ratio.
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: KTO is unpaired, so there is NO reward margin / accuracy -- those are DPO-family
+# paired metrics. swift registers no KTO-specific metric (only dpo/cpo/orpo/simpo get DPOMetric), so the
+# record holds just the bare loss + grad_norm and you judge by the LOSS falling and grad_norm staying finite:
+#   - console head signal:  `step N  loss=...  grad_norm=...`;
+#   - tensorboard scalars:  `loss` and `grad_norm` (no `train/` prefix; no rewards/*, no kl term). The loss
+#                           starts near 0.5 and drifts down slowly -- with a single label per row there is no
+#                           margin to widen, so a steady finite loss + finite grad_norm IS the healthy signal.
+#
+# Data / NO periodic eval / placement: --dataset is the unpaired kto set. Offline preference training has no
+# eval loop, so there is no --split_dataset_ratio / --eval_steps (an eval split raises NotImplementedError).
+# mode='ray' forced, no vLLM sampler; --nproc_per_node required. `#10000` takes a 10000-row slice of the real
+# hub dataset AI-ModelScope/ultrafeedback-binarized-preferences-cleaned-kto. --padding_free true is wired for kto.
+#
+# Attention kernel: --attn_impl flash_attention_2 is PINNED because bf16 training on the default SDPA path can
+# select a cuDNN attention kernel whose BACKWARD returns NaN on some torch/cuDNN builds (reproduced on torch
+# 2.11 / cuDNN 9.19: loss goes NaN a few steps in, during warmup, while the lr is still ~0 -- a kernel NaN, not
+# divergence). flash-attn needs the flash-attn package and an Ampere+ GPU; drop the flag only if your stack does
+# not hit the SDPA NaN.
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0/2 busy, so the default below uses 1,3. Global batch is
+# per_device * dp * grad_accum; --nproc_per_node 1 halves dp, so double --gradient_accumulation_steps to 16.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold, not a 2-step demo. For a fast smoke run, shrink everything at once: a
+# smaller policy (Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), a tiny slice (`#512`), and cap `--max_steps 60`.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type kto \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'AI-ModelScope/ultrafeedback-binarized-preferences-cleaned-kto#10000' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --beta 0.1 \
+    --desirable_weight 1.0 \
+    --undesirable_weight 1.0 \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --gradient_checkpointing true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) with LoRA, on 3 GPUs through Ray + vLLM.
+# Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30406 (Open-MOPD)
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI (swift.dev.cli.rl). `--rlhf_type mopd` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.distill.run_mopd.
+#
+# What MOPD does: the student generates ONE on-policy trajectory; K frozen DOMAIN teachers each re-score that
+# SAME trajectory token-by-token; their per-token distributions are fused into a single target by WEIGHTED
+# PROBABILITY MIXTURE (log sum_k w_k p_k), and the student is pulled toward it with the same sampled-token k3
+# surrogate OPSD uses (twinkle.loss.mopd.MOPDLoss). Compared with single-teacher OPSD/GKD, MOPD reduces the
+# cross-domain degradation a student suffers when trained on ONE teacher's distribution alone. With a single
+# teacher the fused target is exactly that teacher's log-probs, i.e. MOPD degenerates to OPSD.
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: MOPD's loss IS the fused teacher->student divergence (the k3 surrogate), so -- unlike
+# RL, where you watch the REWARD -- here the LOSS FALLING is the convergence signal: the student's distribution
+# is collapsing onto the mixture of the K teachers'. There is no reward channel (MOPD scores no ground truth).
+# Watch the console head signal (`step N  loss=...`) and the tensorboard scalars `loss` +
+# `grad_norm` (LossMetric emits them unprefixed; the `train/`-prefixed keys belong to the reward/policy
+# components MOPD does not register); both come from twinkle.metric components merged by the shared record
+# path, not hand-folded. There is likewise no --log_completions: completion logging is GRPO-only (it lives in
+# GRPOLoop's rollout assembly, which the distillation loops bypass), so on MOPD it is a dead flag the config
+# validator rejects.
+#
+# Teachers: --teacher_model is a LIST, one id per domain expert. EVERY teacher must share the student's
+# tokenizer, since each re-scores the student's OWN response token ids. This example mixes two Qwen2.5 domain
+# experts of the same tokenizer family into a 1.5B student -- a MATH specialist (Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct) and a
+# GENERAL instruct model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) -- so the student learns math from the specialist while retaining
+# general reasoning/formatting from the instruct model, instead of degrading on either when trained on one alone.
+# --teacher_weights is optional (one entry per teacher, non-negative; normalized to sum 1 inside MOPDLoss); unset
+# weights every teacher equally. The weights below favor the math expert on a math corpus.
+#
+# Teacher placement: all K teachers are built as frozen Ray actors that SHARE ONE 'teacher' DeviceGroup -- a
+# single card by default, scoring trajectories SERIALLY (forward_only). That one card must therefore hold the K
+# teachers' COMBINED weights (two 7B models here, ~28GB in bf16); use --teacher_parallel_spec to give the group
+# more GPUs when the teachers are too big for one card. MOPD REJECTS --offload_teacher_model, the single-model
+# disable-adapter self-teacher, and --teacher_adapters (each teacher is a distinct full model). The teacher card
+# is placed AFTER the trainer/sampler cards.
+#
+# Dataset: MOPD has NO privileged `teacher_prompt` view (that is OPSD's single-teacher trick) -- teacher and
+# student see the SAME on-policy prompt -- so MOPD needs NO plugin and reads a plain prompts dataset. This example
+# uses the real hub dataset AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR (the same one GRPO/RFT/OPSD here train on); the `#2000` suffix
+# takes a 2000-row slice. Its rows carry no system turn, so --system supplies the math answering instruction
+# (OPSD's plugin injects one per row, which is why the OPSD example does NOT pass --system).
+#
+# num_generations 1: distillation samples ONE on-policy trajectory per prompt -- there is no group-relative
+# baseline as in GRPO, so a group of completions would only multiply the K teachers' scoring cost. The step budget
+# is derived from the prompt set x num_train_epochs (NOT a toy --max_steps).
+#
+# MOPD v1 applies NO reference-KL term, so --beta is REJECTED (not silently ignored). --sampling_temperature sets
+# how hot the student ROLLS OUT (a separate role from any distillation temperature, which the k3 surrogate does
+# not apply). --opsd_reverse true is the paper's on-policy divergence direction (r = teacher - student; the
+# default it shares with OPSD, shown for discoverability). --lmbda 1.0 samples on-policy every step.
+#
+# Placement: MOPD is Ray-only with a weight-syncable vLLM sampler -- the dev CLI forces use_vllm=true,
+# vllm_mode=colocate and mode=ray for --rlhf_type mopd. --nproc_per_node IS required because in Ray mode the
+# driver orchestrates and holds no GPU. colocate shares the trainer GPUs with the sampler (CUDA-IPC weight sync,
+# sleep/wake hand-over each step), so --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization must leave room for training.
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0/2 busy, so the default below uses 1,3 (trainer+sampler,
+# colocate) and 4 (the ONE 'teacher' group hosting BOTH 7B teachers): 2 + 1 = 3 GPUs. Adjust CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES,
+# --nproc_per_node and --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization to the cards/memory you actually have.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold (a full pass over a 2000-row slice, --num_train_epochs 1), not a 2-step demo,
+# so it downloads two 7B teachers and a 1.5B student and runs a while. For a fast smoke run, shrink everything at
+# once: a tiny student with two tiny teachers of the SAME tokenizer family (--model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
+# --teacher_model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B --teacher_weights 0.6 0.4), a tiny slice
+# (`AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR#8`), and cap `--max_steps 4`.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3,4 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type mopd \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct \
+    --teacher_model Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --teacher_weights 0.7 0.3 \
+    --dataset 'AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR#2000' \
+    --system "You are a helpful math assistant. Solve the problem step by step and put your final answer within \boxed{}." \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --lmbda 1.0 \
+    --opsd_reverse true \
+    --num_generations 1 \
+    --sampling_temperature 1.0 \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --vllm_mode colocate \
+    --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization 0.5 \
+    --max_completion_length 2048 \
+    --max_length 8192 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 4 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 1 \
+    --learning_rate 2e-5 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --logging_steps 1 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --save_only_model true \
+    --gradient_checkpointing true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) with LoRA, on 3 GPUs through Ray + vLLM.
+# Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18734
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI (swift.dev.cli.rl). `--rlhf_type opsd` dispatches
+# to swift.dev.recipe.distill.run_opsd.
+#
+# What OPSD does: the student conditions on the question ALONE; a teacher conditions on a PRIVILEGED view
+# (question + a reference solution) supplied per-row by the dataset's `teacher_prompt` column. Each step the
+# student generates an on-policy response, the teacher re-scores those SAME response tokens under the
+# privileged prompt, and the student is pulled toward the teacher's per-token log-probs with a dense,
+# logits-free sampled-token k3 surrogate (twinkle.loss.opsd.OPSDLoss). Because the two views differ, the
+# distillation signal is non-zero even when the weights are shared.
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: OPSD's loss IS the teacher->student divergence (the k3 surrogate), so -- unlike RL,
+# where you watch the REWARD -- here the LOSS FALLING is the convergence signal: the student's distribution
+# is collapsing onto the privileged teacher's. There is no reward channel (OPSD scores no ground truth).
+# Watch the console head signal (`step N  loss=...`) and the tensorboard scalars `loss` +
+# `grad_norm` (LossMetric emits them unprefixed; the `train/`-prefixed keys belong to the reward/policy
+# components OPSD does not register); both come from twinkle.metric components merged by the shared record
+# path, not hand-folded. There is likewise no --log_completions: completion logging is GRPO-only (it lives in
+# GRPOLoop's rollout assembly, which the distillation loops bypass), so on OPSD it is a dead flag the config
+# validator rejects.
+#
+# Teacher selection (every teacher scores the PRIVILEGED view with forward_only; there is no HTTP server):
+#   * SEPARATE FROZEN TEACHER (used here): --teacher_model is a DISTINCT, stronger model (a 7B teacher into a
+#     1.5B student). It is built as a frozen Ray actor on its OWN 'teacher' DeviceGroup, so it needs +1 GPU
+#     beyond the trainer/sampler cards. It MUST share the student's tokenizer (both Qwen2.5 here), since it
+#     re-scores the student's own response token ids.
+#   * DISABLE-ADAPTER self-teacher: set --teacher_model == --model with a LoRA student -> the teacher is the
+#     student's own FROZEN BASE (adapter disabled) on the privileged view. A stable target, the paper-following
+#     setup (legacy examples/train/rlhf/opsd reports +60% AIME2025), and it reuses the policy actor (NO extra
+#     GPU).
+#   * DYNAMIC self-teacher: drop --teacher_model entirely -> the student's CURRENT weights on the privileged
+#     view (a moving target; the teacher_model=None branch the v5 e2e suite covers). Also no extra GPU.
+#
+# Dataset: OPSD is DEFINED by the privileged `teacher_prompt` column. The accompanying plugin derives it from
+# a REAL hub math corpus -- `opsd_numina` streams AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR (the same dataset GRPO/RFT here train
+# on) and builds teacher_prompt from each row's problem/solution. `#5000` takes a 5000-row slice. For an
+# OFFLINE run with no hub access, select the plugin's 4-row `opsd_synthetic`, or the pre-built
+# examples/rl/data/opsd.jsonl (ships teacher_prompt directly, needs no plugin).
+#
+# num_generations 1: distillation samples ONE on-policy trajectory per prompt -- there is no group-relative
+# baseline as in GRPO, so a group of completions would only multiply the teacher's scoring cost. The step
+# budget is derived from the prompt set x num_train_epochs (NOT a toy --max_steps).
+#
+# OPSD v1 applies NO reference-KL term, so --beta is REJECTED (not silently ignored). --sampling_temperature
+# sets how hot the student ROLLS OUT (a separate role from any distillation temperature, which the k3
+# surrogate does not apply). --opsd_reverse true is the paper's on-policy divergence direction
+# (r = teacher - student; the default, shown for discoverability). The plugin already puts a system prompt in
+# every row, so --system is NOT passed here (it would only duplicate the row's own).
+#
+# Placement: OPSD is Ray-only with a weight-syncable vLLM sampler -- the dev CLI forces use_vllm=true,
+# vllm_mode=colocate and mode=ray for --rlhf_type opsd. --nproc_per_node IS required because in Ray mode the
+# driver orchestrates and holds no GPU. colocate shares the trainer GPUs with the sampler (CUDA-IPC weight
+# sync, sleep/wake hand-over each step), so --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization must leave room for training; the
+# separate teacher is placed on its own card AFTER the trainer/sampler cards.
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0/2 busy, so the default below uses 1,3 (trainer+sampler,
+# colocate) and 4 (the separate frozen teacher): 2 + 1 = 3 GPUs. Adjust CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES,
+# --nproc_per_node and --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization to the cards/memory you actually have; a self-teacher
+# (disable-adapter / dynamic) drops the third card.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold (a full pass over a 5000-row slice, --num_train_epochs 1), not a 2-step
+# demo, so it downloads a 7B teacher and a 1.5B student and runs a while. For a fast smoke run, shrink
+# everything at once: a tiny student with a tiny separate teacher of the SAME tokenizer family
+# (--model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --teacher_model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B), a tiny slice (`opsd_numina#16`, or
+# the offline `opsd_synthetic`), and cap `--max_steps 4`.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3,4 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type opsd \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct \
+    --teacher_model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \

+# Copyright (c) ModelScope Contributors. All rights reserved.
+"""OPSD dataset plugin: derive the privileged ``teacher_prompt`` column from a reference solution.
+
+On-Policy Self-Distillation needs one extra column beyond the dialogue: ``teacher_prompt``. It carries
+the PRIVILEGED view the teacher conditions on -- the student's question PLUS a reference solution /
+rubric -- while the student itself only ever sees the question. run_opsd replaces the first user turn
+with ``teacher_prompt`` when it builds the teacher's scoring view, and keeps the response tokens shared
+between teacher and student.
+
+A dataset that already ships a ``teacher_prompt`` column needs no plugin (see examples/rl/data/
+opsd.jsonl). This plugin is the pattern for a REAL dataset that only has a ``solution`` / ``answer``
+column: it registers self-contained datasets whose loaders build ``teacher_prompt`` in code, so the
+derivation lives next to the data rather than being hand-written into every row. Two are registered:
+
+  * ``opsd_numina`` -- the REAL path: streams ``AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR`` from the hub and derives
+    ``teacher_prompt`` from each row's ``problem`` / ``solution`` columns (``OPSDNuminaLoader``);
+  * ``opsd_synthetic`` -- a 4-row in-code corpus that needs NO hub access, for an offline smoke run.
+
+Loaded with ``--external_plugins examples/rl/opsd/opsd_plugin.py`` and selected with ``--dataset
+opsd_numina`` (or ``opsd_synthetic``) -- the ``dataset_type`` each loader registers below. Point
+``OPSDNuminaLoader`` at another hub dataset by changing its ``datasets`` id and the two column names
+``_numina_row`` reads, to distil from any problem/solution corpus.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
+
+from datasets import Dataset as HfDataset
+
+from swift.dev.dataset.loader import DatasetLoader, register_dataset
+
+SYSTEM_PROMPT = 'Solve the problem step by step, and put your final answer within \\boxed{}.'
+
+TRANSITION_PROMPT = ('After understanding the reference solution and the rationale behind each step, '
+                     'now articulate your own step-by-step reasoning that derives the final answer.')
+
+#: (problem, reference solution) pairs. ``_ROWS`` stands in for a real dataset's problem/solution columns.
+_ROWS: List[Dict[str, str]] = [
+    {
+        'problem': 'What is 12 * 8?',
+        'solution': '12 * 8 = 96, so the answer is 96.'
+    },
+    {
+        'problem': 'What is 15 + 27?',
+        'solution': '15 + 27 = 42, so the answer is 42.'
+    },
+    {
+        'problem': 'A shop sells pens 3 for $2. How many dollars do 9 pens cost?',
+        'solution': '9 pens is 9 / 3 = 3 groups of 3, and each group costs $2, so 3 * 2 = $6.'
+    },
+    {
+        'problem': 'What is the area of a rectangle with sides 5 and 4?',
+        'solution': 'Area = length * width = 5 * 4 = 20.'
+    },
+]
+
+
+def _build_row(problem: str, solution: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """One standard row: the student's ``messages`` (question only) plus the teacher's privileged view.
+
+    ``teacher_prompt`` is the FULL replacement for the first user turn, so it repeats the problem and
+    appends the reference solution and a transition instruction. When there is no reference solution the
+    row carries no ``teacher_prompt``; run_opsd rejects such a dataset loudly (a teacher that sees exactly
+    what the student sees makes the distillation signal identically zero -- that is plain GKD, not OPSD).
+    """
+    messages = [
+        {
+            'role': 'system',
+            'content': SYSTEM_PROMPT
+        },
+        {
+            'role': 'user',
+            'content': problem
+        },
+    ]
+    row: Dict[str, Any] = {'messages': messages}
+    if solution:
+        row['teacher_prompt'] = (f'{problem}\n\n'
+                                 f'Here is a reference solution to this problem:\n{solution}\n\n'
+                                 f'{TRANSITION_PROMPT}')
+    return row
+
+
+@register_dataset
+class OPSDSyntheticLoader(DatasetLoader):
+    """``--dataset opsd_synthetic`` loads these rows with no hub access.
+
+    Rows arrive in the standard ``messages`` layout plus a ``teacher_prompt`` column; the auto-detecting
+    format converter passes both through (it keeps unknown columns), and run_opsd reads ``teacher_prompt``
+    from each row's extras. Overriding ``build_dataset`` is the hook a self-contained dataset uses.
+    """
+
+    dataset_type = 'opsd_synthetic'
+
+    def build_dataset(self, subset, split, **kwargs):
+        rows = [_build_row(raw['problem'], raw.get('solution')) for raw in _ROWS]
+        return HfDataset.from_list(rows)
+
+
+def _numina_row(raw: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """One NuminaMath-TIR row -> the standard OPSD row, deriving ``teacher_prompt`` from ``solution``.
+
+    A module-level function (not a closure) so ``datasets.map`` can pickle it under ``num_proc>1``. The
+    returned ``messages`` (system + the problem as the only user turn, no assistant turn) REPLACES the
+    dataset's own ``messages`` column, so the student rolls out on-policy from the bare question while the
+    teacher's privileged view is rebuilt from ``teacher_prompt``.
+    """
+    return _build_row(raw['problem'], raw.get('solution'))
+
+
+@register_dataset
+class OPSDNuminaLoader(DatasetLoader):
+    """``--dataset opsd_numina``: the REAL hub-backed OPSD corpus (``AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR``).
+
+    Declares the hub id so the base :meth:`DatasetLoader.build_dataset` fetches it (through dev's hub
+    layer, ModelScope or HuggingFace per ``USE_HF``); this override only maps each raw row through
+    :func:`_numina_row` to derive ``teacher_prompt`` and drop the raw ``problem`` / ``solution`` columns.
+    The ``#N`` row budget (e.g. ``opsd_numina#2000``) is applied downstream by ``post_process``, so the
+    same slice syntax the other RL examples use works here unchanged.
+    """
+
+    dataset_type = 'opsd_numina'
+    datasets = [('AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR', 'AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR')]
+    tags = ('grpo', 'math', 'distill')
+
+    def build_dataset(self, subset, split, **kwargs):
+        raw = super().build_dataset(subset, split, **kwargs)
+        return raw.map(_numina_row, remove_columns=['problem', 'solution'])
