+# v5 Odds Ratio Preference Optimization (ORPO) with LoRA, on 2 GPUs through Ray.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type orpo` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.preference.run_dpo (the offline-preference family: dpo/kto/cpo/orpo/simpo/rm share one entry point).
+#
+# What ORPO does: it fuses supervised fine-tuning and preference alignment into a SINGLE stage with NO
+# reference model. The loss is the plain NLL (cross-entropy) on the CHOSEN completion -- the SFT term -- plus
+# an ODDS-RATIO penalty that pushes the odds of the chosen completion above the odds of the rejected one. The
+# odds ratio (not the log-prob ratio DPO uses) is what makes the reference unnecessary: the SFT term already
+# anchors the policy to the preferred answer, and the odds-ratio term separates chosen from rejected. The two
+# are combined as  loss = NLL(chosen) + lambda_orpo * odds_ratio_penalty.
+#
+# The beta slot carries lambda_orpo: ORPO has no reference and no KL, so it has no beta of its own. Its single
+# weight is lambda_orpo, which legacy/TRL carry in the beta slot -- so `--beta 0.1` below IS lambda_orpo (the
+# odds-ratio penalty weight), mapped onto twinkle's lambda_orpo by the loss configurator. The default is 0.1;
+# a larger value leans harder on preference separation relative to the SFT term.
+#
+# Reference-free: no second model, no adapter-disabled forward. Do NOT pass --ref_model (rejected for orpo) or
+# --reference_free (a DPO knob; ORPO has no reference to free).
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: ORPO is reference-free, so like CPO it has NO rewards/margins and NO rewards/accuracies
+# (those need reference logps, which ORPO never computes -- DPOMetric emits them only when a reference exists).
+# The record holds just logps/chosen|rejected (scalar tags carry NO `train/` prefix):
+#   - console head signal:  `step N  loss=...  grad_norm=...` (no margins/accuracies);
+#   - tensorboard scalars:  `logps/chosen` (should RISE), `logps/rejected` (should FALL or rise less), so the
+#                           GAP logps/chosen - logps/rejected WIDENS -- the preference being learned -- plus
+#                           `loss` (falls) and `grad_norm`. No `rewards/*`, no `logps/ref_*`.
+# The loss here includes the SFT NLL term on chosen, so it starts higher than pure-DPO and its fall mixes the
+# behaviour-cloning fit with the odds-ratio separation; read the logps GAP for the preference signal itself.
+#
+# Data / NO periodic eval / placement: identical to DPO. --dataset is a chosen/rejected preference set fed
+# INTERLEAVED; --per_device_train_batch_size counts preference ROWS (pairs). No eval loop, so no
+# --split_dataset_ratio / --eval_steps. mode='ray' forced, no vLLM sampler; --nproc_per_node required.
+# `#10000` takes a 10000-row slice. --padding_free true is wired for orpo.
+#
+# Attention kernel: --attn_impl flash_attention_2 is PINNED because bf16 training on the default SDPA path can
+# select a cuDNN attention kernel whose BACKWARD returns NaN on some torch/cuDNN builds (reproduced on torch
+# 2.11 / cuDNN 9.19: loss goes NaN a few steps in, during warmup, while the lr is still ~0 -- a kernel NaN, not
+# divergence). flash-attn needs the flash-attn package and an Ampere+ GPU; drop the flag only if your stack does
+# not hit the SDPA NaN.
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0/2 busy, so the default below uses 1,3. Global batch is
+# per_device * dp * grad_accum; --nproc_per_node 1 halves dp, so double --gradient_accumulation_steps to 16.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold, not a 2-step demo. For a fast smoke run, shrink everything at once: a
+# smaller policy (Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), a tiny slice (`#512`), and cap `--max_steps 60`.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type orpo \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'hjh0119/shareAI-Llama3-DPO-zh-en-emoji#10000' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --beta 0.1 \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --gradient_checkpointing true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with LoRA, on 3 GPUs through Ray + vLLM.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type ppo` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.ppo.run_ppo.
+#
+# What PPO does: it is the online RL method WITH a learned value function -- the piece GRPO drops. Each step:
+# sample --num_generations completions per prompt from the CURRENT policy (trained weights are synced into the
+# vLLM sampler before every rollout), score each completion with a frozen reward MODEL, then compute a
+# PER-TOKEN advantage with Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) against a trained critic. The policy is
+# updated with a PPO-style CLIPPED surrogate (--cliprange) on that advantage plus a per-token KL-to-reference
+# penalty (--kl_coef); the critic is updated in the same step by a CLIPPED value loss (--cliprange_value)
+# toward the GAE returns. GRPO replaces the critic with a group-relative baseline; PPO learns the baseline.
+#
+# The FOUR models PPO assembles (this is why it is the heaviest online path):
+#   1. policy   -- the trained model (LoRA here);
+#   2. critic   -- a trainable seq_cls num_labels=1 VALUE head, built automatically (task='value' keeps its
+#                  per-token output V(s_t) instead of pooling to one scalar). It is initialised from the
+#                  FIRST reward model in --orm (TRL inits the value function from the reward model), or from
+#                  the policy base if the channel carries none. You do NOT configure it separately;
+#   3. reference-- the frozen model the KL penalty anchors to. Under LoRA it is the policy's OWN base with the
+#                  adapter DISABLED (no second model, no extra GPU); a full-parameter run loads a separate
+#                  frozen copy on its own DeviceGroup;
+#   4. reward   -- the frozen scalar reward MODEL (a model-id item of --orm), scoring each completion once.
+#
+# Reward model (READ THIS): PPO's reward is a trained scalar model passed as a MODEL-ID ITEM of the shared
+# --orm channel (rules and models share the one heterogeneous list). It MUST share the policy's
+# tokenizer/template (the four forwards line up token-for-token), so the safe choice is the same base
+# family. For a MEANINGFUL reward, train one on your preference data first with examples/rl/rm/rm.sh, then
+# either point --orm at that full checkpoint, or keep the shared base below and attach the RM LoRA with
+# `--orm_adapters <rm_ckpt>` (one entry per model id in the channel). Loading the bare base as the reward
+# model (as below) initialises its score head randomly: every PPO mechanism (critic, per-token GAE,
+# clipped surrogate + value loss, KL) still runs and trains, but the reward signal is untrained until you
+# supply a real RM -- so treat the bare-base form as a plumbing demo, not an alignment run.
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: judge convergence by the REWARD climbing AND the critic's EXPLAINED VARIANCE staying
+# high -- the clipped-surrogate loss oscillates around zero by construction and hides the trend. Watch:
+#   - console head signal:  `step N  loss=...  value_loss=...  reward=<mean total reward>  explained_variance=...`;
+#   - tensorboard scalars:  `train/total_reward` (should climb), `train/completion_length`, the critic's
+#                           `train/explained_variance` (how well V predicts the returns -- should stay near/
+#                           above 0; a collapse means the critic is not keeping up), `train/value_mean`,
+#                           `train/return_mean`, `train/value_clip_ratio`, and the policy's PPOMetric stats
+#                           `train/clip_ratio`, `train/approx_kl`, `train/policy_confidence`, plus the bare
+#                           `loss`/`grad_norm` (policy) and `value_loss`/`value_grad_norm` (critic).
+# reward comes from the driver-side CompletionRewardMetric; explained_variance/value_* from the critic's
+# PPOValueMetric; clip_ratio/approx_kl from the policy's PPOMetric (which shares GRPOMetric's token stats).
+#
+# PPO knobs: --num_ppo_epochs (default 4) replays each rollout's captured advantages/returns/old_logps/
+# old_values that many times -- the genuine PPO batch re-use; --gamma (1.0) / --lam (0.95) parameterise GAE;
+# --whiten_rewards standardises the advantages across the rollout. --num_generations is completions per prompt.
+#
+# Placement: PPO is Ray-only with a weight-syncable vLLM (or SGLang) sampler, like GRPO/RFT. The dev CLI
+# forces vllm_mode (colocate by default) and mode=ray; --nproc_per_node IS required (the driver
+# holds no GPU). Device budget = nproc_per_node (policy + critic share one mesh, sampler colocates on them)
+# PLUS one disjoint GPU per full-parameter reward model -- so nproc_per_node 2 below needs 3 cards. PPO runs
+# SP=1: the per-token value head does not cover sequence-parallel/packed layouts, and --sequence_parallel_size
+# > 1 is rejected. --padding_free/--packing are likewise not used by the critic path.
+#
+# NO GRPO-only controls: --log_completions (and the GRPO clipping/replay/entropy/FIPO knobs) are rejected for
+# ppo -- completion logging lives in GRPOLoop's rollout assembly, which PPO's own loop bypasses, so it is a
+# dead flag the validator refuses rather than silently ignores.
+#
+# Attention kernel: if bf16 training on the default SDPA path selects a cuDNN attention kernel whose BACKWARD
+# returns NaN on your torch/cuDNN build (loss goes NaN a few steps in, during warmup, while the lr is still ~0
+# -- a kernel NaN, not divergence; reproduced on torch 2.11 / cuDNN 9.19 for the offline-preference family),
+# pin `--attn_impl flash_attention_2` (needs the flash-attn package and an Ampere+ GPU).
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0 busy, so the default below uses 1,3,5 (2 trainer + 1
+# reward). Adjust CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization to the cards/memory you actually have.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold, not a 2-step demo. For a fast smoke run, shrink everything at once: a
+# smaller policy AND reward model (Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct for both), a tiny slice (`#256`),
+# --nproc_per_node 1 (then 2 cards: 1 trainer + 1 reward), --num_generations 2, and cap `--max_steps 4`.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3,5 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type ppo \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'AI-ModelScope/alpaca-gpt4-data-zh#20000' \
+    --orm Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --vllm_mode colocate \
+    --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization 0.4 \
+    --num_generations 2 \
+    --num_ppo_epochs 4 \
+    --cliprange 0.2 \
+    --cliprange_value 0.2 \
+    --gamma 1.0 \
+    --lam 0.95 \
+    --kl_coef 0.05 \
+    --temperature 0.7 \
+    --max_completion_length 512 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-5 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --logging_steps 1 \

+# v5 Rejection-sampling Fine-Tuning (RFT / RAFT / ReST) with LoRA, on 2 GPUs through Ray + vLLM.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type rft` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.rft.run_rft.
+#
+# What RFT does: it reuses GRPO's rollout + reward machinery for a simpler purpose than policy gradient.
+# Each round: sample --rft_num_samples completions per prompt from the CURRENT policy (the trained weights
+# are synced into the vLLM sampler before each rollout, so the behaviour policy tracks the trained one),
+# score them with the --orm reward, KEEP only the good ones, and run plain cross-entropy SFT on the kept
+# set. Repeating over --rft_iterations rounds -- each re-sampling from the just-improved policy -- is the
+# rejection-sampling bootstrap: no advantage estimator, no reference model, no importance ratio. RFT sets
+# the SFT cross_entropy loss, NOT an RL loss.
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: the SFT loss on the kept subset does fall, but the signal that shows the BOOTSTRAP
+# working is the REWARD of the freshly generated rollouts climbing round over round -- the policy is sampling
+# better answers, so more of them clear the filter. Watch:
+#   - console head signal:  `step N  loss=...  reward=<mean total reward of the round's rollouts>`;
+#   - tensorboard scalars:  `train/total_reward` (+ per-channel `train/<orm>_reward`), `train/completion_length`.
+# The reward is fed from the WHOLE generated rollout BEFORE rejection (the driver-side CompletionRewardMetric
+# shared with GRPO), so it tracks sample quality, not just the kept subset the loss trains on.
+# NOTE: no --log_completions here -- completion logging is GRPO-only (it lives in GRPOLoop's rollout assembly,
+# which RFT's rejection-sampling fit bypasses), so on RFT it is a dead flag the config validator rejects.
+#
+# Selection (--rft_select):
+#   best_of_n (default) -- keep the single highest-reward completion per prompt (always keeps one, so a
+#                          round never comes up empty; used here);
+#   threshold           -- keep every completion scoring >= --rft_threshold;
+#   top_k               -- keep the --rft_top_k best per prompt.
+# --rft_max_samples_per_prompt caps how many a single prompt contributes. An empty kept set (possible with
+# threshold) skips that round's SFT pass with a warning rather than failing. A round whose kept set is
+# smaller than train_batch_size (per_device_train_batch_size * dp_size) also skips with a warning, so keep
+# --rft_num_samples comfortably above that width.
+#
+# Reward: --orm accuracy is MathAccuracy (backed by math_verify); it reads the dataset's `solution` column as
+# ground truth and the completion's \boxed{} answer. This example uses the real hub dataset
+# AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR (the same one GRPO trains on); the `#2000` suffix takes a 2000-row slice.
+#
+# Placement: RFT is Ray-only with a vLLM sampler -- the SAME requirement as GRPO/PPO. The dev CLI forces
+# use_vllm=true, vllm_mode (colocate by default) and mode=ray for --rlhf_type rft; --nproc_per_node IS
+# required because in Ray mode the driver orchestrates and holds no GPU. vllm_mode=colocate shares the GPUs
+# between sampler and training (CUDA-IPC weight sync); use vllm_mode=disaggregated for separate device groups.
+#
+# Step budget: RFT is bounded by --rft_iterations rounds over the prompt set (each round = one generation
+# pass + one SFT pass over the kept completions), NOT by a toy --max_steps. --gradient_accumulation_steps 1
+# keeps every mini-batch its own optimizer step; raise it for a larger effective batch (over a full round the
+# trailing partial accumulation window is dropped, which is negligible at this scale).
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0/2 busy, so the default below uses 1,3. Adjust
+# CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization to the cards/memory you actually have.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold, not a 2-step demo. For a fast smoke run, shrink everything at once: a
+# smaller policy (Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct), a tiny slice (`#64`), --rft_iterations 1, and cap --max_steps 4.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type rft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR#2000' \
+    --system "You are a helpful math assistant. Solve the problem step by step and put your final answer within \boxed{}." \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --orm accuracy \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --vllm_mode colocate \
+    --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization 0.5 \
+    --rft_num_samples 8 \
+    --rft_select best_of_n \
+    --rft_iterations 3 \
+    --temperature 1.0 \
+    --max_completion_length 2048 \
+    --max_length 3072 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 2 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 1 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --logging_steps 1 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --gradient_checkpointing true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 Reward Model (RM) training with LoRA, on 2 GPUs through Ray.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type rm` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.preference.run_dpo (the offline-preference family: dpo/kto/cpo/orpo/simpo/rm share one entry point).
+#
+# What RM training does: instead of updating a policy, it trains a SCALAR REWARD MODEL -- the reward function
+# that online RL (GRPO/PPO/RFT) later scores rollouts with. The model grows a single-logit sequence-
+# classification head on top of the LM (task_type='seq_cls', num_labels=1, derived automatically from
+# --rlhf_type rm -- you do NOT pass --task_type/--num_labels yourself). Each prompt+completion is pooled to one
+# scalar score. The pairwise RewardLoss then asks for the CHOSEN completion to score higher than the REJECTED
+# one:  loss = -log sigmoid(r_chosen - r_rejected). It reads no reference and no policy logps -- it is a
+# regression on the preference labels, which is why it rides the same chosen/rejected data pipeline as DPO but
+# with a seq_cls head instead of a causal-LM loss.
+#
+# Reference-free, and no ref_model: RM has no reference term. Do NOT pass --ref_model (rejected for rm). There
+# is no --beta either (RM has no KL-to-reference weight); --center_rewards_coefficient is the only RM-specific
+# knob -- an optional L2-style penalty that keeps the scalar rewards centred near zero (off by default; set it,
+# e.g. 0.01, if the reward scale drifts and destabilises the downstream RL).
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: RM is a seq_cls regression, so there is NO DPO reward-margin / accuracy in the head --
+# those come from the paired-policy DPOMetric, which does not apply to a reward head. Judge by the LOSS falling
+# and grad_norm staying finite:
+#   - console head signal:  `step N  loss=...  grad_norm=...`;
+#   - tensorboard scalars:  `loss` and `grad_norm` (bare tags, no `train/` prefix; no rewards/*, no logps/*).
+#     A falling RewardLoss means the head is separating chosen from
+#     rejected; the trained checkpoint is then handed to online RL as a frozen scorer via `--orm <this_ckpt>`.
+#
+# Data / NO periodic eval / placement: --dataset is a chosen/rejected preference set fed INTERLEAVED (the head
+# scores both, the loss compares them); --per_device_train_batch_size counts preference ROWS (pairs). No eval
+# loop, so no --split_dataset_ratio / --eval_steps. mode='ray' forced, no vLLM sampler; --nproc_per_node
+# required. `#10000` takes a 10000-row slice of the real hub dataset.
+# NOTE: --padding_free / --packing are REJECTED for rm (the seq_cls head pools one score per sequence, and a
+# flattened packed row would not split back into one score per sub-sequence) -- do not enable them here.
+#
+# Attention kernel: --attn_impl flash_attention_2 is PINNED because bf16 training on the default SDPA path can
+# select a cuDNN attention kernel whose BACKWARD returns NaN on some torch/cuDNN builds (reproduced on torch
+# 2.11 / cuDNN 9.19: loss goes NaN a few steps in, during warmup, while the lr is still ~0 -- a kernel NaN, not
+# divergence). flash-attn needs the flash-attn package and an Ampere+ GPU; drop the flag only if your stack does
+# not hit the SDPA NaN.
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0/2 busy, so the default below uses 1,3. Global batch is
+# per_device * dp * grad_accum; --nproc_per_node 1 halves dp, so double --gradient_accumulation_steps to 16.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold, not a 2-step demo. For a fast smoke run, shrink everything at once: a
+# smaller policy (Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), a tiny slice (`#512`), and cap `--max_steps 60`.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type rm \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'hjh0119/shareAI-Llama3-DPO-zh-en-emoji#10000' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --gradient_checkpointing true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 Simple Preference Optimization (SimPO) with LoRA, on 2 GPUs through Ray.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift rl` to the v5 dev CLI. `--rlhf_type simpo` dispatches to
+# swift.dev.recipe.preference.run_dpo (the offline-preference family: dpo/kto/cpo/orpo/simpo/rm share one entry point).
+#
+# What SimPO does: a reference-free preference loss whose implicit reward is the LENGTH-NORMALIZED log-prob of
+# a completion -- the average per-token logp, beta * (1/|y|) * sum_t logp(y_t) -- rather than DPO's summed
+# log-ratio against a reference. Normalizing by length removes SimPO's two big pitfalls: no reference model to
+# load or forward, and no reward hacking toward long completions (a long chosen answer cannot win just by
+# accumulating logp). The loss is a logistic on the margin between the chosen and rejected normalized rewards,
+# shifted by a TARGET MARGIN --simpo_gamma:  loss = -log sigmoid( beta*(r_chosen - r_rejected) - gamma ).
+# Requiring the chosen reward to beat the rejected one by at least gamma is what makes SimPO align better with
+# generation (which is also length-normalized) than plain DPO.
+#
+# beta and gamma: --beta scales the normalized reward (SimPO's default is 2.0, notably larger than DPO's 0.1
+# because the reward is a mean, not a sum); --simpo_gamma is the target margin (default 1.0). Tune the two
+# together -- a larger gamma demands a wider separation and can destabilise training if beta is small.
+#
+# Reference-free: no second model, no adapter-disabled forward. Do NOT pass --ref_model (rejected for simpo) or
+# --reference_free (a DPO knob; SimPO has no reference to free). The paper trains SimPO full-parameter; LoRA is
+# used here to keep the example light and single-node smoke-able -- switch to `--tuner full` with a lower
+# learning_rate (e.g. 1e-5) for the full-parameter recipe.
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: SimPO is reference-free, so like CPO/ORPO it has NO rewards/margins and NO
+# rewards/accuracies -- those need reference logps, which SimPO never computes (DPOMetric emits them only when
+# a reference exists). The record holds just logps/chosen|rejected (scalar tags carry NO `train/` prefix):
+#   - console head signal:  `step N  loss=...  grad_norm=...` (no margins/accuracies);
+#   - tensorboard scalars:  `logps/chosen` and `logps/rejected` -- note these are SEQUENCE-SUMMED logps (the
+#                           metric sums per-token logp), NOT the length-normalized reward the loss uses, so
+#                           their absolute scale differs from the reward. The preference signal is the GAP
+#                           logps/chosen - logps/rejected WIDENING (in practice SimPO drives it mostly by
+#                           pushing logps/rejected DOWN), plus `loss` (falls) and `grad_norm`.
+#                           No `rewards/*`, no `logps/ref_*`.
+#
+# Data / NO periodic eval / placement: identical to DPO. --dataset is a chosen/rejected preference set fed
+# INTERLEAVED; --per_device_train_batch_size counts preference ROWS (pairs). No eval loop, so no
+# --split_dataset_ratio / --eval_steps. mode='ray' forced, no vLLM sampler; --nproc_per_node required.
+# `#10000` takes a 10000-row slice. --padding_free true is wired for simpo.
+#
+# Attention kernel: --attn_impl flash_attention_2 is PINNED because bf16 training on the default SDPA path can
+# select a cuDNN attention kernel whose BACKWARD returns NaN on some torch/cuDNN builds (reproduced on torch
+# 2.11 / cuDNN 9.19: loss goes NaN a few steps in, during warmup, while the lr is still ~0 -- a kernel NaN, not
+# divergence). flash-attn needs the flash-attn package and an Ampere+ GPU; drop the flag only if your stack does
+# not hit the SDPA NaN.
+#
+# DEVICES: pick FREE cards -- this box keeps GPU 0/2 busy, so the default below uses 1,3. Global batch is
+# per_device * dp * grad_accum; --nproc_per_node 1 halves dp, so double --gradient_accumulation_steps to 16.
+#
+# This is a real training scaffold, not a 2-step demo. For a fast smoke run, shrink everything at once: a
+# smaller policy (Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), a tiny slice (`#512`), and cap `--max_steps 60`.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,3 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift rl \
+    --rlhf_type simpo \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'hjh0119/shareAI-Llama3-DPO-zh-en-emoji#10000' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --beta 2.0 \
+    --simpo_gamma 1.0 \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \

+# v5 server examples — twinkle server-client multi-LoRA cookbook
+
+v5 has **no `swift server` command**. Serving a *trainable* model over HTTP is done by driving
+`twinkle-server` directly: a `ServerConfig` deploys four Ray Serve applications — a gateway, a model app, a
+sampler app and a processor app — and a thin Python client attaches LoRA adapters, trains them and samples
+them, all over HTTP. This directory is a complete, **e2e-verified** walkthrough of that path: two named
+adapters (`assistant`, `coder`) were trained against one resident base and each sampled back correctly.
+
+## Files
+
+| file | role |
+| --- | --- |
+| `server_config.yaml` | the deployment: gateway + model + sampler + processor apps, `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, `max_loras: 4` |
+| `serve.sh` | `ray start --head` (idempotent) → `twinkle-server check-config` → `twinkle-server launch`; blocks in the foreground |
+| `train.sh` | waits for the gateway, then runs `client.py` from a neutral cwd |
+| `client.py` | the client half: attach several named LoRA adapters → train each → save → sample base + each adapter |
+
+## How to run
+
+Two shells. The server blocks, so it needs its own:
+
+```shell
+# shell 1 — start the server (2 GPUs: one for the model app, one for the vLLM sampler)
+GPUS=1,2 RAY_PORT=6379 bash examples/server/serve.sh
+
+# shell 2 — once serve.sh prints that the gateway is up, drive the client
+bash examples/server/train.sh
+```
+
+Env overrides (all optional, read by `train.sh`/`client.py`): `TWINKLE_SERVER_URL` (default
+`http://localhost:8000`), `TWINKLE_SERVER_TOKEN` (`EMPTY_TOKEN`), `TWINKLE_MODEL_ID`
+(`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`), `TWINKLE_ADAPTER_NAMES` (`assistant,coder`), `TWINKLE_MAX_STEPS` (`6`),
+`TWINKLE_DATA_SLICE` (`200`), `TWINKLE_TEMPLATE` (`Template`).
+
+## Load-bearing details (why the scripts look the way they do)
+
+- **`ray start --head` is mandatory before launch.** `twinkle-server`'s launcher calls
+  `ray.init(address='auto')`, which only *attaches* to an existing cluster and never starts one. `serve.sh`
+  starts a head (reusing one already on `RAY_PORT` if present) and pins `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` for it.
+- **The model app is loaded through swift.** `model_loader: swift.dev.model.loader:build_model_loader` is a
+  `module:callable` factory resolved inside the Ray actor at startup, so **ms-swift must be importable in
+  this env** (from the repo root, `pip install -e .`). `serve.sh` fails fast if it is not.
+- **`max_loras: N` makes it a multi-LoRA host** — several named adapters co-resident on one base. Adding a
+  second name via `add_adapter_to_model(name, ...)` is what exercises the multi-LoRA path.
+- **Do not pass a client-side `save_dir`.** The server owns the checkpoint store
+  (`TWINKLE_DEFAULT_SAVE_DIR`, default `./outputs` under the server cwd); `save()` returns a `twinkle://`
+  URI. A client-side `save_dir` only resolves when client and server share a filesystem *and* the directory
+  already exists on the server, so the managed store is the portable choice.
+- **Resolve the tokenizer through modelscope, not HF hub.** The client decodes sampler token ids with the
+  base tokenizer; `swift.dev.utils.hub.safe_snapshot_download(base_model)` points at the local modelscope
+  snapshot so it works on an offline, modelscope-cached box (`AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('Qwen/...')`
+  would otherwise hit HF hub and fail).
+- **Template namespace is only three classes.** twinkle ships `Template`, `Qwen3_5Template` and
+  `DeepseekV4Template`. Any other family — including `Qwen2.5` here — uses the base `Template`, which
+  renders through the checkpoint's own jinja `chat_template`.
+- **The sampler is vLLM with LoRA enabled** (`enable_lora: true`); `sample(..., adapter_uri=twinkle_path)`
+  selects a trained adapter, `adapter_uri=None` samples the base.
+
+## Deploying a sentence-transformers embedding model
+
+A `SentenceTransformer` is a module pipeline (`Transformer -> Pooling -> Normalize`) that pools *inside* the
+model, so it cannot be built by the AutoModel path and does **not** go through the `task='embedding'`
+processor pooling. The model app serves it through an explicit class instead:
+
+```yaml
+# server_config.yaml, model app args
+model_cls: swift.dev.model.multi_lora_sentence_transformer_model:MultiLoraSentenceTransformerModel
+```
+
+`MultiLoraSentenceTransformerModel` keeps the ST pipeline as the model and installs the multi-tenant LoRA
+slots on its HF backbone, so the usual client flow (`add_adapter_to_model` -> `forward_backward` -> `save`)
+works unchanged against a `sentence_transformers` model id. Two requirements: the `sentence-transformers`
+package must be installed in the model workers (the class imports it lazily and fails with an explicit
+message otherwise), and `max_length` — the per-sample length cap checked before every forward, default
+8192 for that class — must be raised if the model trains on longer sequences. `model_cls` is accepted only
+for `backend: transformers` with `train_mode: lora` and no `hybrid` block.
+
+See the twinkle cookbooks under `twinkle/cookbook/client/{swift_model,server/transformer}/` for the upstream
+shapes this directory adapts.

+# v5 server client: multi-LoRA fine-tuning + sampling against a running twinkle-server.
+#
+# This is the client half of the server/ pair. It attaches SEVERAL named LoRA adapters to
+# one resident base model (the server's model app is configured with max_loras=4), trains
+# each over HTTP, saves it, then samples from the saved adapter to verify end-to-end. The
+# base model is built server-side through swift's family loader (see server_config.yaml).
+#
+# The server must already be running (see serve.sh). Everything here is remote: no model
+# weights are loaded in this process; it only issues HTTP calls via the twinkle client.
+#
+# Run through train.sh, which pins the env vars below and the interpreter.
+
+import os
+
+from peft import LoraConfig
+from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+from twinkle import get_logger, init_twinkle_client
+from twinkle.dataloader import DataLoader
+from twinkle.dataset import Dataset, DatasetMeta
+from twinkle_client.model import MultiLoraTransformersModel
+from twinkle_client.sampler import vLLMSampler
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+# Public model name served by this pair; must match server_config.yaml's supported_models
+# and the model/sampler route tails.
+base_model = os.environ.get('TWINKLE_MODEL_ID', 'Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct')
+base_url = os.environ.get('TWINKLE_SERVER_URL', 'http://localhost:8000')
+api_key = os.environ.get('TWINKLE_SERVER_TOKEN', 'EMPTY_TOKEN')
+
+# Qwen2.5 has no dedicated twinkle template class (only Qwen3.5 / DeepSeek-V4 do), so use
+# the base 'Template', which renders through the checkpoint's own jinja chat_template.
+template_cls = os.environ.get('TWINKLE_TEMPLATE', 'Template')
+
+# Multi-LoRA: several named adapters co-resident on one base model. Comma-separated; the
+# smoke shrinks this to a single name and a couple of steps.
+adapter_names = [n for n in os.environ.get('TWINKLE_ADAPTER_NAMES', 'assistant,coder').split(',') if n]
+max_steps = int(os.environ.get('TWINKLE_MAX_STEPS', '6'))
+data_slice = int(os.environ.get('TWINKLE_DATA_SLICE', '200'))
+
+
+def build_dataloader():
+    # Self-cognition dataset: teaches the model its own name/author. Encoded server-side by
+    # the processor app; the client only ships the recipe.
+    dataset = Dataset(dataset_meta=DatasetMeta('ms://swift/self-cognition', data_slice=range(data_slice)))
+    dataset.set_template(template_cls, model_id=f'ms://{base_model}', max_length=512)
+    dataset.map('SelfCognitionProcessor', init_args={'model_name': 'twinkle模型', 'model_author': 'ModelScope社区'})
+    dataset.encode(batched=True)
+    return DataLoader(dataset=dataset, batch_size=4)
+
+
+def train_adapter(model, dataloader, adapter_name):
+    # Attach a named LoRA adapter to the resident base model. max_loras on the server bounds
+    # how many can coexist; adding a second name here is what makes this multi-LoRA.
+    # Deliberately NO save_dir: the server owns the checkpoint store (TWINKLE_DEFAULT_SAVE_DIR,
+    # default ./outputs under the server cwd) and save() hands back a `twinkle://` URI. Passing
+    # a client-side save_dir only works when client and server share a filesystem and the
+    # directory already exists on the server, so the managed store is the portable choice.
+    lora_config = LoraConfig(target_modules='all-linear')
+    model.add_adapter_to_model(adapter_name, lora_config, gradient_accumulation_steps=2)
+
+    model.set_template(template_cls)
+    model.set_processor('InputProcessor', padding_side='right')
+    model.set_loss('CrossEntropyLoss')
+    model.set_optimizer('Adam', lr=1e-4)
+
+    logger.info(f'[{adapter_name}] train configs: {model.get_train_configs().model_dump()}')
+
+    losses = []
+    global_step = 0
+    for epoch in range(3):
+        for cur_step, batch in enumerate(dataloader, start=1):
+            model.forward_backward(inputs=batch)
+            model.clip_grad_and_step()
+            global_step += 1
+
+            if cur_step % 2 == 0:
+                metric = model.calculate_metric(is_training=True)
+                losses.append(metric.result)
+                logger.info(f'[{adapter_name}] step {cur_step}/{len(dataloader)}, metric: {metric.result}')
+
+            if global_step >= max_steps:
+                break
+        if global_step >= max_steps:
+            break
+
+    resp = model.save(
+        name=f'{adapter_name}-lora',
+        save_optimizer=True,
+        consumed_train_samples=dataloader.get_state()['consumed_train_samples'],
+    )
+    logger.info(f'[{adapter_name}] saved checkpoint: {resp.twinkle_path}')
+    return resp.twinkle_path, losses
+
+
+def sample(adapter_uri=None, tokenizer=None):
+    # Generation runs on the server's vLLM sampler; adapter_uri selects a trained LoRA
+    # (None -> base model). This is the HTTP-only equivalent of a local infer.
+    sampler = vLLMSampler(model_id=base_model)
+    sampler.set_template(template_cls, model_id=base_model)
+
+    trajectory = {
+        'messages': [
+            {'role': 'system', 'content': 'You are a helpful assistant.'},
+            {'role': 'user', 'content': '你是谁？'},
+        ]
+    }
+    responses = sampler.sample(
+        inputs=[trajectory],
+        sampling_params={'max_tokens': 64, 'temperature': 0.0},
+        adapter_uri=adapter_uri,
+    )
+
+    texts = []
+    for response in responses:
+        for seq in response.sequences:
+            text = tokenizer.decode(seq.tokens, skip_special_tokens=True)
+            texts.append(text)
+            logger.info(f'[sample adapter_uri={adapter_uri}] {text}')
+    return texts
+
+
+def main():
+    client = init_twinkle_client(base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key)
+
+    logger.info('Available models:')
+    for item in client.get_server_capabilities().supported_models:
+        logger.info('- ' + item.model_name)
+
+    dataloader = build_dataloader()
+    model = MultiLoraTransformersModel(model_id=f'ms://{base_model}')
+
+    # Decode sampler token ids with the base tokenizer. Resolve the checkpoint through
+    # modelscope (not HF hub) so this works offline on a modelscope-cached box.
+    from swift.dev.utils.hub import safe_snapshot_download

+

+    saved = {}
+    for adapter_name in adapter_names:
+        twinkle_path, losses = train_adapter(model, dataloader, adapter_name)
+        saved[adapter_name] = twinkle_path
+        if losses:
+            logger.info(f'[{adapter_name}] first={losses[0]} last={losses[-1]} (loss is finite and computed per step)')

+    sample(adapter_uri=None, tokenizer=tokenizer)
+    for adapter_name, twinkle_path in saved.items():
+        sample(adapter_uri=twinkle_path, tokenizer=tokenizer)
+
+    logger.info(f'DONE adapters={list(saved)}')
+

+    main()

+# v5 server: start the twinkle-server that hosts a swift-loaded, multi-LoRA trainable
+# model + a vLLM sampler, driven directly (v5 has no `swift server` command).
+#
+# KEY GOTCHA: twinkle-server's launcher does ray.init(address='auto'), which only ATTACHES
+# to an existing Ray cluster and never starts one. So we must `ray start --head` first.
+# This script is idempotent: it reuses a running cluster on RAY_PORT if one is up.
+#
+# What gets deployed is defined entirely by server_config.yaml (server + model + sampler +
+# processor apps). The model app names swift.dev.model.loader:build_model_loader, so
+# ms-swift MUST be importable in this env (its Ray actors inherit it) -- from the ms-swift
+# root run `pip install -e .` first.
+#
+# Blocks in the foreground until Ctrl-C. Run client.py (via train.sh) from another shell.
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")"
+
+export USE_SWIFT_V5=1
+export TWINKLE_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE=1
+
+# 2 GPUs by default: 1 for the model app, 1 for the vLLM sampler (device_group ranks in the
+# YAML). GPU0 is often busy on shared boxes, so default to 1,2. Override with GPUS=.
+GPUS=${GPUS:-1,2}
+RAY_PORT=${RAY_PORT:-6379}
+RAY_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1:${RAY_PORT}
+
+# Fail fast with a clear message if the toolchain or swift loader is missing.
+command -v ray >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'ray not installed; install server deps first' >&2; exit 1; }
+command -v twinkle-server >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'twinkle-server not installed; pip install -e ".[client,server]"' >&2; exit 1; }
+python -c 'import swift.dev.model.loader' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+  || { echo 'ms-swift not importable; from the ms-swift root run: pip install -e .' >&2; exit 1; }
+
+if ! ray status --address="${RAY_ADDRESS}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=${GPUS} ray start \
+    --head \
+    --port="${RAY_PORT}" \
+    --num-gpus=2 \
+    --include-dashboard=false \
+    --disable-usage-stats
+fi
+
+twinkle-server check-config -c server_config.yaml
+exec twinkle-server launch -c server_config.yaml

+# v5 server: twinkle-server config for a swift-loaded, multi-LoRA trainable model.
+#
+# v5 has no `swift server` command. Serving a *trainable* model (attach LoRA adapters,
+# run optimizer steps over HTTP) is done by driving twinkle-server directly; this file
+# is the single source of truth for what gets deployed. serve.sh starts Ray and launches
+# it; client.py (via train.sh) attaches adapters, trains and samples against it.
+#
+# Four applications are deployed on one Ray Serve cluster:
+#   1. server    - the Tinker-compatible gateway clients talk to (route_prefix /api/v1).
+#   2. model     - the trainable base model. `model_loader` names swift's family-loader
+#                  factory, imported *inside the model actor* at startup, so the checkpoint
+#                  is built by swift.dev.model.loader (correct model_cls / remote-code /
+#                  quant knobs) instead of twinkle's generic AutoModel path. max_loras=4
+#                  is what makes this a MULTI-LoRA host: several named adapters can be
+#                  attached and trained concurrently against one resident base model.
+#   3. sampler   - a vLLM engine (enable_lora) for generation, so a just-trained adapter
+#                  can be sampled over HTTP without leaving the server.
+#   4. processor - CPU workers that tokenize/encode datasets.
+#
+# Model choice: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct keeps this smokeable on 2 GPUs (1 for the model app,
+# 1 for the sampler). Swap model_id + supported_models + the two route_prefixes together to
+# serve a larger family (e.g. ms://Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, which also has a dedicated
+# Qwen3_5Template on the client side).
+
+proxy_location: EveryNode
+
+http_options:
+  host: 0.0.0.0
+  port: 8000
+
+telemetry:
+  enabled: false
+  otlp_endpoint: http://localhost:4317
+
+# ServerState (sessions, models, futures) persists to a local file so training runs and
+# checkpoints survive across client reconnects within the same server lifetime.
+persistence:
+  mode: file
+  file_path: /tmp/twinkle_server_examples_state.json
+
+applications:
+
+  # 1. Gateway / API server. supported_models is the public name clients address; it must
+  #    match the model app's route_prefix tail and the sampler's model_id.
+  - name: server
+    route_prefix: /api/v1
+    import_path: server
+    args:
+      server_config:
+        per_token_model_limit: 3
+      supported_models:
+        - Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
+    deployments:
+      - name: TinkerCompatServer
+        max_ongoing_requests: 50
+        autoscaling_config:
+          min_replicas: 1
+          max_replicas: 1
+          target_ongoing_requests: 128
+        ray_actor_options:
+          num_cpus: 0.1
+          runtime_env:
+            env_vars:
+              TWINKLE_FAIL_FAST: "0"
+
+  # 2. Trainable model, built through swift's family loader. Single GPU (dp_size 1) is
+  #    enough for a 0.5B checkpoint; raise device_group.ranks + device_mesh.fsdp_size
+  #    together to shard a larger model.
+  - name: models-Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
+    route_prefix: /api/v1/model/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
+    import_path: model
+    args:
+      backend: transformers
+      model_id: "ms://Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct"
+      # The swift family-loader factory: `module:callable`, imported inside the actor and
+      # called with model_id. Remove this line to fall back to twinkle's generic AutoModel
+      # path (which loses swift's per-family config/quant corrections).
+      model_loader: swift.dev.model.loader:build_model_loader
+      # `model_cls: module:attr` names the class the model app serves, resolved inside the actor
+      # and layered with twinkle's tinker/twinkle compat methods; unset, it is twinkle's
+      # multi-LoRA transformers wrapper. A sentence-transformers embedding model needs
+      #   model_cls: swift.dev.model.multi_lora_sentence_transformer_model:MultiLoraSentenceTransformerModel
+      # because its pipeline (Transformer -> Pooling -> Normalize) pools inside the model and cannot
+      # be built by the AutoModel path. That deployment also needs the `sentence-transformers`
+      # package in the model workers; `max_length` caps each sample before a forward (default 8192
+      # for that class), so raise it for longer sequences.
+      # Only allowed for backend: transformers with train_mode: lora and no `hybrid` block.
+      max_loras: 4
+      max_length: 2048
+      nproc_per_node: 1
+      device_group:
+        name: model
+        ranks: 1
+        device_type: cuda
+      device_mesh:
+        device_type: cuda
+        dp_size: 1
+      queue_config:
+        rps_limit: 100
+        tps_limit: 100000
+      adapter_config:
+        adapter_timeout: 30
+    deployments:
+      - name: ModelManagement
+        autoscaling_config:
+          min_replicas: 1
+          max_replicas: 1
+          target_ongoing_requests: 16
+        ray_actor_options:
+          num_cpus: 0.1
+          runtime_env:
+            env_vars:
+              TWINKLE_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE: "1"
+              TWINKLE_FAIL_FAST: "0"
+
+  # 3. Sampler service - vLLM engine for generation. enable_lora lets a trained adapter be
+  #    sampled by URI (see client.py's sampler.sample(adapter_uri=...)).
+  - name: sampler-Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
+    route_prefix: /api/v1/sampler/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
+    import_path: sampler
+    args:
+      model_id: "ms://Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct"
+      nproc_per_node: 1
+      sampler_type: vllm
+      engine_args:
+        max_model_len: 2048
+        gpu_memory_utilization: 0.5
+        enable_lora: true
+        enforce_eager: true
+        logprobs_mode: processed_logprobs
+      device_group:
+        name: sampler
+        ranks: 1
+        device_type: cuda
+      device_mesh:
+        device_type: cuda
+        dp_size: 1
+      queue_config:
+        rps_limit: 100
+        tps_limit: 100000
+    deployments:
+      - name: SamplerManagement
+        autoscaling_config:
+          min_replicas: 1
+          max_replicas: 1
+          target_ongoing_requests: 16
+        ray_actor_options:
+          num_cpus: 0.1
+          runtime_env:
+            env_vars:
+              TWINKLE_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE: "1"
+              TWINKLE_FAIL_FAST: "0"
+
+  # 4. Processor service - tokenizes/encodes datasets on CPU workers.
+  - name: processor
+    route_prefix: /api/v1/processor
+    import_path: processor
+    args:
+      ncpu_proc_per_node: 2
+      device_group:
+        name: model
+        ranks: 2
+        device_type: CPU
+      device_mesh:
+        device_type: CPU
+        dp_size: 2
+    deployments:
+      - name: ProcessorManagement
+        autoscaling_config:
+          min_replicas: 1
+          max_replicas: 1
+          target_ongoing_requests: 128
+        ray_actor_options:
+          num_cpus: 0.1
+          runtime_env:
+            env_vars:
+              TWINKLE_FAIL_FAST: "0"

+# v5 server: drive client.py to attach + train multi-LoRA adapters and sample them, all
+# over HTTP against the twinkle-server started by serve.sh.
+#
+# Run serve.sh first (in another shell) and wait until it prints that the gateway is up.
+# This script only issues client calls; it loads no model weights locally.
+#
+# Env overrides (all optional):
+#   TWINKLE_SERVER_URL   gateway root          (default http://localhost:8000)
+#   TWINKLE_SERVER_TOKEN api key               (default EMPTY_TOKEN)
+#   TWINKLE_MODEL_ID     public model name     (default Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct)
+#   TWINKLE_ADAPTER_NAMES comma-separated LoRA names to train (default assistant,coder)
+#   TWINKLE_MAX_STEPS    optimizer steps per adapter (default 6)
+#   TWINKLE_DATA_SLICE   self-cognition rows   (default 200)
+set -euo pipefail
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}"
+
+export USE_SWIFT_V5=1
+export TWINKLE_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE=1
+
+# The client imports twinkle/twinkle_client only; run from a neutral cwd so the repo's
+# top-level `twinkle/` package directory cannot shadow the installed one.
+export TWINKLE_SERVER_URL=${TWINKLE_SERVER_URL:-http://localhost:8000}
+export TWINKLE_SERVER_TOKEN=${TWINKLE_SERVER_TOKEN:-EMPTY_TOKEN}
+export TWINKLE_MODEL_ID=${TWINKLE_MODEL_ID:-Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct}
+
+# Wait for the gateway to accept connections before firing client calls.
+python - <<'PY'
+import os, time, urllib.request
+url = os.environ['TWINKLE_SERVER_URL'].rstrip('/')
+for _ in range(120):
+    try:
+        urllib.request.urlopen(url + '/api/v1/models', timeout=5)
+        print('gateway ready:', url)
+        break
+    except Exception:
+        time.sleep(5)
+else:
+    raise SystemExit('gateway not ready at ' + url)
+PY
+
+cd /tmp
+python "${SCRIPT_DIR}/client.py"

+# v5 AdaLoRA (--tuner adalora): LoRA that re-allocates rank across modules during training.
+#
+# Plain LoRA gives every target module the same fixed rank r. AdaLoRA (adaptive LoRA) instead starts each
+# module at a larger `--adalora_init_r` and prunes toward an average `--adalora_target_r` over the course of
+# training, spending rank where it matters most (by an importance/sensitivity score) and trimming it where it
+# does not. Same memory budget at convergence as fixed-rank LoRA of r=target_r, but the allocation is learned
+# rather than uniform.
+#
+# `--tuner adalora` selects it (v5 tuners are exactly lora/adalora/trainable_tokens/full -- there is no
+# qlora/dora/rslora; those are LoRA flags, not tuners). The adalora_* knobs (swift/dev/config/adapter_config.py)
+# control the schedule: init_r -> target_r is the pruning range, tinit/tfinal/deltaT set when and how often the
+# rank budget is updated, beta1/beta2 smooth the importance estimate, orth_reg_weight penalises redundant
+# singular directions. target_modules works the same as LoRA ('all-linear' covers every linear layer).
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#600' \
+    --tuner adalora \
+    --adalora_init_r 12 \
+    --adalora_target_r 8 \
+    --adalora_deltaT 1 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --num_train_epochs 3 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --split_dataset_ratio 0.01 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 agentic SFT: fine-tune tool use on an agent dataset, weighted by --loss_scale.
+#
+# There is NO --agent_template flag in v5 (it was removed). The agent surface is expressed two ways:
+#   - the chat TEMPLATE renders the conversation into the model's own format; it comes from the model's
+#     registered template, so you do not select it separately here;
+#   - --loss_scale picks the weighting strategy that knows the agent transcript's markers. It scores the
+#     spans the model must LEARN TO EMIT as the target while down-weighting the spans it only reads.
+#
+# ms_agent is the canonical ReAct-format agent set: the system prompt lists the callable APIs and the
+# Thought/Action/Action Input/Observation scaffolding, and each assistant turn carries those markers
+# inline (there is no separate tool_call role). --loss_scale react (swift/loss_scale/config/react.json)
+# up-weights `Action:` / `Action Input:` (2.0) as the learning target, zeroes the `Observation:` CONTENT
+# (the tool result the model reads but never emits), and leaves `Thought:` / `Final Answer:` at 1.0.
+# Other agent strategies: hermes / qwen / agentflan / alpha_umi (swift/loss_scale/mapping.py); strategies

+# full tool output), so max_length is 4096 and --truncation_strategy delete drops the rare longer row

+# v5 base -> chat: turn a BASE (pretrained, non-instruct) model into a chat model with full-parameter SFT.
+#
+# Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B is the raw pretrained base -- it continues text but does not follow the turn-taking chat
+# format. This example fine-tunes it on conversational data WITH a chat template applied, so it learns the
+# system/user/assistant structure and to emit an end-of-turn. The mechanics that make it "base to chat":
+#   --model points at the BASE checkpoint (not -Instruct),
+#   --use_chat_template true wraps every row in the model family's chat template (the base repo ships no
+#     chat config, so this is what imposes the conversational format),
+#   --tuner full updates all weights -- a base model usually needs full-parameter SFT (not a small adapter) to
+#     actually acquire instruction-following, since there is no prior chat behaviour to nudge.
+#
+# DATASET: self-cognition is used here only because it is small and cached, so the smoke is fast; it teaches
+# the chat FORMAT plus a narrow identity. For a real base->chat conversion point --dataset at a broad
+# instruction corpus (e.g. an alpaca-style set) so the model learns general following, not one persona.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --use_chat_template true \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#600' \
+    --tuner full \
+    --num_train_epochs 3 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-5 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --split_dataset_ratio 0.01 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 cached_dataset: tokenize a dataset ONCE, save it to disk, then train straight from the cache.
+#
+# Two stages. Stage 1 runs `swift export --to_cached_dataset`, which drives the load + encode chain a
+# single time and save_to_disk's the result under <output_dir>/train (plus /val when
+# --split_dataset_ratio > 0). It is a CPU job (only the tokenizer is loaded -- no model, no distributed
+# init). Stage 2 points `--cached_dataset <output_dir>/train` at that SUBDIRECTORY and skips encoding
+# entirely: dev's forward sees the rows already carry input_ids and does not re-encode them.
+#
+# THE CACHE IS TOKENIZER-BOUND: stage 2 must use the SAME --model (tokenizer) as stage 1, or the cached
+# token ids mean something different. --template_mode on the export selects the objective ('train' here;
+# 'rlhf' / 'kto' encode chosen/rejected shapes instead) and must match the training run that reads it.
+# cached_dataset is map-style, so it cannot be combined with --streaming.
+#
+# The write half of this feature also lives at examples/export/cached_dataset; this script keeps both
+# halves together so the consume side is runnable end to end on a small, cached model.
+
+# --- stage 1: build the cache ---------------------------------------------------------------------
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift export \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#2000' \
+    --split_dataset_ratio 0.02 \
+    --to_cached_dataset true \
+    --template_mode train \
+    --dataset_num_proc 4 \
+    --output_dir ./self_cognition_cached
+
+# --- stage 2: train from the cache ----------------------------------------------------------------
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --cached_dataset ./self_cognition_cached/train \
+    --cached_val_dataset ./self_cognition_cached/val \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --per_device_eval_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --eval_strategy steps \
+    --eval_steps 20 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 custom dataset, declared as DATA (no Python): --custom_dataset_info + a dataset_info JSON.
+#
+# Most custom datasets differ from a built-in one only in *what* they are -- a local file / a hub id,
+# which subsets exist, and which raw column means query vs response -- not in *how* they are read. Those
+# need no code: declare them in a JSON file (the same shape as dev's built-in dataset_info.json) and pass
+# it to --custom_dataset_info. dev synthesises a DatasetLoader per entry (register_dataset_info), so a

+# Custom model family + custom chat template, registered as a plugin and loaded with --external_plugins.
+#
+# Importing this file (via --external_plugins, before anything is built) runs registration side effects.
+# A custom `--model_type` is looked up in TWO independent registries during one SFT run, so a custom
+# family registers in both -- they are not derived from each other:
+#
+#   1. dev's model-loader registry (swift.dev.model.loader). build_model resolves `--model_type`
+#      through it to pick the transformers family loader; an UNregistered model_type there is treated as
+#      an external plugin path, so the family must be a @register_model ModelLoader subclass. It declares
+#      the checkpoints it covers (`models`), the template it speaks (`template`) and the transformers
+#      class to build (`model_cls`, which has no safe default).
+#   2. the legacy model registry (swift.model). build_template -> load_model_processor delegates to
+#      swift.model.get_model_processor, which validates `--model_type` against the legacy MODEL_MAPPING;
+#      a custom family is a register_model(ModelMeta(...)) entry listing the same ids and template.
+#
+# The chat TEMPLATE is registered once, into swift.template's registry (dev resolves templates through
+# the legacy get_template). TemplateMeta requires template_type / prefix / prompt / chat_sep; {{SYSTEM}}
+# / {{QUERY}} are the placeholders dev fills. Select it with --template custom_im.
+#
+# Here the family just re-points at a stock Qwen2.5 checkpoint with our own template, which is enough to
+# exercise both registries end to end; a real custom family lists its own `models`, and overrides the
+# loader's build_config / build_processor / build_model hooks when the plain AutoModel path is not enough.
+from swift.dev.model.loader import ModelLoader, register_model
+from swift.model import Model, ModelGroup, ModelMeta
+from swift.model import register_model as register_legacy_model
+from swift.template import TemplateMeta, register_template
+
+
+@register_model(exist_ok=True)
+class CustomIMLoader(ModelLoader):
+    model_type = 'custom_im'
+    model_cls = 'transformers:AutoModelForCausalLM'
+    template = 'custom_im'
+    models = ['Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct']
+
+
+register_legacy_model(
+    ModelMeta(
+        model_type='custom_im',
+        model_groups=[ModelGroup([
+            Model('Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct', 'Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct'),
+        ])],
+        template='custom_im',
+        architectures=['Qwen2ForCausalLM'],
+    ),
+    exist_ok=True)
+
+register_template(
+    TemplateMeta(
+        template_type='custom_im',
+        prefix=['<|im_start|>system\n{{SYSTEM}}<|im_end|>\n'],
+        prompt=['<|im_start|>user\n{{QUERY}}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n'],
+        chat_sep=['<|im_end|>\n'],
+        default_system='You are a helpful assistant.'))

+# v5 early stopping (--early_stop_interval N): stop as soon as the eval metric stalls, instead of running all epochs.
+#
+# SFT on a small set keeps improving for a while, then the eval loss flattens (or turns up = overfitting). Early
+# stopping watches the eval metric every evaluation and halts training once it has failed to improve for
+# `--early_stop_interval` consecutive evaluations (dev's EarlyStopCallback; the value is a count of EVALS, i.e.
+# HF "patience"). The callback is appended automatically only when --early_stop_interval is set.
+#
+# THE FLAGS MUST AGREE, or it silently does nothing / errors at the end:
+#   --eval_strategy steps + --eval_steps 20      run an eval every 20 optimizer steps (the stall is counted in
+#                                                evals, so eval cadence sets the granularity);
+#   --metric_for_best_model eval_loss            the watched key. NOTE it is the literal eval-metric name: dev
+#                                                looks it up verbatim in the eval result (train_loop._track_best)
+#                                                and eval emits 'eval_loss', so 'loss' would NOT match and
+#                                                best-model tracking is skipped with a warning;
+#   --greater_is_better false                    loss improves by going DOWN;
+#   --load_best_model_at_end true                reload the best checkpoint when training ends;
+#   --save_steps 20 == --eval_steps               the best step must be checkpointed to be reloaded, and
+#   --save_total_limit 10 (NOT 2)                 must not have been pruned -- an aggressive limit makes
+#                                                load_best_model_at_end raise FileNotFoundError.
+# --split_dataset_ratio carves the val set the eval loss is computed on. num_train_epochs is set high on
+# purpose: early stopping is expected to cut the run well short of it.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#600' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --num_train_epochs 10 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --per_device_eval_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --eval_strategy steps \
+    --eval_steps 20 \
+    --metric_for_best_model eval_loss \
+    --greater_is_better false \
+    --load_best_model_at_end true \

+# v5 embedding training (task_type=embedding) with the InfoNCE objective on a single GPU.
+#
+# `--task_type embedding` dispatches to run_embedding, which pools the last token into a sentence
+# vector; `--loss infonce` selects the contrastive InfoNCE objective (others: cosine_similarity,
+# contrastive, online_contrastive). Each row carries an anchor `messages` plus `positive_messages` and
+# `negative_messages` -- each of those a LIST OF conversations (one per candidate), not a single one.
+# Embedding has no classification head, so LoRA trains cleanly here.
+#
+# HOW TO READ THIS RUN: the InfoNCE loss alone is an opaque scalar, so run_embedding registers twinkle's
+# EmbeddingMetric -- watch the tensorboard `pos_sim` (anchor-to-positive cosine, should RISE) and `neg_sim`
+# (anchor vs in-batch negatives, should stay flat or FALL); a widening pos_sim - neg_sim gap is the embedding
+# model converging. (`accuracy` is auto-registered but is a no-op here -- embeddings carry no class label.)
+#
+# Dataset: `stsb:positive#2000` is a REAL hub set -- the STS-B sentence-similarity pairs, filtered to the
+# genuinely-similar ones (score >= 0.75) the `positive` subset keeps, so each anchor's partner is a TRUE
+# positive. InfoNCE needs no explicit negatives: it contrasts each anchor against the OTHER rows of the batch
+# (in-batch negatives, all-gathered across ranks). Reference it by the REGISTERED name (`stsb:positive`), not
+# the raw `sentence-transformers/stsb` id, so the InfoNCE preprocessor emits `positive_messages`. The 0.5B LM
+# keeps the example light; for a production embedder use a dedicated checkpoint (e.g. Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B).
+#
+# ATTENTION BACKEND IS LOAD-BEARING -- keep `--attn_impl flash_attention_2`. Left unset, attn_impl=None and
+# transformers picks SDPA, which on a current torch/cuDNN build resolves to the cuDNN attention kernel whose
+# bf16 BACKWARD returns NaN: the run trains cleanly for ~15 steps, then grad_norm goes non-finite (it drops out
+# of the log line entirely -- the tracker's coercion discards non-finite scalars) and every subsequent step is
+# loss=nan. Verified: default SDPA/cuDNN -> nan by step ~18; flash_attention_2 -> 40+ steps clean, loss 1.17->0.02.
+# `--attn_impl eager` also avoids the cuDNN kernel if flash-attn is unavailable. NOTE the token: the dev
+# (transformers) backend passes attn_impl straight through to HF, so it must be `flash_attention_2`, NOT legacy
+# swift's `flash_attn` (which HF rejects). The reference qwen3_emb.sh pins flash attention for the same reason.
+#
+# BATCH SIZE IS THE NEGATIVE COUNT. `--per_device_train_batch_size 8` gives each anchor 7 in-batch negatives
+# (the reference qwen3_emb.sh on this same dataset uses 8); a batch of 2 leaves only ONE negative per anchor,
+# which makes the contrastive task trivially separable and starves the objective. Keep the batch >= 8 and
+# --learning_rate at 5e-5 (both the reference values).
+# OFFLINE fallback (no hub): the bundled `examples/train/data/embedding.jsonl`.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type embedding \
+    --loss infonce \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'stsb:positive#2000' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --num_train_epochs 3 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 8 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 1 \
+    --learning_rate 5e-5 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 512 \
+    --logging_steps 1 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 FlashAttention-3 (--attn_impl flash_attention_3).  *** REFERENCE-ONLY -- see the hardware note below. ***
+#
+# FA3 is the Hopper-generation rewrite of flash-attention: it exploits the H100/H800 tensor-memory + warp
+# specialisation (and FP8 attention) for a large throughput jump over FA2 on long sequences. In v5 the attention
+# backend is one flag -- `--attn_impl` -- passed straight through to the transformers model, so switching
+# FA2 -> FA3 is only this token. Valid values on the dev (transformers) backend are the HF ones
+# (`eager` / `sdpa` / `flash_attention_2` / `flash_attention_3`); the legacy spelling `flash_attn` is rejected.
+# For a multimodal model the vision tower has its own `--vit_attn_impl`.
+#
+# WHY THIS IS REFERENCE-ONLY (cannot be smoked on the authoring box): FA3 requires (a) a Hopper GPU -- compute

+# kernel; asking for flash_attention_3 there fails at kernel dispatch, not in swift. Everything else in this
+# script is the ordinary lora SFT that IS smoke-validated (train/lora/train.sh); only the attn token differs.

+# v5 text SFT (causal_lm) with LoRA on a single GPU.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift sft` to the v5 dev CLI (swift.dev.cli.sft), which parses argv straight
+# into the dev Config dataclasses -- there is no legacy SftArguments bridge. `--tuner lora` selects the
+# LoRA adapter path (TunerConfig); drop it (or set `--tuner full`) for full-parameter training.
+# The 0.5B model keeps the example light; swap in Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct for a real run.
+#
+# DATASET CHOICE = VISIBLE CONVERGENCE. This uses `swift/self-cognition`, not alpaca-gpt4: an
+# already-instruct Qwen2.5-0.5B has almost no headroom on alpaca, so its loss plateaus at ~1.6 (measured
+# 1.78 -> 1.58 over 3 epochs) and the run looks like it is not learning. self-cognition is new knowledge
+# the model must actually fit, so the loss falls clearly (measured 2.6 -> 0.28) -- a real SFT curve. Keep
+# --num_train_epochs 3 so the descent completes; swap the dataset back to alpaca for a general-SFT run
+# whose curve is genuinely flatter.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \

+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#600' \

+    --num_train_epochs 3 \

+# v5 Megatron-backend MoE SFT: expert parallelism (ep4) on 4 GPUs, Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, top-8, 3B active).
+#
+# Same launcher as the dense tp_pp example -- `swift sft --backend megatron`, NPROC_PER_NODE relaunches under
+# torch.distributed.run -- the only thing that changes is the parallel axis. tp_pp splits every weight matrix
+# (tensor parallel) and the layer stack (pipeline parallel); an MoE instead splits the EXPERTS: with
+# --expert_model_parallel_size 4 the 128 experts are sharded 4-way (32 per rank) and each token is routed to
+# its top-8 experts across ranks via an all-to-all (--moe_token_dispatcher_type alltoall). The attention/dense
+# part is replicated, so ep (not tp) is the axis that makes a sparse model fit. The world size must equal
+# tp x pp x ep x dp; here it is ep4 x dp1 = 4 = NPROC_PER_NODE.
+#
+# MoE-only knobs (all MegatronConfig/MoEConfig, read only on this backend): --moe_grouped_gemm runs the 32
+# local experts as one grouped GEMM instead of a loop; --moe_permute_fusion folds the token-permute into the
+# dispatch kernel; --moe_aux_loss_coeff weights the load-balancing loss that keeps the router from collapsing
+# onto a few experts. Qwen3-30B-A3B has NO shared expert (num_shared_experts is unset), so
+# --moe_shared_expert_overlap is deliberately omitted -- it would be a dead flag on this model.
+#
+# Megatron batch knobs, not per_device_train_batch_size: --micro_batch_size is per rank per step, and
+# --global_batch_size is the whole-optimizer-step batch across all ranks (must be a multiple of
+# micro_batch_size x dp). Megatron derives gradient accumulation from the two.
+#
+# DATASET CHOICE = VISIBLE CONVERGENCE. `swift/self-cognition` is new knowledge the model must fit, so the
+# loss falls clearly; an instruct model on alpaca plateaus and looks flat. Keep --num_train_epochs 3.
+#
+# SCALING UP. Bigger sparse models add pipeline parallel and more expert parallel across more nodes, e.g.
+# Qwen3-235B-A22B or DeepSeek-V3: raise --expert_model_parallel_size (and --pipeline_model_parallel_size),
+# add NNODES/NODE_RANK/MASTER_ADDR exactly as in examples/train/multi-node/torchrun, and switch --tuner lora
+# to full-parameter training with --use_distributed_optimizer. When the optimizer state no longer fits,
+# offload it to CPU with --optimizer_cpu_offload true --optimizer_offload_fraction 1. Resources: the ep4 x
+# 4-GPU layout here fits Qwen3-30B-A3B with LoRA + full recompute on ~40GB-class GPUs; a 235B/671B MoE needs
+# a multi-node cluster.
+PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF='expandable_segments:True' \
+NPROC_PER_NODE=4 \
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --backend megatron \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#600' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --expert_model_parallel_size 4 \
+    --moe_token_dispatcher_type alltoall \
+    --moe_grouped_gemm true \
+    --moe_permute_fusion true \
+    --moe_aux_loss_coeff 1e-3 \
+    --micro_batch_size 1 \
+    --global_batch_size 8 \
+    --recompute_granularity full \
+    --recompute_method uniform \
+    --recompute_num_layers 1 \
+    --finetune true \
+    --cross_entropy_loss_fusion true \
+    --attention_backend flash \
+    --lr 1e-4 \
+    --min_lr 1e-5 \
+    --lr_warmup_fraction 0.05 \
+    --num_train_epochs 3 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_safetensors true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 Megatron-backend SFT with tensor parallelism (tp2) on 2 GPUs.
+#
+# v5 has NO separate `megatron` command: twinkle unifies both stacks, so the Megatron path is selected by
+# `--backend megatron` on `swift sft`. NPROC_PER_NODE relaunches under torch.distributed.run, and the
+# Megatron mesh is built from the parallel-size flags. Megatron uses its own batch knobs
+# (--micro_batch_size / --global_batch_size) rather than per_device_train_batch_size, and
+# --sequence_parallel here is Megatron's TP-region sequence parallelism (distinct from the transformers
+# Ulysses --sequence_parallel_size). The 0.5B model keeps the example light and locally smoke-testable.
+#
+# DATASET CHOICE = VISIBLE CONVERGENCE. `swift/self-cognition` (not alpaca-gpt4): an already-instruct
+# Qwen2.5-0.5B plateaus at ~1.6 loss on alpaca (no headroom), so the run looks flat; self-cognition is new
+# knowledge it must fit, so the loss falls clearly (measured 2.6 -> 0.28 on the transformers path). Keep
+# --num_train_epochs 3 so the descent completes.
+#
+# PIPELINE PARALLEL: add `--pipeline_model_parallel_size 2` (and NPROC_PER_NODE=4 / CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3
+# for tp2 x pp2), or state the whole layout at once with `--parallel_spec tp2pp2`. Megatron supports only
+# causal_lm SFT -- seq_cls/embedding/reranker stay on the transformers backend (drop --backend).
+#
+# SCALING UP. For a larger dense model (7B/32B/72B) raise --tensor_model_parallel_size, add
+# --pipeline_model_parallel_size across more GPUs/nodes (NNODES/NODE_RANK/MASTER_ADDR exactly as in
+# examples/train/multi-node/torchrun), and switch --tuner lora to full-parameter training with
+# --use_distributed_optimizer. When the optimizer state no longer fits, offload it to CPU with
+# --optimizer_cpu_offload true --optimizer_offload_fraction 1 (slower steps, far less GPU memory).
+PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF='expandable_segments:True' \
+NPROC_PER_NODE=2 \
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --backend megatron \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#600' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --tensor_model_parallel_size 2 \
+    --sequence_parallel true \
+    --micro_batch_size 1 \
+    --global_batch_size 8 \
+    --recompute_granularity full \
+    --recompute_method uniform \
+    --recompute_num_layers 1 \
+    --finetune true \
+    --cross_entropy_loss_fusion true \
+    --lr 1e-4 \
+    --min_lr 1e-5 \
+    --lr_warmup_fraction 0.05 \
+    --num_train_epochs 3 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_safetensors true \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 SFT launched through Ray on the transformers backend (mode=ray, 2 data-parallel workers).
+#
+# Unlike the torchrun path, there is NO NPROC_PER_NODE and no torch.distributed.run: `--mode ray` makes
+# initialize_twinkle build a 'model' DeviceGroup that 2 Ray workers join, while the driver process only
+# orchestrates (it holds no GPU itself, so `--nproc_per_node` must be given explicitly). Batch semantics
+# match torchrun: per_device_train_batch_size is PER DP RANK. The driver's DataLoader builds the GLOBAL
+# batch (per_device x dp = 2 x 2 = 4 here) and forward_backward(dispatch='slice_dp') scatters it to
+# per_device rows on each worker, so the global batch is per_device x dp x gradient_accumulation_steps --
+# the same as under torchrun. The transformers backend has no TP/PP weight sharding, so the Ray mesh is
+# pure data parallelism.
+#
+# --attn_impl flash_attention_2 is pinned: on the validation box (torch 2.11 + cuDNN 9.19) the default
+# SDPA path picks a cuDNN attention kernel whose bf16 backward returns NaN on longer rows -- clean
+# through ~step 25, then grad_norm goes non-finite and loss becomes nan. FA2 avoids it (and is standard
+# for multi-GPU long-sequence training); `--attn_impl eager` is the fallback where flash-attn is absent.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --dataset 'AI-ModelScope/alpaca-gpt4-data-zh#500' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --mode ray \
+    --nproc_per_node 2 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 2 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 SFT under torchrun: data parallel (dp2), with the sequence-parallel (Ulysses) variant noted.
+#
+# Setting NPROC_PER_NODE makes swift/cli/main.py relaunch the dev CLI under `torch.distributed.run`
+# (mode='local'): each of the 2 ranks runs the same recipe over its shard, and the transformers backend
+# builds a pure data-parallel mesh from the world size. `--parallel_spec dp2` states that layout
+# explicitly (it is the default here). per_device_train_batch_size must be >= the dp size, since the
+# driver batch is scattered across the dp ranks.
+#
+# SEQUENCE PARALLEL (Ulysses) instead splits each sequence along the token dim inside attention: add
+# `--sequence_parallel_size 2` (TemplateConfig). A hybrid dp x sp layout uses parallel_spec, e.g.
+# `--parallel_spec dp2sp2` under NPROC_PER_NODE=4. SP is a pure re-partition, so the loss equals the
+# single-process loss on the same global batch.
+#
+# MEMORY SHARDING is a flag on this same command, not a separate launch form. Plain dp2 (above) keeps a
+# full replica per rank; to shard optimizer state / gradients / parameters across the ranks add
+# `--deepspeed zero2` (optim+grads) or `--deepspeed zero3` (params too), or `--fsdp` / `--fsdp fsdp2`
+# with `--fsdp_config` for torch FSDP. DDP is the default (no flag); `device_map` model-parallel is not
+# a training path here. The launcher and every other flag are unchanged.
+#
+# --attn_impl flash_attention_2 is pinned on purpose. On the box these examples were validated on
+# (torch 2.11 + cuDNN 9.19) the default SDPA path selects a cuDNN attention kernel whose bf16 BACKWARD
+# returns NaN on the longer alpaca rows: training is clean through ~step 25, then grad_norm goes
+# non-finite (it drops out of the log, the tracker discards non-finite scalars) and loss becomes nan.
+# FA2 avoids that kernel and is the usual choice for multi-GPU long-sequence training anyway. An
+# environment without flash-attn can use `--attn_impl eager`, which also sidesteps cuDNN.
+NPROC_PER_NODE=2 \
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --dataset 'AI-ModelScope/alpaca-gpt4-data-zh#500' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --parallel_spec dp2 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
