+# v5 multi-node SFT through Ray: ONE driver command over a pre-started, cluster-wide Ray pool.
+#
+# Why Ray differs from the torchrun path. There is no per-node command and no NNODES / NODE_RANK /
+# MASTER_ADDR: you first bring up a Ray cluster spanning the nodes, then run a single `swift sft
+# --mode ray` on any node that can reach it. `--mode ray` makes initialize_twinkle build a 'model'
+# DeviceGroup that the Ray workers join, while the driver process only orchestrates and holds NO GPU.
+# Ray schedules those workers onto GPUs across the whole cluster, so crossing a node boundary is
+# transparent to swift -- the only thing that changes versus single-node Ray is how the cluster was
+# started. DO NOT export NPROC_PER_NODE here: that variable makes swift/cli/main.py relaunch under
+# torchrun, which is the other (mutually exclusive) launch path. The Ray worker count is the CLI flag
+# `--nproc_per_node` instead.
+#
+# 1) start the cluster (once per node). Head node, then every worker node points at it:
+#      head:    ray start --head --port=6379 --num-gpus=2
+#      worker:  ray start --address=<head_ip>:6379 --num-gpus=2
+# 2) run the driver on the head (RAY_ADDRESS finds the cluster; --nproc_per_node is the TOTAL rank
+#    count across ALL nodes, i.e. nodes x gpus-per-node = 2 x 2 = 4 here):
+#      RAY_ADDRESS=<head_ip>:6379 bash train.sh
+#
+# SINGLE-BOX simulation (how this was smoke-validated): one node stands in for the cluster, so the
+# multi-worker Ray placement is exercised for real while the workers happen to share one machine.
+#   ray start --head --num-gpus=4     # or let ray.init() auto-start a local cluster
+#   RAY_ADDRESS=auto NPROC_TOTAL=4 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,2,3,4 bash train.sh
+# Truly spanning physical machines only needs the workers' `ray start --address` to dial the same head.
+#
+# Batch semantics under Ray MATCH torchrun: per_device_train_batch_size is PER DP RANK, not a global
+# batch. The driver's DataLoader builds the GLOBAL batch (per_device x dp = 8 x 4 = 32 here, sized by
+# _twinkle_loader_layout) and forward_backward(dispatch='slice_dp') scatters it back to per_device rows
+# on each rank, so the global batch is per_device x dp x gradient_accumulation_steps exactly as under
+# torchrun. The transformers backend has no TP/PP sharding, so the Ray mesh is pure data parallelism.
+# (With 500 rows / global batch 32 / ga 2, one epoch is ~7 optimizer steps -- a short run by design.)
+#
+# --attn_impl flash_attention_2 is pinned: on the validation box (torch 2.11 + cuDNN 9.19) the default
+# SDPA path picks a cuDNN attention kernel whose bf16 backward returns NaN on longer rows -- clean
+# through ~step 25, then grad_norm goes non-finite and loss becomes nan. FA2 avoids it (and is standard
+# for multi-node long-sequence training); `--attn_impl eager` is the fallback where flash-attn is absent.
+RAY_ADDRESS=${RAY_ADDRESS:-auto} \
+NPROC_TOTAL=${NPROC_TOTAL:-4} \
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-0,1,2,3} \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --dataset 'AI-ModelScope/alpaca-gpt4-data-zh#500' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --mode ray \
+    --nproc_per_node "$NPROC_TOTAL" \
+    --ray_exp_name qwen05b_multinode_ray \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 8 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 2 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 multi-node SFT under torchrun: run THIS SAME command on every node, only NODE_RANK differs.
+#
+# Launch model. Unlike the legacy form (hand-writing `torchrun ... swift/cli/sft.py`), v5 drives the
+# launcher through environment variables: setting NNODES (or NPROC_PER_NODE) makes swift/cli/main.py
+# relaunch the dev CLI under `torch.distributed.run`, forwarding NPROC_PER_NODE / NNODES / NODE_RANK /
+# MASTER_ADDR / MASTER_PORT verbatim (get_torchrun_args). So a node only exports the five variables and
+# calls `swift sft`; there is no torchrun line to maintain per node.
+#
+# Topology. World size = NNODES x NPROC_PER_NODE. Each rank runs the same recipe over its shard
+# (mode='local': twinkle.initialize builds a pure data-parallel mesh from Platform.get_world_size(),
+# which reads the WORLD_SIZE torchrun exports). The transformers backend has no TP/PP weight sharding,
+# so every rank holds a full replica and only the data is split. per_device_train_batch_size is PER
+# RANK; the global batch is per_device x world x gradient_accumulation_steps.
+#
+# REAL multi-node (2 nodes x 2 GPUs). Run on each node, changing only NODE_RANK and the local GPUs;
+# MASTER_ADDR is the rank-0 node's reachable IP on BOTH nodes, and all nodes must agree on NNODES,
+# NPROC_PER_NODE and MASTER_PORT:
+#   node 0:  NODE_RANK=0 MASTER_ADDR=<rank0_ip> CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 bash train.sh
+#   node 1:  NODE_RANK=1 MASTER_ADDR=<rank0_ip> CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 bash train.sh
+#
+# SINGLE-BOX simulation (how this was smoke-validated): two terminals on one machine, MASTER_ADDR over
+# loopback, disjoint GPUs so the 2 nodes do not collide, NPROC_PER_NODE=2 -> world=4. The rendezvous
+# and the cross-"node" all-reduce are the real thing; only the network is loopback.
+#   terminal A:  NODE_RANK=0 MASTER_ADDR=127.0.0.1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,2 NPROC_PER_NODE=2 bash train.sh
+#   terminal B:  NODE_RANK=1 MASTER_ADDR=127.0.0.1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3,4 NPROC_PER_NODE=2 bash train.sh
+#
+# Full-parameter multi-node training usually also shards the optimizer/parameters to fit: add

+# v5 image-text multimodal embedding (task_type=embedding) with the InfoNCE objective on a single GPU.
+#
+# The multimodal sibling of embedding.sh: `--task_type embedding` dispatches to run_embedding, which

+# AND in each candidate conversation, with its own parallel media column -- `images` for the anchor,
+# `positive_images` / `negative_images` for the candidates. The positive/negative media columns are
+# list-of-list: the outer list aligns with the candidate conversations (one positive is the documented
+# constraint), the inner list with the `<image>` tags in that conversation. See data/vl_embedding.jsonl

+# v5 SFT with the Muon optimizer (causal_lm, full-parameter, single GPU).
+#
+# `--optim muon` resolves to twinkle's MuonClip, which orthogonalises the update for the parameter groups
+# it selects (the 2D hidden weights) and runs an AdamW step for the rest; a muon_config is assembled from
+# TrainConfig's muon_* fields (all left at their defaults here). Muon trains FULL parameters, and lr 1e-4
+# is stable for it (measured: loss stays finite, grad_norm ~10-20). On the Megatron backend the equivalent
+# is `--optimizer muon` / `dist_muon` (the sharded variant). Note plain `muon` reads whole parameters, so
+# the DistributedConfig overlap_grad_reduce/overlap_param_gather knobs must stay off (use `dist_muon` with
+# those overlaps).
+#
+# QK-Clip IS OFF BY DEFAULT -- and you almost certainly want to keep it off for SFT. MuonClip can also run
+# QK-Clip, a from-scratch-pretraining brake (Kimi K2) that rescales the Q/K WEIGHTS by sqrt(tau / peak
+# attention logit) on every step whose peak exceeds `--qk_clip_tau`. dev defaults `--qk_clip_enabled false`
+# so `--optim muon` is plain Muon. Do NOT flip it on for a pretrained model without raising tau: an
+# instruct Qwen2.5 already runs attention logits ~1e3, so the default-scale ceiling trips EVERY step and
+# geometrically collapses Q/K (measured: weight norm 60 -> 0.001 in 6 steps, loss 1.8 -> 8, and it does so
+# at lr 1e-5 exactly as at 1e-4 because the rescale never multiplies by lr). Opt in only for from-scratch
+# runs, e.g. `--qk_clip_enabled true --qk_clip_tau 10000` (tau above the model's natural logit scale).
+#
+# DATASET CHOICE = VISIBLE CONVERGENCE. `swift/self-cognition` (not alpaca-gpt4): an already-instruct
+# Qwen2.5-0.5B plateaus at ~1.6 loss on alpaca (no headroom), so the run looks flat; self-cognition is new
+# knowledge it must fit, so the loss falls clearly. Keep --num_train_epochs 3 so the descent completes.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#600' \
+    --tuner full \
+    --optim muon \
+    --num_train_epochs 3 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 sequence packing (--packing true): concatenate many short samples into few dense fixed-length rows.
+#
+# USE_SWIFT_V5=1 routes `swift sft` to the dev CLI. `--packing true` (DatasetConfig.packing) groups encoded
+# samples with a bin-packer into rows of `--packing_length` tokens, so one forward/backward covers several
+# logical samples instead of one sample + padding. Packing AUTO-ENABLES padding_free (see
+# swift/dev/config/process.py: `Setting padding_free=True because packing is enabled`): the packed row is a
+# single [1, total] sequence whose per-sample position_ids restart at 0, and attention is block-diagonal so
+# samples cannot see each other. That varlen/block-diagonal attention is why `--attn_impl flash_attention_2`
+# is pinned here -- it is the backend that honours the packed layout on this stack.
+#
+# PACKING IS causal_lm ONLY. Pooled tasks (embedding/reranker/seq_cls) have no legal packed layout -- they
+# pool per sequence and cannot recover sub-sequence boundaries after concatenation -- so dev rejects packing
+# for them; do not copy this flag into an embedding/reranker/seq_cls script.
+#
+# --packing_length caps each packed row (keep it <= --max_length). --packing_strategy binpack fills rows
+# greedily (fewest rows); 'sequential' concatenates in dataset order. self-cognition rows are short, so
+# packing shows its value clearly: ~2000 tiny samples collapse into a few hundred dense rows.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#2000' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --packing true \
+    --packing_length 1024 \
+    --packing_strategy binpack \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 2 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --split_dataset_ratio 0.01 \

+# v5 padding-free training (--padding_free true): drop pad tokens by flattening a batch into one sequence.
+#
+# Without padding_free, a batch of B variable-length samples is a [B, T] tensor padded to the longest T, and
+# the pad tokens are wasted compute masked out of the loss. `--padding_free true` (TemplateConfig.padding_free)
+# instead concatenates the B samples into a single [1, sum_len] row and passes per-sample position_ids that
+# restart at 0 for each sample; flash-attention's varlen kernel then keeps attention block-diagonal, so the
+# result is mathematically identical to the padded batch but with zero pad tokens. Throughput rises with how
+# uneven the sample lengths are.
+#
+# DIFFERENT FROM --packing: padding_free removes padding WITHIN a batch at collate time (samples stay 1:1 with
+# the dataset); packing pre-concatenates samples ACROSS the dataset into fixed-length rows (and turns
+# padding_free on itself). Use padding_free alone for a normal SFT run with ragged lengths; use packing when
+# samples are much shorter than max_length and you want to fill every row.
+#
+# --attn_impl flash_attention_2 is required: only the varlen flash kernel consumes the packed position_ids and
+# enforces the block-diagonal mask. Like packing, padding_free is causal_lm-only -- pooled tasks
+# (embedding/reranker/seq_cls) cannot recover per-sequence pooling boundaries from a flattened row.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#2000' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --padding_free true \
+    --attn_impl flash_attention_2 \
+    --num_train_epochs 1 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 4 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --split_dataset_ratio 0.01 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# A custom training callback plugin, loaded with --external_plugins and selected with --callbacks.
+#
+# The `callback` extension point (swift.dev.callbacks) fires at transformers-Trainer-equivalent points
+# in dev's training loop. A callback subclasses TrainCallback, overrides only the events it needs (all
+# no-op by default), and is registered by name with @PluginRegistry.register('callback', <name>). The
+# loop passes a CallbackState (where training is: global_step / epoch / loss / metrics / best_metric)
+# and a CallbackControl (what to ask the loop to do next: should_training_stop / should_save /
+# should_evaluate / should_log). Set a control flag to steer the run -- e.g. should_save forces a
+# checkpoint at that step.
+#
+# This plugin just observes and logs progress; see EarlyStopCallback (swift.dev.callbacks.builtins) for a
+# built-in that reads the same state and sets control.should_training_stop.
+from typing import Any, Dict, Optional
+
+from swift.dev.callbacks import CallbackControl, CallbackState, TrainCallback
+from swift.dev.utils.plugin import PluginRegistry
+from swift.dev.utils import get_logger
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+
+@PluginRegistry.register('callback', 'progress_printer')
+class ProgressPrinterCallback(TrainCallback):
+    """Log a heartbeat every 10 optimizer steps, plus the eval and end-of-run summaries."""
+
+    def on_train_begin(self, state: CallbackState, control: CallbackControl) -> None:
+        logger.info('[progress_printer] training started')
+
+    def on_step_end(self, state: CallbackState, control: CallbackControl) -> None:
+        if state.global_step % 10 == 0:
+            logger.info(f'[progress_printer] step={state.global_step} epoch={state.epoch} loss={state.loss}')
+
+    def on_evaluate(self,
+                    state: CallbackState,
+                    control: CallbackControl,
+                    metrics: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> None:
+        logger.info(f'[progress_printer] eval at step {state.global_step}: {metrics}')
+
+    def on_train_end(self, state: CallbackState, control: CallbackControl) -> None:
+        logger.info(f'[progress_printer] training ended at step {state.global_step}; best={state.best_metric}')

+# v5 reranker training (task_type=reranker) with a pointwise objective on a single GPU.
+#
+# `--task_type reranker` dispatches to run_reranker, which builds a num_labels=1 cross-encoder scoring

+# `listwise_reranker` for a list-wise softmax objective). Rows carry the same anchor + positive_messages
+# / negative_messages layout as embedding. `--task_type generative_reranker` is the alternative that
+# scores off the vocab head instead of a dedicated cross-encoder head.
+#
+# The scoring head is freshly initialized, so this trains FULL parameters (`--tuner full`). Dataset:
+# `scidocs-reranking#2000` is a REAL hub set -- the MTEB SciDocs reranking benchmark, whose rows the loader
+# turns into a query `messages` plus `positive_messages` (relevant docs) and `negative_messages` (irrelevant
+# ones), exactly the pointwise_reranker layout. Reference it by the REGISTERED name (`scidocs-reranking`), NOT
+# the raw `MTEB/scidocs-reranking` id, so the reranking preprocessor emits those two columns. OFFLINE fallback

-"""OPSD dataset plugin for open-r1/OpenThoughts-114k-math.
-
-Prepares the dataset for On-Policy Self-Distillation:
-- Student sees only the problem.
-- Teacher sees the problem + reference solution (privileged info via teacher_prompt).
-- Only verified-correct examples are used.
-
-Usage:
-    # GKD path (teacher KL as a direct loss):
-    swift rlhf --rlhf_type gkd --external_plugins opsd_plugin.py ...
-    # OPD-RL path (teacher KL as a per-token RL advantage):
-    swift rlhf --rlhf_type grpo --teacher_model <same-as-model> --external_plugins opsd_plugin.py ...
-"""
-from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
-
-from swift.dataset import DatasetMeta, RowPreprocessor, register_dataset
-
-SYSTEM_PROMPT = 'Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \\boxed{}.'
-
-TRANSITION_PROMPT = ('After understanding the reference solution and the rationale behind each step, '
-                     'now articulate your own step-by-step reasoning that derives the final answer.')
-
-
-class OpenThoughtsOPSDPreprocessor(RowPreprocessor):
-    """Preprocessor that builds teacher_prompt from the reference solution.
-
-    Both student and teacher share the same system prompt for format guidance.
-    The teacher's user message additionally includes the reference solution as privileged info.
-    """
-
-    def preprocess(self, row: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
-        if not row.get('correct', True):
-            return None
-
-        problem = row.get('problem', '')
-        solution = row.get('solution', '')
-
-        teacher_prompt = (f'{problem}\n\n'
-                          f'Here is a reference solution to this problem:\n{solution}\n\n'
-                          f'{TRANSITION_PROMPT}')
-
-        messages: List[Dict[str, str]] = [
-            {
-                'role': 'system',
-                'content': SYSTEM_PROMPT
-            },
-            {
-                'role': 'user',
-                'content': problem
-            },
-        ]
-
-        return {'messages': messages, 'teacher_prompt': teacher_prompt}
-
-
-register_dataset(
-    DatasetMeta(
-        ms_dataset_id='open-r1/OpenThoughts-114k-math',
-        hf_dataset_id='open-r1/OpenThoughts-114k-math',
-        preprocess_func=OpenThoughtsOPSDPreprocessor(),
-        tags=['math', 'opsd'],
-    ))

+# v5 sequence-classification SFT (task_type=seq_cls) on a single GPU.
+#
+# `--task_type seq_cls` dispatches swift.dev.cli.sft to run_seq_cls, which builds a num_labels-wide
+# classification head on the causal LM. `--problem_type single_label_classification` selects the
+# cross-entropy objective (use `regression` with `--num_labels 1` for a scalar MSE head, or
+# `multi_label_classification` for BCE). The head is freshly initialized, so this trains FULL
+# parameters (`--tuner full`): a LoRA run would need the head listed in modules_to_save to move it.
+#
+# Dataset: `hc3-zh:finance_cls#2000` is a REAL hub set -- the HC3-Chinese finance subset posed as a 2-way
+# Human-vs-ChatGPT classification (the `_cls` view emits an int `label` beside `messages`, matching
+# `--num_labels 2`); `#2000` takes a 2000-row slice. Reference it by the REGISTERED name (`hc3-zh:...`), not
+# the raw hub id, so the loader's classification preprocessor runs and the `label` column is produced. For an
+# OFFLINE run with no hub access, fall back to the bundled `examples/train/data/seq_cls.jsonl` (the same
+# {messages, label} shape).
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type seq_cls \
+    --num_labels 2 \
+    --problem_type single_label_classification \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'hc3-zh:finance_cls#2000' \
+    --tuner full \
+    --num_train_epochs 3 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 2 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 1 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-5 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 512 \
+    --logging_steps 1 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 streaming (--streaming true): train from a dataset read as a lazy stream, not fully downloaded/materialised.
+#
+# By default dev loads and encodes the whole dataset up front (fine for small sets, impossible for a 100M-row
+# corpus). `--streaming true` (DatasetConfig.streaming) switches the source to an IterableDataset: rows are
+# pulled, tokenised, and batched on the fly, so memory stays flat and training starts after the first shard is
+# fetched rather than after the whole download. `--lazy_tokenize` is implied by streaming (encode per row as it
+# arrives); `--shuffle_buffer_size` holds a rolling buffer that is shuffled in place, since a stream cannot be
+# globally shuffled without one.
+#
+# TWO CONSEQUENCES OF STREAMING, both reflected below:
+#   1. A stream has no known length, so `--num_train_epochs` cannot size the run -- bound it with `--max_steps`
+#      instead. (An epoch over an unbounded stream never ends.)
+#   2. Holdout splitting a stream is awkward, so this trains only (`--split_dataset_ratio 0`); use a separate
+#      `--val_dataset` if you need eval while streaming.
+# The 110k distill set is used to make the point -- streaming pulls only the ~few hundred rows max_steps needs,
+# never the full file. Swap in any large hub dataset id.
+#
+# OVER-LENGTH ROWS: this reasoning-distill corpus has rows longer than max_length, and the default
+# truncation_strategy=None FAILS LOUDLY (MaxLengthError) the moment one is reached -- you cannot know up front
+# which streamed row is too long. So `--truncation_strategy delete` drops any row exceeding `--max_length`
+# instead of crashing (alternatives: 'left'/'right' truncate, 'split' chunks it). max_length is set to 4096 to
+# keep most rows and delete only the rare longer one.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'swift/Chinese-Qwen3-235B-2507-Distill-data-110k-SFT' \
+    --streaming true \
+    --shuffle_buffer_size 1000 \
+    --max_steps 50 \
+    --truncation_strategy delete \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 4096 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --split_dataset_ratio 0 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 thinking-mode control (--enable_thinking): train a hybrid-reasoning model (Qwen3) in think or non-think mode.
+#
+# Qwen3 is a hybrid thinking model: the same weights can answer directly, or first emit a <think>...</think>
+# rationale. Which behaviour a training run teaches is controlled at the TEMPLATE layer, not by a different
+# model. `--enable_thinking` (TemplateConfig.enable_thinking) is the switch:
+#   true  -> the template runs in thinking mode; the reasoning span is part of the trained target.
+#   false -> non-thinking mode; the model is trained to answer without a visible rationale.
+#   unset -> follow the checkpoint's default (Qwen3-0.6B defaults to thinking on).
+# Related knobs: `--preserve_thinking` keeps think blocks already present in the data verbatim instead of
+# re-deriving them; `--add_non_thinking_prefix` (default true) prepends the empty-think prefix so a
+# non-thinking turn is explicit; `--loss_scale ignore_empty_think` (see swift/loss_scale/mapping.py) drops an
+# empty <think> from the loss.
+#
+# self-cognition is used only because it is small and cached so the smoke is quick; it demonstrates that the
+# flag is accepted and the run converges. For a real reasoning run point --dataset at data whose responses
+# actually contain rationales, and pair --enable_thinking true with --preserve_thinking.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --enable_thinking true \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#600' \
+    --tuner lora \
+    --lora_rank 8 \
+    --lora_alpha 32 \
+    --target_modules all-linear \
+    --num_train_epochs 3 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-4 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 4096 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --split_dataset_ratio 0.01 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 trainable_tokens tuner: train ONLY chosen embedding rows, freezing the rest of the model.
+#
+# `--tuner trainable_tokens` builds a peft TrainableTokens adapter that unfreezes just the embedding rows
+# listed in `--trainable_token_indices` (int token ids) and trains nothing else. It is the standard way to
+# learn embeddings for NEWLY ADDED special tokens: pass --new_special_tokens to extend the vocabulary
+# (dev resizes the embedding), then list the new ids -- they start at the pre-extension tokenizer length
+# (for Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct that is 151665, so the first added token is 151665, the next 151666, ...).
+# --tuner trainable_tokens REQUIRES --trainable_token_indices (dev raises without it).
+#
+# Trainable tokens also ride alongside LoRA: `--tuner lora --trainable_token_indices ...` adapts the model
+# with LoRA while additionally learning those embedding rows -- the usual production pattern when you add
+# domain tokens and still want a full adaptation. Standalone (shown here) is for when the base is meant to
+# stay frozen and only the new-token embeddings should move.
+#
+# This runnable demo points the indices at a handful of frequent EXISTING token ids of
+# Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (you=9330, are=546, the=1782, assistant=77091, What=3838, I=40, a=64, to=983) so
+# gradients flow and the loss moves without needing a dataset that contains brand-new tokens; swap in your
+# own new-special-token ids for the real workflow.
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
+    --task_type causal_lm \
+    --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
+    --dataset 'swift/self-cognition#600' \
+    --tuner trainable_tokens \
+    --trainable_token_indices 9330 546 1782 77091 3838 40 64 983 \
+    --num_train_epochs 3 \
+    --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
+    --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \
+    --learning_rate 1e-3 \
+    --lr_scheduler cosine \
+    --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
+    --max_length 2048 \
+    --logging_steps 5 \
+    --save_steps 100 \
+    --save_total_limit 2 \
+    --split_dataset_ratio 0.01 \
+    --output_dir output \
+    --report_to tensorboard

+# v5 YAML config: the entire argument set for `swift sft`, as a file instead of a flag list.
+#
+# Consumed by `swift sft examples/train/yaml/sft.yaml` (see train.sh next to this file). swift/cli/main.py
+# parse_yaml_args loads the FIRST positional arg when it ends in .yaml/.yml/.json, then rewrites it into the
+# equivalent `--key value` flags before the dev CLI ever sees argv:
+#   - a scalar  (model: X)        -> --model X
+#   - a list    (dataset: [a, b]) -> --dataset a b        (each item appended)
+#   - a dict                      -> --key '<json blob>'  (json.dumps)
+# So this file is exactly the lora/train.sh flag set, in YAML. Nothing is YAML-only; it is the same Config.
+#
+# An optional top-level `ENV:` mapping is popped and written into os.environ (existing vars win). NOTE the one
+# thing it CANNOT do: enable v5 itself. resolve_route() reads USE_SWIFT_V5 BEFORE parse_yaml_args runs, so
+# putting USE_SWIFT_V5 under ENV here is too late -- the run would route to the legacy CLI. That is why
+# train.sh exports USE_SWIFT_V5=1 (and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES) in the shell, and this file stays pure config.
+model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
+task_type: causal_lm
+torch_dtype: bfloat16
+dataset:
+  - 'swift/self-cognition#600'
+tuner: lora
+lora_rank: 8
+lora_alpha: 32
+target_modules:
+  - all-linear
+num_train_epochs: 3
+per_device_train_batch_size: 1
+gradient_accumulation_steps: 8
+learning_rate: 0.0001
+lr_scheduler: cosine
+warmup_ratio: 0.05
+max_length: 2048
+logging_steps: 5
+save_steps: 100
+save_total_limit: 2
+split_dataset_ratio: 0.01
+output_dir: output
+report_to: tensorboard

+# v5 YAML-driven SFT: same run as train/lora/train.sh, but every argument lives in sft.yaml.
+#
+# The YAML file is passed as the FIRST positional arg after the subcommand; swift/cli/main.py expands it into
+# the equivalent --flags before dispatch (see the header in sft.yaml for the scalar/list/dict rules). USE_SWIFT_V5
+# and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES are set HERE, in the shell, not in the yaml's ENV block: resolve_route() reads
+# USE_SWIFT_V5 before the yaml is parsed, so v5 routing must be decided by the environment the process starts in.
+#
+# Run from the repository root (the yaml path, like every examples/ path, is repo-root-relative).
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
+USE_SWIFT_V5=1 \
+swift sft examples/train/yaml/sft.yaml

+# Copyright (c) ModelScope Contributors. All rights reserved.
+"""Shared plumbing for the supported-models-and-datasets doc generators.
+
+``run_model_info.py`` and ``run_dataset_info.py`` each regenerate one half of the same bilingual
+markdown file and must preserve the other half verbatim, so they share a single definition of the
+file paths, the section headings that delimit the two halves, the hub-link format, and the tags
+legend. Centralising those is what stops the two scripts from drifting apart: a heading renamed in
+one but not the other would silently duplicate or drop a whole section on the next run.
+
+Ownership split, delimited by the ``## Datasets`` / ``## 数据集`` heading:
+
+- ``run_model_info`` regenerates everything *above* that heading (title, table of contents, tags
+  legend, and the model tables) and preserves the dataset half.
+- ``run_dataset_info`` regenerates that heading and everything *below* it, preserving the model half.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+from swift.dev.utils.tags import CONTROLLED_TAGS
+
+# (language, path). The two files are generated together and carry identical tables; only the
+# surrounding prose differs by language.
+DOC_PATHS: List[Tuple[str, str]] = [
+    ('zh', 'docs/source/Instruction/Supported-models-and-datasets.md'),
+    ('en', 'docs/source_en/Instruction/Supported-models-and-datasets.md'),
+]
+
+# Headings per language. ``datasets`` doubles as the boundary between the two halves, so it must stay
+# in sync with what the generators emit and with the heading already present in the committed docs.
+PROSE: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = {
+    'zh': {
+        'title': '支持的模型和数据集',
+        'toc': '目录',
+        'tags_legend': 'Tags 说明',
+        'models': '模型',
+        'llm': '大语言模型',
+        'mllm': '多模态大模型',
+        'datasets': '数据集',
+        'tags_legend_intro': ('`tags` 取自受控词表（单一真源：`swift/dev/tags.py`）。注册模型或数据集时使用词表之外的 '
+                              'tag 会直接报错，因此下表列出的即当前允许的全部 tag：'),
+    },
+    'en': {
+        'title': 'Supported Models and Datasets',
+        'toc': 'Table of Contents',
+        'tags_legend': 'Tags Legend',
+        'models': 'Models',
+        'llm': 'Large language models',

+# Copyright (c) ModelScope Contributors. All rights reserved.
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, List, Optional
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from swift.dev.config import TunerConfig
+    from swift.dev.model import TrainableModel
+
+# tuners that are peft-backed and reachable from dev. Anything else fails fast in apply_tuner
+# rather than being silently downgraded to LoRA.
+SUPPORTED_TUNER_TYPES = ('lora', 'trainable_tokens')
+
+#: The classification-head module names an HF ``*ForSequenceClassification`` model may use, added to
+#: ``modules_to_save`` for a seq_cls / reranker LoRA run so the fresh head is trained AND saved. Both are
+#: listed (family-specific: Qwen/LLaMA use ``score``, Bert/Deberta ``classifier``) because it cannot be
+#: probed here: under Ray this runs on the driver against a model PROXY, and peft matches by
+#: ``name.endswith(entry)`` with strict_module_check=False, so the miss is a safe no-op.
+_SEQ_CLS_HEAD_MODULES = ('score', 'classifier')
+#: task_types that ride a separate classification head needing the modules_to_save treatment above.
+#: generative_reranker keeps the CausalLM vocab head (no new module); the PPO value critic rides seq_cls.
+_HEAD_SAVING_TASK_TYPES = ('seq_cls', 'reranker')
+
+
+def _resolve_target_modules(cfg: TunerConfig):
+    """target_regex wins over target_modules; collapse the 1-element 'all-linear' list peft wants
+    as a bare string."""
+    target_modules = cfg.target_regex or cfg.target_modules
+    # peft accepts a str ('all-linear'/regex) or a list of module names.
+    if isinstance(target_modules, list) and len(target_modules) == 1 and target_modules[0] == 'all-linear':
+        target_modules = 'all-linear'
+    return target_modules
+
+
+def is_base_modifying_init(init_weights) -> bool:
+    """Whether a peft ``init_lora_weights`` strategy reads or rewrites the base weight at injection.
+
+    The pissa family (pissa / pissa_niter_[N] / olora / corda / lora_ga) subtracts its init factor from
+    the base weight, and 'loftq' quantises it -- an adapter trained with one only fits the *residual*
+    base it produced. Consumed by the streaming merge's fallback routing and by the checkpoint saver's
+    converted-adapter flow.
+    """
+    return isinstance(init_weights, str) and (
+        init_weights.startswith(('pissa', 'corda')) or init_weights in ('olora', 'lora_ga', 'loftq'))
+
+
+def _resolve_init_weights(cfg: TunerConfig):
+    """swift spells it init_weights and accepts the strings 'true'/'false'; peft wants a bool there
+    and keeps the real strategy names ('gaussian'/'pissa'/'olora'/...) as-is."""
+    init_weights = cfg.init_weights
+    if isinstance(init_weights, str) and init_weights.lower() in {'true', 'false'}:
+        return init_weights.lower() == 'true'
+    # LoRA-GA needs the lora_ga_* parameters (rejected as unsupported) and a separate weight-init pass
+    # dev does not run; peft would only raise a confusing error, so reject here with the actual reason.
+    if isinstance(init_weights, str) and init_weights.lower().replace('-', '_') == 'lora_ga':
+        raise ValueError(
+            "init_weights='lora-ga' (LoRA-GA) is not supported by dev: it needs the lora_ga_* parameters "
+            '(rejected as unsupported) and a separate weight-initialization pass dev does not run. Use a '
+            "supported init_weights ('true'/'false'/'gaussian'/'pissa'/'pissa_niter_[N]'/'olora').")
+    return init_weights
+
+
+def _lora_common_kwargs(cfg: TunerConfig, task_type: Optional[str] = None) -> dict:
+    """The LoraConfig kwargs shared by every supported tuner here."""
+    # A seq_cls / reranker run builds a fresh classification head; LoRA wraps target_modules only, so
+    # without the head in modules_to_save the checkpoint reloads with a random head. Copied, not mutated.
+    modules_to_save = list(cfg.modules_to_save or [])
+    # The 'all-norm'/'all-embedding' shorthands ride through verbatim and are expanded worker-side
+    # (twinkle _expand_modules_to_save) against the real modules; megatron rejects 'all-norm'.
+    if task_type in _HEAD_SAVING_TASK_TYPES:
+        modules_to_save += [name for name in _SEQ_CLS_HEAD_MODULES if name not in modules_to_save]
+    kwargs = dict(
+        r=cfg.lora_rank,
+        lora_alpha=cfg.lora_alpha,
+        lora_dropout=cfg.lora_dropout,
+        bias=cfg.lora_bias,
+        target_modules=_resolve_target_modules(cfg),
+        modules_to_save=(modules_to_save or None),
+        use_rslora=cfg.use_rslora,
+        use_dora=cfg.use_dora,
+        init_lora_weights=_resolve_init_weights(cfg),
+    )
+    # Newer peft additions that default to "unset"; only pass them when requested so an older peft
+    # is not handed an unknown kwarg.
+    if cfg.target_parameters:
+        # requires peft>=0.17.0
+        kwargs['target_parameters'] = cfg.target_parameters
+    if cfg.trainable_token_indices:
+        kwargs['trainable_token_indices'] = cfg.trainable_token_indices
+    return kwargs
+
+
+def _build_adapter_config(cfg: TunerConfig,
+                          *,
+                          task_type: Optional[str] = None):
+    """Build the peft config for ``cfg.tuner``: lora -> LoraConfig (QLoRA/DoRA/rsLoRA are flags),
+    trainable_tokens -> TrainableTokensConfig; anything else raises.
+
+    peft's own ``task_type`` FIELD is intentionally NOT set: get_peft_model then returns a base PeftModel
+    that forwards straight to the wrapped model, matching every twinkle cookbook -- the CAUSAL_LM wrapper
+    reads base_model.config.model_type, which the Megatron path's mcore ModelConfig lacks. The
+    ``task_type`` ARGUMENT is dev's (seq_cls/reranker/...), used only for the head-saving rule above.
+    """
+    tuner = cfg.tuner
+
+    if tuner == 'lora':
+        from peft import LoraConfig
+        return LoraConfig(**_lora_common_kwargs(cfg, task_type=task_type))
+
+    if tuner == 'trainable_tokens':
+        from peft import TrainableTokensConfig
+        # Standalone TrainableTokens spells the indices token_indices (LoRA's passthrough field is
+        # trainable_token_indices); with no explicit target peft infers the input-embedding module.
+        if not cfg.trainable_token_indices:
+            raise ValueError('tuner="trainable_tokens" requires trainable_token_indices.')
+        kwargs = {}
+        if cfg.target_regex or cfg.target_modules != ['all-linear']:
+            kwargs['target_modules'] = _resolve_target_modules(cfg)
+        return TrainableTokensConfig(token_indices=cfg.trainable_token_indices, **kwargs)
+
+    raise NotImplementedError(f'tuner={tuner!r} is not supported by dev; '
+                              f'supported: {", ".join(SUPPORTED_TUNER_TYPES)}. '
+                              f'(DoRA/rsLoRA are LoRA flags -- use tuner="lora" with '
+                              f'use_dora/use_rslora; QLoRA is LoRA + a quantized base model via '
+                              f'QuantizeConfig; LoRA+ is the "lorap" optimizer, not a tuner.)')
+
+
+def apply_tuner(model: TrainableModel,
+                tuner_cfg: TunerConfig,
+                *,
+                adapter_name: str = 'default',
+                gradient_accumulation_steps: int = 1,
+                task_type: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
+    adapter_config = _build_adapter_config(tuner_cfg, task_type=task_type)
+    model.add_adapter_to_model(
+        adapter_name,
+        adapter_config,
+        gradient_accumulation_steps=gradient_accumulation_steps,
+        freeze_llm=tuner_cfg.freeze_llm,
+        freeze_vit=tuner_cfg.freeze_vit,
+        freeze_aligner=tuner_cfg.freeze_aligner)
+
+
+def configure_frozen_adapter(model: Any, template: Any, adapters: List[str], *, role: str) -> Any:
+    """Load one frozen adapter onto an auxiliary model and bind its processor/template group."""
+    from swift.dev.processor import InputProcessor
+
+    if len(adapters) > 1:
+        raise ValueError(f'{role}_adapters currently supports exactly one adapter per auxiliary model.')
+    if adapters:
+        adapter_name = f'{role}_adapter'
+        model.add_adapter_to_model(adapter_name, adapters[0], is_trainable=False)

+def build_dataset(dataset_config: DatasetConfig,
+                  template: Any,
+                  train_config: TrainConfig,
+                  distributed_config: DistributedConfig,
+                  *,
+                  encode: bool = True,
+                  template_config: Optional[TemplateConfig] = None,
+                  device_mesh: Optional['DeviceMesh'] = None) -> Any:
+    """Load train (+val) once and return ``(train_loader, val_loader)`` (either may be None).
+
+    ``encode`` pre-tokenizes now (SFT) or defers to train/rollout time (GRPO/GKD: False);
+    ``cached_dataset`` splits join after encoding and are never re-encoded (legacy SwiftSft).
+    """
+    from swift.dev.dataset import load_dataset, register_dataset_info
+    # legacy base_args.py: a nonzero split ratio alongside val_dataset would carve a slice out of
+    # --dataset that is neither trained on (train keeps only its remainder) nor evaluated.
+    if dataset_config.val_dataset and dataset_config.split_dataset_ratio:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f'split_dataset_ratio={dataset_config.split_dataset_ratio} cannot be combined with '
+            'val_dataset: the ratio carves a val slice out of --dataset that is then neither trained '
+            'on (train keeps only its remainder) nor evaluated (val_dataset overrides it). Drop '
+            'split_dataset_ratio, or drop val_dataset to eval on the split-off slice instead.')
+    for info_path in dataset_config.custom_dataset_info:
+        register_dataset_info(info_path, exist_ok=True)
+
+    load_kwargs = _load_kwargs(dataset_config)
+
+    train_raw, val_raw = (None, None)
+    if dataset_config.dataset:
+        # load-time shuffle is dataset_shuffle (whole-dataset shuffle at load, legacy semantics)
+        train_raw, val_raw = load_dataset(
+            dataset_config.dataset,
+            split_dataset_ratio=dataset_config.split_dataset_ratio,
+            shuffle=dataset_config.dataset_shuffle,
+            **load_kwargs)
+    if dataset_config.val_dataset:
+        # legacy base_args.py: val_dataset replaces any split-off val; interleave_prob is a
+        # train-mixing knob and must not sample the val set.
+        load_kwargs.pop('interleave_prob', None)
+        _, val_raw = load_dataset(
+            dataset_config.val_dataset,
+            split_dataset_ratio=1.0,
+            shuffle=dataset_config.val_dataset_shuffle,
+            **load_kwargs)
+
+    cached_train, cached_val = _load_cached_datasets(dataset_config, template_config)
+    encode_mode = _encode_mode(dataset_config, template) if encode else None
+    train_loader = _build_split_loader(

+        encode=encode, encode_mode=encode_mode, is_val=False, cached=cached_train,
+        device_mesh=device_mesh)

+def _load_kwargs(dataset_config: DatasetConfig) -> dict:
+    """Full load_dataset kwargs, mirroring legacy DataArguments.get_dataset_kwargs.
+
+    remove_unused_columns / disable_auto_column_mapping are refused rather than forwarded: the dev
+    dataset framework always drops consumed source columns and always applies declared renames.
+    """
+    if not dataset_config.remove_unused_columns:
+        raise ValueError('remove_unused_columns=False is not supported by the dev dataset framework: its '
+                         'preprocessors always drop the source columns they consumed. Drop the flag, or keep '
+                         'the extra columns by loading the dataset without a preprocessor.')
+    if dataset_config.disable_auto_column_mapping:
+        raise ValueError('disable_auto_column_mapping=True is not supported by the dev dataset framework: a '
+                         "dataset's `columns` renames are part of its loader declaration and always apply. "
+                         'Pass `columns` to override individual names instead.')
+    return dict(
+        seed=dataset_config.data_seed,
+        num_proc=dataset_config.dataset_num_proc,
+        load_from_cache_file=dataset_config.load_from_cache_file,
+        streaming=dataset_config.streaming,
+        interleave_prob=dataset_config.interleave_prob,
+        stopping_strategy=dataset_config.stopping_strategy,
+        shuffle_buffer_size=dataset_config.shuffle_buffer_size,
+        use_hf=dataset_config.use_hf,
+        hub_token=dataset_config.hub_token,

+def _load_cached_datasets(dataset_config: DatasetConfig, template_config: Any) -> tuple:
+    """Load ``cached_dataset`` / ``cached_val_dataset`` from disk as ``(train_splits, val_splits)`` lists.
+
+    DatasetLoader.load_cached_datasets owns the length->lengths rename, the delete-strategy length filter
+    and the ``path#N`` subsampling; template_config is optional (None = no length filter applied).
+    """
+    if not dataset_config.cached_dataset and not dataset_config.cached_val_dataset:
+        return [], []
+    from swift.dev.dataset import DatasetLoader
+
+    train_datasets, val_datasets = DatasetLoader.load_cached_datasets(
+        dataset_config.cached_dataset,
+        dataset_config.cached_val_dataset,
+        max_length=getattr(template_config, 'max_length', None),
+        truncation_strategy=getattr(template_config, 'truncation_strategy', None),
+        data_seed=dataset_config.data_seed,
+        shuffle=dataset_config.dataset_shuffle,
+    )
+    logger.info(f'cached_dataset: {len(train_datasets)} train split(s), {len(val_datasets)} val split(s)')
+    return train_datasets, val_datasets

+def _encode_mode(dataset_config: DatasetConfig, template: Any) -> Literal['stream', 'eager', 'lazy']:
+    if dataset_config.streaming:
+        return 'stream'
+    lazy = dataset_config.lazy_tokenize

+    if lazy is None:

+            and not dataset_config.cached_val_dataset and not dataset_config.packing
+            and not dataset_config.group_by_length)
+        logger.info(f'Setting lazy_tokenize: {lazy}')
+    return 'lazy' if lazy else 'eager'

+def _build_split_loader(raw: Any,
+                        template: Any,
+                        dataset_config: DatasetConfig,
+                        train_config: TrainConfig,
+                        distributed_config: DistributedConfig,
+                        *,
+                        encode: bool,
+                        encode_mode: Optional[str],
+                        is_val: bool,
+                        cached: Optional[list] = None,
+                        device_mesh: Optional['DeviceMesh'] = None) -> Any:
+    """Encode -> merge cached -> optional pack -> dataloader for one split (None+no cache -> None)."""
+    if raw is None and not cached:

+            strict=dataset_config.strict, data_seed=dataset_config.data_seed)

+    # (AddLengthPreprocessor would waste it; EncodePreprocessor would corrupt already-tokenized rows)

+                             'the `lengths` column produced by encoding, which is skipped when encode=False.')
+        enc = _pack(

+            packing_strategy=dataset_config.packing_strategy,
+            num_proc=dataset_config.packing_num_proc,
+            strict=dataset_config.strict,
+            data_seed=dataset_config.data_seed)

+    batch_size = (train_config.per_device_eval_batch_size if is_val else train_config.per_device_train_batch_size)
+    dl_shuffle = (not is_val) and dataset_config.train_dataloader_shuffle

+    group_by_length = dataset_config.group_by_length and (not is_val)

+    # failing when group_by_length is also on, so those Megatron scripts keep running

+    # whether to skip -- eval never resumes

+        logger.warning('Streaming packing uses one dataset reader; setting `dataloader_num_workers=0`. '
+                       '`packing_num_proc` still controls parallel encoding.')

+        # same replacement; strict (max_retries=0) stops the run on the first failure instead
+        retry_seed=dataset_config.data_seed,
+        max_retries=0 if dataset_config.strict else 20,
+        collate_fn=_identity_collate,

+def _identity_collate(batch):
+    """Return the batch as a ``list[InputFeature]`` unchanged; dev collates inside the model forward."""
+    return list(batch)
+
+
+def _twinkle_loader_layout(distributed_config: DistributedConfig,
+                           per_device_batch_size: int,
+                           device_mesh: Optional['DeviceMesh'] = None) -> tuple:
+    """``(global_batch_size, loader_device_mesh)``: twinkle's DataLoader takes the GLOBAL batch and its
+    ShardedBatchSampler slices it per DP rank, so the batch is scaled by the DP width.
+    """
+    if device_mesh is not None:
+        # HF Ulysses SP: the sampler slices by data_world_size (world/ulysses), so SP peers get
+        # identical samples and only DP groups differ
+        return per_device_batch_size * device_mesh.data_world_size, device_mesh
+    if distributed_config.nproc_per_node is None:
+        # plain transformers torchrun (world size lives in the env, not the config): scale by the same
+        # source twinkle's local initialize reads; mesh stays None to inherit twinkle's global DP mesh
+        from twinkle.utils import Platform
+        return per_device_batch_size * Platform.get_world_size(), None
+    # Megatron path: build_parallel_mesh sizes the DP layout off nproc_per_node; under ray the loader is
+    # a bare driver loader and the DP scatter happens later in model.forward_backward('slice_dp')
+    from swift.dev.builders.model import build_parallel_mesh
+    mesh = build_parallel_mesh(distributed_config)
+    return per_device_batch_size * mesh.data_world_size, (None if distributed_config.mode == 'ray' else mesh)
+

+def _concat_with_cached(enc: Any, cached: list, *, encode_mode: Optional[str]) -> Any:
+    """Concatenate the freshly-encoded split with pre-encoded splits loaded from disk.
+
+    lazy/stream wrappers cannot be concatenated with the map-style cache, so mixing `dataset` with
+    `cached_dataset` is refused in those modes; a cache ALONE is fine in any mode.
+    """
+    from swift.dev.dataset import DatasetLoader
+
+    if enc is None:
+        _, cached = _align_features(None, cached)
+        return DatasetLoader.concat_datasets(cached)
+    if encode_mode in ('lazy', 'stream'):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f'cached_dataset cannot be combined with `dataset` when encode_mode={encode_mode!r}: the freshly '
+            'loaded split is a lazy/iterable wrapper and cannot be concatenated with the map-style cached '
+            'dataset. Either set DatasetConfig.lazy_tokenize=False (streaming=False) to encode eagerly, or '
+            'pass only cached_dataset (already encoded on disk).')
+    enc, cached = _align_features(enc, cached)
+    return DatasetLoader.concat_datasets([enc] + cached)

+
+def _align_features(enc: Any, cached: list) -> tuple:
+    """Make ``enc`` and the cached splits share one Arrow schema, returning both sides aligned.
+
+    list-of-dict columns come back struct or arrow.json depending on how the split was produced and
+    cannot be concatenated mixed; pyarrow casts struct -> Json but not back, so both sides go CACHED.
+    """
+    cached = list(cached)
+    if not cached:
+        return enc, cached
+    enc_features = getattr(enc, 'features', None)
+    cache_features = getattr(cached[0], 'features', None)
+    if enc_features is None or cache_features is None or enc_features == cache_features:
+        return enc, cached
+    if set(enc_features) != set(cache_features):
+        raise ValueError(f'cached_dataset columns {sorted(cache_features)} do not match the training split '
+                         f'{sorted(enc_features)}. The cache was produced with a different template/config; '
+                         're-export it with the same TemplateConfig, or drop the mismatched path.')
+    # Cast the fresh split onto the cache's schema (struct -> Json is castable; the reverse is not).
+    try:
+        enc = enc.cast(cache_features)
+    except Exception as e:
+        raise ValueError(f'cached_dataset could not be aligned with the training split: {e}. Re-export the '
+                         'cache with the current TemplateConfig, or train on the cache alone.') from e
+    aligned = []
+    for ds in cached:
+        features = getattr(ds, 'features', None)
+        if features is not None and features != cache_features:
+            ds = ds.cast(cache_features)
+        aligned.append(ds)
+    return enc, aligned

+def _extract_lengths(enc: Any) -> list:
+    column_names = getattr(enc, 'column_names', None)
+    if column_names is not None and 'lengths' in column_names:
+        return list(enc['lengths'])
+    raise ValueError('group_by_length=True requires a `lengths` column, which is only produced by EAGER '
+                     'encoding. Set DatasetConfig.lazy_tokenize=False (and use a non-streaming, map-style '
+                     'dataset) so the length of every sample is precomputed. Legacy swift has the same '
+                     'requirement (it reads train_dataset[\'lengths\']).')
+
+
+def _drop_last(distributed_config: DistributedConfig) -> bool:
+    """Megatron drops a trailing partial batch (exact global_batch_size invariant); hf keeps it (legacy)."""
+    return distributed_config.backend == 'megatron'
+
+
+def _encode(raw: Any, template: Any, *, mode: Literal['lazy', 'eager', 'stream'], num_proc: int, strict: bool,
+            materialize: bool = False, data_seed: Optional[int] = None) -> Any:
+    """Encode a raw messages split into trainable samples.
+
+    lazy -> LazyLLMDataset (encode at __getitem__); 'split' truncation / an explicit ``materialize``
+    need the full EncodePreprocessor; otherwise MeasurePreprocessor only adds `lengths`, rows stay raw.
+    """
+    from swift.dev.dataset import EncodePreprocessor, LazyLLMDataset, MeasurePreprocessor
+
+    truncation_strategy = getattr(template, 'truncation_strategy', None)
+    if truncation_strategy == 'split' and mode != 'eager':
+        raise ValueError(f"truncation_strategy='split' requires mode='eager', got mode='{mode}'. "
+                         "The 'split' strategy may produce multiple samples per input.")
+
+    if mode == 'lazy':
+        return LazyLLMDataset(raw, template.encode)
+
+    # 'split' emits multiple samples per input; materialize (only the cached-dataset exporter sets it)
+    # forces input_ids/labels into the rows. data_seed pins build-time random preprocessing per row.
+    preprocessor_kwargs = {} if data_seed is None else {'seed': data_seed}
+    if truncation_strategy == 'split' or materialize:
+        preprocessor = EncodePreprocessor(template, **preprocessor_kwargs)
+    else:
+        preprocessor = MeasurePreprocessor(template, **preprocessor_kwargs)
+    return preprocessor(raw, num_proc=num_proc, strict=strict)
+
+
+def _pack(dataset: Any, template: Any, *, streaming: bool, packing_length: Optional[int], packing_strategy: str,
+          num_proc: int, strict: bool, data_seed: int = 0) -> Any:
+    """Pack an encoded dataset for efficient training (map-style or iterable)."""
+    from swift.dev.dataset import IterablePackingDataset, PackingDataset
+
+    length = packing_length or template.max_length
+    cls = IterablePackingDataset if streaming else PackingDataset
+    # data_seed is the streaming protocol's (set_data_seed on a state restore); the map-style
+    # PackingDataset forwards **kwargs to SwiftDataset, whose signature is closed, so it must
+    # not receive it -- map-style resume rides SampleIndex.epoch instead.
+    seed_kwargs = {'data_seed': data_seed} if streaming else {}
+    return cls(
+        template,
+        dataset,
+        num_proc=num_proc,
+        packing_length=length,
+        packing_strategy=packing_strategy,
+        strict=strict,
+        **seed_kwargs)
+
+
+def load_prompt_only_rows(dataset_config: DatasetConfig, max_rows: Optional[int],
+                          split_dataset_ratio: float) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Load the raw prompt rows the rollout/sampling recipes (infer/gkd/grpo) drive generation from.
+
+    ``val_dataset`` wins outright; otherwise only the eval slice of ``dataset`` is used (ratio=0 runs
+    all) -- legacy infer's ``_prepare_val_dataset`` semantics.
+    """
+    from swift.dev.dataset import load_dataset
+
+    kwargs = _load_kwargs(dataset_config)
+    # legacy infer: val_dataset loads whole (its own shuffle flag; interleave_prob -- a train-mixing
+    # knob -- popped); the eval slice of --dataset uses dataset_shuffle, before the max_rows cut
+    if dataset_config.val_dataset:
+        kwargs.pop('interleave_prob', None)
+        _, rows = load_dataset(
+            datasets=list(dataset_config.val_dataset), split_dataset_ratio=1.0,
+            shuffle=dataset_config.val_dataset_shuffle, **kwargs)
+    elif split_dataset_ratio:
+        _, rows = load_dataset(
+            datasets=list(dataset_config.dataset), split_dataset_ratio=split_dataset_ratio,
+            shuffle=dataset_config.dataset_shuffle, **kwargs)
+        logger.info(f'load_prompt_only_rows: using the eval split of --dataset (split_dataset_ratio='
+                    f'{split_dataset_ratio}); pass split_dataset_ratio=0 to run over all of it.')
+    else:
+        rows, _ = load_dataset(
+            datasets=list(dataset_config.dataset), split_dataset_ratio=0.0,
+            shuffle=dataset_config.dataset_shuffle, **kwargs)
+
+    rows = list(rows or [])
+    if max_rows is not None:
+        rows = rows[:max_rows]
+    return rows
+
+
+def build_prompt_dataloader(prompts: List[List[dict]],
+                            prompt_extras: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]],
+                            *,
+                            seed: int,
+                            batch_size: int = 256) -> Any:
+    """A twinkle ``DataLoader`` over the online-RL prompt rows (the prompt-side build_dataset).
+
+    No encoding -- the rollout encodes each prompt itself; seeded reshuffle per pass, one pass per
+    ``iter()``; drop_last stays off so a partial batch is never a dropped prompt.
+    """
+    from twinkle.dataset import Dataset, DatasetMeta
+    from twinkle.dataloader import DataLoader
+
+    if not prompts:
+        raise ValueError('build_prompt_dataloader needs at least one prompt, got an empty sequence.')
+    if batch_size <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f'batch_size must be > 0, got {batch_size}.')
+    if prompt_extras is not None and len(prompt_extras) != len(prompts):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f'prompt_extras must align with prompts ({len(prompts)} rows), got {len(prompt_extras)}.')
+    extras = prompt_extras if prompt_extras is not None else [{} for _ in prompts]
+    rows = [{'messages': messages, **extra} for messages, extra in zip(prompts, extras)]
+    dataset = Dataset(DatasetMeta(data=rows))
+    return DataLoader(
+        dataset,
+        batch_size=batch_size,
+        data_seed=seed,
+        num_workers=0,
+        collate_fn=_identity_collate,
+        shuffle=True)
+
+
+def to_trajectory(row: Dict[str, Any], messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
+                  template_config: 'TemplateConfig') -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """Build the twinkle Trajectory for one row.
+
+    ``TemplateConfig.system`` REPLACES a system turn the row already has rather than stacking a second
+    one, matching legacy: two system messages is not a supported prompt shape for most templates.
+    """
+    trajectory: Dict[str, Any] = {'messages': messages}
+    system = getattr(template_config, 'system', None)
+    if system:
+        without_system = [message for message in messages if message.get('role') != 'system']
+        trajectory['messages'] = [{'role': 'system', 'content': system}] + without_system
+    for key in ('images', 'audios', 'videos', 'objects', 'tools'):
+        if row.get(key):
+            trajectory[key] = row[key]
+    return trajectory
+
+
+def split_prompt_and_reference(rows: List[Dict[str, Any]],
+                               template_config: 'TemplateConfig') -> Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], List[Optional[str]]]:
+    """rows -> ``(trajectories, references)``, with each row's trailing assistant turn moved aside.
+
+    Generation must see a prompt that stops before the reference answer, and the answer itself is
+    needed afterwards (metric label / reward ground truth); one place keeps "what the model saw"
+    identical across every consumer.
+    """
+    trajectories, references = [], []
+    for row in rows:
+        messages = list(row['messages'])
+        reference = messages.pop()['content'] if messages and messages[-1]['role'] == 'assistant' else None
+        references.append(reference)
+        trajectories.append(to_trajectory(row, messages, template_config))
+    return trajectories, references

+    translation here stops call sites from each forwarding a different subset of the contract.
+    """
+    import torch
+
+    from swift.model import get_model_processor
+
+    # Vision preprocessing overrides go through env so the loader's patch_qwen_vl_utils (read via
+    # get_env_args) picks them up inside the worker's process_tokenizer across the Ray boundary.
+    if model_config.vision_process_kwargs:
+        for key, value in model_config.vision_process_kwargs.items():
+            os.environ[key.upper()] = str(value)
+
+    kwargs = dict(model_config.model_kwargs or {})
+    values = {
+        'model_type': model_config.model_type,
+        'revision': model_config.model_revision,
+        'experts_impl': model_config.experts_impl,
+        'new_special_tokens': model_config.new_special_tokens,
+        'rope_scaling': model_config.rope_scaling,
+        'max_model_len': model_config.max_model_len,
+        'max_memory': model_config.max_memory,
+        'local_repo_path': model_config.local_repo_path,
+        'task_type': model_config.task_type,
+        'num_labels': model_config.num_labels,
+        'problem_type': model_config.problem_type,
+        'init_strategy': model_config.init_strategy,
+    }
+    if model_config.torch_dtype:
+        values['torch_dtype'] = getattr(torch, model_config.torch_dtype)
+    if model_config.attn_impl:
+        values['attn_impl'] = model_config.attn_impl
+    for name, value in values.items():
+        if value is not None and value != []:
+            _set_load_kwarg(kwargs, name, value)
+    for name, value in overrides.items():
+        _set_load_kwarg(kwargs, name, value)
+    # trust_remote_code loads make every rank race on the same dynamic-module cache write; the
+    # patch serializes the first writer while the rest wait (legacy register.py applies the same).
+    from swift.dev.patch.transformers_dynamic_module import TransformersDynamicModulePatch
+    from twinkle.patch import apply_context
+
+    with apply_context(None, TransformersDynamicModulePatch()):
+        return get_model_processor(model_config.model, load_model=load_model, **kwargs)
+
+
+def build_dp_mesh(distributed_config: DistributedConfig,
+                  sequence_parallel_size: int = 1) -> Optional['DeviceMesh']:
+    """The transformers-backend data-parallel DeviceMesh (dp x ulysses), for local AND ray modes.
+
+    Local reads Platform.get_world_size(), ray reads nproc_per_node; local + sp=1 with no spec
+    returns None. dp spans ALL ranks, so SP peers share one data rank (identical samples).
+    """
+    from twinkle import DeviceMesh
+
+    spec = distributed_config.parallel_spec
+    is_ray = distributed_config.mode == 'ray'
+
+    if is_ray:
+        world = distributed_config.nproc_per_node
+        if world is None:
+            raise ValueError("DistributedConfig.nproc_per_node is required in mode='ray' (it sizes the 'model' "
+                             'DeviceGroup and its data-parallel mesh). Pass it explicitly -- there is no default.')
+    else:
+        from twinkle.utils import Platform
+        world = Platform.get_world_size()
+
+    if spec:
+        return DeviceMesh.from_spec(spec, world_size=world)
+
+    if not is_ray and sequence_parallel_size <= 1:
+        return None
+
+    if sequence_parallel_size > 1:
+        if world < 2:
+            raise ValueError(f'sequence_parallel_size={sequence_parallel_size} requires WORLD_SIZE>=2; '
+                             'a single process has no ranks to split a sequence across.')
+        if world % sequence_parallel_size != 0:
+            raise ValueError(f'world_size={world} is not divisible by sequence_parallel_size='
+                             f'{sequence_parallel_size}.')
+    return DeviceMesh.from_sizes(world_size=world, dp_size=world, ulysses_size=sequence_parallel_size)
+
+
+def build_model(model_config: ModelConfig,
+                distributed_config: DistributedConfig,
+                train_config: Optional[TrainConfig] = None,
+                tuner_config: Optional[TunerConfig] = None,
+                device_mesh: Optional['DeviceMesh'] = None,
+                quantize_config: Optional[QuantizeConfig] = None,
+                megatron_config: Optional[MegatronConfig] = None,
+                moe_config: Optional['MoEConfig'] = None,
+                remote_group: Optional[str] = None,
+                instance_id: Optional[str] = None,
+                enable_router_replay: bool = False,
+                torch_dtype: Optional[str] = None) -> TrainableModel:
+    """ModelConfig + DistributedConfig -> a twinkle-native Model (no loss/optim yet).
+
+    megatron -> MegatronModel (bridge), else TransformersModel; device_mesh is transformers-only.
+    remote_group/instance_id name the ray group; enable_router_replay is the MoE replay flag.
+    ``torch_dtype`` overrides ModelConfig.torch_dtype on the transformers branch only (RL's
+    trainable actor pins float32 there; the megatron branch ignores it).
+    """
+    # Aux models (teacher/reference/reward) arrive as bare hub ids that never pass _resolve_model;
+    # resolve here so callers may hand in either form -- a local path short-circuits the download.
+    if model_config.model:
+        from swift.dev.utils.hub import safe_snapshot_download
+        model_config.model = safe_snapshot_download(model_config.model, revision=model_config.model_revision)
+    if is_megatron_backend(distributed_config):
+        return _build_megatron_model(
+            model_config,
+            distributed_config,
+            train_config,
+            megatron_config=megatron_config,
+            moe_config=moe_config,
+            remote_group=remote_group,
+            instance_id=instance_id,
+            enable_router_replay=enable_router_replay)
+    if torch_dtype is not None:
+        model_config = copy.copy(model_config)
+        model_config.torch_dtype = torch_dtype
+    return _build_transformers_model(
+        model_config,
+        distributed_config,
+        train_config,
+        tuner_config,
+        device_mesh,
+        quantize_config=quantize_config,
+        remote_group=remote_group,
+        instance_id=instance_id,
+        enable_router_replay=enable_router_replay)
+
+
+def apply_full_param_freeze(model: TrainableModel, train_config: Optional[TrainConfig]) -> None:
+    """Consume TrainConfig's freeze/trainable knobs on a full-parameter model.
+
+    Full-param path only (adapters select via target_modules); must run BEFORE configure_optimizer
+    (param groups build from requires_grad). No-op when no knob is set.
+    """
+    if train_config is None:
+        return
+    freeze_names = train_config.freeze_parameters
+    trainable_names = train_config.trainable_parameters
+    freeze_regex = train_config.freeze_parameters_regex
+    trainable_regex = train_config.trainable_parameters_regex
+    freeze_ratio = train_config.freeze_parameters_ratio
+    if not (freeze_ratio or freeze_names or freeze_regex or trainable_names or trainable_regex):
+        return
+    model.freeze_parameters(
+        freeze_ratio=freeze_ratio,
+        freeze_names=freeze_names,
+        freeze_regex=freeze_regex,
+        trainable_names=trainable_names,
+        trainable_regex=trainable_regex)
+
+
+def build_ref_model(*, name: str, model_id: Optional[str], model_config: ModelConfig,
+                    template, distributed_config: DistributedConfig, device_mesh: Any = None,
+                    parallel_spec: Optional[str] = None, adapters: Sequence[str] = (),
+                    policy_model: Any = None, disable_adapter: bool = False,
+                    model_type: Optional[str] = None, model_revision: Optional[str] = None,
+                    instance_id: Optional[str] = None, deepspeed: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[Any]:
+    """One frozen auxiliary (reference / teacher), as the BARE twinkle model (cookbook shape).
+
+    ``disable_adapter`` returns the policy model itself with the caller-side contract "forward it
+    with ``disable_lora=True``" (the LoRA KL anchor -- same weights, adapters off); ``model_id``
+    empty returns ``None`` (the channel is off). Otherwise: build the frozen model in its own
+    remote group ``name`` sized by the GIVEN ``device_mesh`` (the caller derives it from its plan
+    or spec -- a None mesh is a single-rank build) and install the single frozen adapter. The
+    model IS the reference -- twinkle cookbooks forward it directly (``ref_model.forward_only``);
+    ``remote_group=name`` already encodes its placement. ``model_type`` / ``model_revision`` let an
+    architecturally distinct teacher override the policy's metadata; ``instance_id`` disambiguates
+    K same-group actors (MOPD's packed teachers); ``deepspeed`` is the teacher-only engine config.
+    """
+    if disable_adapter:
+        if policy_model is None:
+            raise ValueError(f'{name}: disable_adapter=True needs the policy model (the shared-weights view).')
+        return policy_model
+    if not model_id:
+        return None
+    from swift.dev.processor import InputProcessor
+
+    config = copy.copy(model_config)
+    config.model = model_id
+    if model_type is not None:
+        config.model_type = model_type
+    if model_revision is not None:
+        config.model_revision = model_revision
+    dist = frozen_auxiliary_distributed_config(
+        distributed_config, device_mesh.world_size if device_mesh else 1, parallel_spec=parallel_spec,
+        deepspeed=deepspeed)
+    frozen = build_model(config, dist, device_mesh=device_mesh, remote_group=name, instance_id=instance_id)
+    if len(adapters) > 1:
+        raise ValueError(f'{name} currently supports exactly one frozen adapter per auxiliary model.')
+    if adapters:
+        frozen.add_adapter_to_model(f'{name}_adapter', adapters[0], is_trainable=False)
+        frozen.set_processor(InputProcessor, adapter_name=f'{name}_adapter')
+        frozen.set_template(template, adapter_name=f'{name}_adapter')
+    else:
+        frozen.set_processor(InputProcessor)
+        frozen.set_template(template)
+    return frozen
+
+
+def _mixed_precision_for(torch_dtype: Optional[str]) -> str:
+    """torch_dtype -> twinkle's mixed_precision mode. Shared by both backends so they cannot drift.
+
+    float32 -> 'no' is a DELIBERATE divergence: legacy sets fp16=True for a float32 run, so "full
+    precision" there still autocasts to fp16; dev takes float32 at face value instead.
+    """
+    if torch_dtype == 'float32':
+        return 'no'
+    if torch_dtype == 'float16':
+        return 'fp16'
+    return 'bf16'
+
+
+def is_megatron_backend(distributed_config: DistributedConfig) -> bool:
+    backend = distributed_config.backend
+    if backend in (None, 'hf', 'unsloth'):
+        # 'unsloth' rides the transformers family: it swaps the construction class, not the
+        # strategy/parallel machinery, so every megatron-only guard keeps rejecting it.
+        return False
+    if backend == 'megatron':
+        return True
+    raise ValueError(f"DistributedConfig.backend must be one of {{'megatron', 'hf', 'unsloth'}}, got {backend!r}.")
+
+
+def frozen_auxiliary_distributed_config(distributed_config: DistributedConfig,
+                                        world_size: int,
+                                        *,
+                                        parallel_spec: Optional[str] = None,
+                                        deepspeed: Optional[str] = None) -> DistributedConfig:
+    """The DistributedConfig a FROZEN auxiliary model (reference / teacher / reward) is built with.
+
+    Inherits only the run's backend identity and forces mode='ray' (RL never runs local); NOT the
+    trainer's parallel layout/deepspeed -- a forward-only auxiliary is sized by world_size alone.
+    """
+    from swift.dev.config import DistributedConfig as _DistributedConfig
+    return _DistributedConfig(
+        mode='ray',
+        backend=distributed_config.backend,
+        bridge_backend=distributed_config.bridge_backend,
+        nproc_per_node=world_size,
+        parallel_spec=parallel_spec,
+        deepspeed=deepspeed)
+
